LAYER 8, THE MICROCIRCUIT LAYER: THE TYPES

The Microcircuits of the Human Nervous and Endocrine System

A Complete, Comprehensive, and Thorough Manuscript

Companion volume to the Layer 6 catalogues (302 neuron types; 85 non-neuronal cell types) and the Layer 9 manuscript (Nature's Cognitive Architecture) in the Certified_Neuroscientist corpus of D. R. Dison, Founder, Artificial Intelligence University (AIU).

Date of compilation: August 9, 2026.


INTRODUCTION: THE LAYER OF THE DIAGRAM

A microcircuit is not a cell, and it is not a brain region.

It is a wiring diagram plus a computation: a small, canonical arrangement of connected cells that performs one elementary operation, installed - with local casting changes - at many addresses throughout the nervous and endocrine system.

That special status demanded a chapter template of its own.

The Layer 6 volumes asked, of each cell, what it is and how it behaves.

The Layer 9 manuscript asked, of each region, what it receives and to whom it sends.

This volume asks, of each motif, four systems questions that only a middle layer can be asked.

• Downward to Layer 6: which cell types play the motif's roles, and how does each cell's algorithmic personality - fast-spiking, adapting, bursting, plateau-holding, slow-integrating - colour the computation?

• Downward to Layer 7: which synapses, gap junctions, and paracrine contacts form the motif's fabric, with what transmitters, weights, and learning rules?

• Upward to Layer 9: at which named regions and glands is the motif installed, and how does its presence flavour each region that hosts it?

• Outward to engineering: how would the motif be realised as a publish-subscribe module - because this volume directly informs the konnectome project, whose constitution demands whole-word module names and clean SUBSCRIBE and PUBLISH interfaces for every construct.

Each of the seventy-one chapters therefore runs through twenty-two fixed aspects, from WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES through THE WIRING DIAGRAM, THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES, THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC, the Layer 9 installation map, the input-output transformation, and a KONNECTOME NOTE, to WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE.

Where an aspect genuinely cannot apply, the chapter says so plainly and says why.

Two tags divide the roster, exactly as in the Layer 6 volumes.

• (COG) marks a motif that participates in COGNITION - perception as interpreted, attention, memory, decision, or learning - and every (COG) chapter closes with ENGLISH READABLE CODE and a runnable Python CODE SAMPLE of its signature computation.

• (NON-COG) marks a motif serving a substrate or other role - relay, motor execution, autonomic and endocrine regulation, early sensory filtering, housekeeping - and its two code sections collapse to a single stated sentence.

The plan of the volume follows the outline that preceded it.

• Part One: the elementary wiring primitives.

• Part Two: the inhibitory motifs.

• Part Three: the competitive and normalising motifs.

• Part Four: the temporal and oscillatory motifs.

• Part Five: the memory and attractor motifs.

• Part Six: the great regional composites, at the soft boundary with Layer 9.

• Part Seven: the reflex and autonomic arcs.

• Part Eight: the sensory front-end motifs.

• Part Nine: the neuroendocrine microcircuits.

• Part Ten: the neuro-glial and neurovascular motifs.

• The Cognitive Scoreboard: what the tags teach.

One sentence from the framework governs everything that follows: the motif is generic.

The same diagram that relaxes your antagonist muscle flips you between sleep and waking and picks the winning thought - one wiring pattern, many destinies, distinguished only by the address at which it is installed and the interfaces to which it is wired.


PART ONE. THE ELEMENTARY WIRING PRIMITIVES

Before there is a rhythm, a memory, or a decision, there is a shape - the bare pattern in which one cell reaches another.

These six motifs are the alphabet of that shape, the two-cell and three-cell words from which every larger circuit sentence in this manuscript is spelled.

They are not places and they are not organs; they are diagrams, instantiated in numbers that can only be called astronomical, in the cortex, the spinal cord, the retina, and even the pancreatic islet.

Connectome analysis calls patterns like these network motifs, meaning local wiring arrangements that occur far more often than chance in a real nervous system - a discovery that began with the transcription network of the bacterium Escherichia coli and was quickly found in every nervous system examined.

The lesson of Part One is that computation begins not with a special cell but with a particular way of joining ordinary ones: fan many wires into one and you have summation, fan one wire into many and you have broadcast, close a loop and you have memory.

Master these six and every motif that follows is a variation, a decoration, or a composition of them.


CHAPTER 1. CONVERGENCE (Fan-In Integration Motif) (The Evidence-Pooling Junction) (COG)

Somewhere in your spinal cord, at this instant, a single motor neuron is holding a silent tally of perhaps ten thousand opinions, and only when enough of them agree does your muscle twitch.

That tally is convergence, the oldest and simplest computation the nervous system performs, and it is the physical act of adding evidence together until it crosses a line.

Every decision you have ever made bottomed out, at some cell, in this arithmetic.

Fan-In names the geometry: many wires narrowing onto one receiver, the mouth of a funnel.

Integration names the operation: the receiver sums what arrives across space and time rather than merely passing it on.

Junction names the meeting point, the one cell where the many become a single yes or no.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

Convergence is the wiring pattern in which many presynaptic cells (cells sending a signal) project onto one postsynaptic cell (the cell receiving it), which then combines those inputs into a single output.

The computation is summation to threshold: the receiving cell adds its inputs, and if the running total crosses a firing threshold it produces a spike, the brief electrical pulse that is the nervous system's unit of message.

Depending on the timing and weighting of its inputs the same junction can average many weak signals, detect the coincidence of a few strong ones, or count evidence toward a decision - three faces of one act of addition.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The graph has N source nodes and one sink node, with N directed edges, one from each source to the sink, and no edges among the sources and no return edge from the sink.

Each edge carries a sign and a weight: an excitatory edge (positive, glutamate-releasing) pushes the sink toward threshold, while an inhibitory edge (negative, gamma-aminobutyric-acid-releasing, abbreviated gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-releasing) pushes it away.

The sink integrates the weighted sum of its edges continuously; an engineer would redraw this as a single summing node with N incoming weighted arrows and one thresholded output arrow.

The defining feature is the fan-in ratio N, which in a spinal motor neuron reaches roughly ten thousand synapses and in a cerebellar Purkinje cell approaches two hundred thousand.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The canonical receiver is the alpha motor neuron of the ventral spinal cord, a large integrate-and-fire cell whose smooth summation of spindle, corticospinal, and interneuronal input makes it the final common path of all movement.

Its slow-integrating personality - a long membrane time constant that lets inputs pile up over milliseconds - is precisely what makes it a good adder rather than a coincidence detector.

In the cortex the receiver is the layer 5 extratelencephalic pyramidal cell of the neuron catalogue, whose thick apical dendrite behaves as a second, semi-independent integration site, so that convergence there is compartmental rather than simply pooled.

The prefrontal decision cell, a layer 2/3 or layer 5 pyramidal neuron, plays the receiver when the inputs being summed are streams of sensory evidence, and its adapting firing colours the tally with a built-in leak, so that stale evidence decays.

The senders are heterogeneous by design: thalamic relay cells, other pyramidal cells, and sensory afferents supply the excitatory edges, while parvalbumin basket cells of the neuron catalogue supply fast, subtractive inhibitory edges that raise the effective threshold.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

The excitatory edges are glutamate synapses on dendritic spines and shafts, acting through fast alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors (decay near 2 milliseconds) and slow N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors (decay near 100 milliseconds), the latter giving the junction a short memory that supports temporal summation.

Inhibitory edges are GABA synapses placed strategically near the soma and axon initial segment, where they exert maximal veto over the summed total, acting through fast GABA-A receptors (decay 5 to 10 milliseconds).

Synaptic weights are set by the number of vesicle release sites and postsynaptic receptor count, and they are plastic under spike-timing-dependent rules, so the funnel can learn to weight some sources more than others.

Electrical (gap-junction) edges are rare here; convergence is overwhelmingly a chemical-synapse motif.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One instance is one receiving cell plus its afferent tree, a structure a few hundred micrometres across (a micrometre being a thousandth of a millimetre) for a cortical pyramid and up to a millimetre for a motor neuron's dendritic field.

The fan-in ranges from a handful of inputs (a brainstem relay) to roughly ten thousand (a motor neuron) to about a hundred and fifty thousand parallel-fibre inputs on a single cerebellar Purkinje cell, the most extreme convergence in the body.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

Every neuron that receives more than one input is an instance, so the count is essentially the neuron count of the nervous system, on the order of 86 billion in the brain alone.

Convergence is therefore not localised; it is the default condition of neural tissue, and its density (inputs per cell) rather than its presence is what varies across regions.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• The ventral horn of the spinal cord, where spindle and descending inputs converge on motor neurons to set muscle force.

• The primary motor cortex, where premotor and thalamic streams converge on layer 5 output cells.

• The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, where sensory-evidence streams converge on decision cells during deliberation.

• The cerebellar cortex, where parallel fibres converge in vast numbers on Purkinje cells for motor calibration.

• The retinal ganglion cell layer, where bipolar and amacrine inputs converge to form each ganglion cell's receptive field.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Delete convergence from the ventral horn and the muscle would receive a babble of unreconciled commands rather than a single graded force; the spinal cord would lose its power to add.

Delete it from prefrontal cortex and evidence could arrive but never accumulate, so a choice could be prompted but never justified - the region would perceive without ever deciding.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

In plain words the junction computes a weighted sum passed through a threshold: output rises steeply once the summed input exceeds a critical value near minus 50 millivolts at the axon hillock, and stays near zero below it.

The established mathematical form is threshold-linear (also called rectified-linear) for rate coding, and integrate-and-fire for spike coding, with the membrane acting as a leaky integrator whose leak sets how long past inputs still count.

With a membrane time constant of 10 to 20 milliseconds, inputs arriving within about 20 milliseconds sum effectively, while inputs spaced further apart are treated as independent - the numerical basis of coincidence detection versus averaging.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

Fast excitatory inputs summate over a window set by the membrane time constant, so the junction is a low-pass filter with a corner near 10 to 50 hertz.

Coincident inputs (within a couple of milliseconds) are supralinearly effective when NMDA receptors and dendritic spikes engage, giving the same anatomy a fast coincidence-detecting mode on top of its slow averaging mode.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

At low input the junction is an averager, smoothing noise; at high synchrony it is a coincidence detector, firing only when inputs align; between these it is an evidence integrator, ramping its rate with accumulated input.

Which regime is active depends on the balance of AMPA to NMDA conductance and on the level of background inhibition, so neuromodulators can shift a single junction from one mode to another without any rewiring.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

Each edge's weight is adjustable by long-term potentiation and depression under spike-timing rules operating within tens of milliseconds, so the funnel learns which sources predict its own firing.

Homeostatic scaling multiplies all weights up or down over hours to hold the cell's average rate near a target, preventing convergence from silencing or saturating itself as synapses are added and removed.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

Linear convergence sums inputs on a compact electrotonic structure (a small interneuron); compartmental convergence sums within semi-independent dendritic branches first, then across them (a pyramidal cell); and coincidence-tuned convergence weights near-simultaneous inputs supralinearly.

A distinct subtype is multimodal convergence, where inputs of different sensory modalities meet on one cell, the anatomical basis of cross-modal binding in association cortex and the superior colliculus.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

Convergence is built by exuberant early innervation followed by activity-dependent pruning: many axons initially contact a target, and correlated firing stabilises some inputs while uncorrelated ones are removed, the rule captured by the phrase cells that fire together wire together.

At the neuromuscular junction this pruning goes to completion (one axon per fibre in the adult), while in the central nervous system it stops at high fan-in, preserving the many-to-one funnel.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

Summation is the most ancient neural computation, present in the nerve nets of jellyfish and the earliest bilaterians, because any cell with more than one input performs it by default.

The elaboration seen in vertebrates - graded weights, dendritic compartments, threshold tuning - is a refinement of a primitive that predates the brain itself.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Astrocytes (star-shaped glial cells) enwrap the converging synapses, clear released glutamate through the transporters EAAT1 and EAAT2, and thereby set how far each input's signal spreads and how quickly the summation window closes.

The metabolic cost of a high-fan-in cell is dominated by its synapses rather than its spikes, so the local blood supply and astrocytic glucose delivery scale with the number of converging inputs.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

In amyotrophic lateral sclerosis the motor neuron, the body's exemplary convergence cell, degenerates, and the funnel of movement is lost input by input.

Excessive effective convergence, when inhibitory edges fail, produces the runaway summation that underlies epileptic recruitment; too little, as in the deafferented cell, produces a receiver that can no longer reach threshold at all.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ N excitatory conductances, each 0.1 to 2 nanosiemens, N from about 10 to about 150,000; inhibitory conductances 0 to 30 nanosiemens near the soma.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ A single spike train whose rate encodes the thresholded weighted sum, 0 to about 200 hertz.

• STATE.

◦ Membrane voltage, per-synapse weights, adaptation current, dendritic compartment voltages.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Threshold near minus 50 millivolts; resting near minus 70 millivolts; fan-in N; per-edge weights.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Membrane 10 to 20 milliseconds; AMPA 2 milliseconds; NMDA 100 milliseconds; adaptation 100 to 300 milliseconds.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Motor neuron loss in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis; deafferentation after peripheral injury; pathological over-summation in seizure recruitment.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

Propose a module named evidence_summation_integrator that subscribes to a variable-length list of weighted signed input messages and publishes a single scalar activation plus a fired boolean when the running weighted sum crosses a published threshold.

Its closest artificial-intelligence analogue is the classic artificial neuron - a weighted sum followed by a nonlinearity - but the biological motif differs in three ways an engineer should preserve: its inputs decay with distinct fast and slow time constants rather than being instantaneous, its dendritic compartments sum locally before summing globally, and its threshold and weights drift under homeostatic and timing-dependent rules rather than being fixed at inference time.

A faithful module therefore carries per-input decay state and a slow self-normalising gain, not merely a static weight vector.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to decide whether a convergence junction fires by summing weighted evidence until it crosses a threshold.

Create a number variable called total with initial value 0.

Create a number variable called threshold with initial value 1.

Create a list variable called inputs holding the signed evidence values arriving this instant.

Create a list variable called weights holding one weight for each input.

For each position in the inputs list, perform the following actions.

    Calculate the product of the input at this position and the weight at this position.

    Add the result to total.

End the loop.

If total is greater than or equal to threshold is true, then perform the following actions.

    Set the output to the value fired.

Otherwise, perform the following actions.

    Set the output to the value silent.

End the conditional block.

Display the output to the console.

The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because a leaky integrator that ramps to threshold is the whole story, and a short loop over time steps shows the accumulation and the decision with no ceremony.

# Convergence as evidence accumulation to threshold: a leaky integrate-and-fire
# junction pooling many noisy inputs (Gerstner & Kistler, Spiking Neuron Models, 2002).
import random

TAU = 15.0        # membrane time constant, milliseconds (leak)
DT = 1.0          # time step, milliseconds
THRESHOLD = 1.0   # firing threshold (arbitrary units)
WEIGHTS = [0.02] * 60   # 60 converging excitatory inputs, each small

v = 0.0
for t in range(200):                      # 200 milliseconds
    drive = sum(w for w in WEIGHTS if random.random() < 0.5)  # ~half active
    v += DT * (-v / TAU + drive)          # leaky summation of the fan-in
    if v >= THRESHOLD:
        print(f"t={t} ms  fired  (pooled evidence crossed threshold)")
        v = 0.0                           # reset after the spike
# With too few inputs the leak wins and v never reaches threshold:
# convergence turns many small, uncertain votes into one timed decision.

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

A single cell wearing a crown of many incoming wires and no outgoing loop, whose voltage is the live running total of everything projecting to it, firing the instant that total crosses a line - the funnel that turns a crowd of signals into one answer.


CHAPTER 2. DIVERGENCE (Fan-Out Broadcast Motif) (The One-to-Many Megaphone) (COG)

A single dopamine neuron in your midbrain, no bigger than a grain of sand at its cell body, sends a branching axon that touches on the order of a million target cells across the striatum.

When it fires, a million synapses hear the same word at nearly the same moment.

That is divergence, the mirror image of convergence, and it is how a nervous system turns one cell's private event into a public announcement.

Fan-Out names the geometry: one wire splitting into many, the mouth of the funnel reversed.

Broadcast names the operation: the same message copied to every branch rather than combined.

Megaphone names the amplifying intent - one voice made loud enough for a whole population to hear at once.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

Divergence is the wiring pattern in which one presynaptic cell projects to many postsynaptic cells, delivering a copy of its output to each.

The computation is broadcast with gain: a single spike train is distributed, and because each branch drives its own target, one input event can trigger many output events, so the motif amplifies as it copies.

Where convergence collapses many signals into one decision, divergence expands one decision into many simultaneous consequences - it is the physical basis of a signal becoming a command that a whole region obeys.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The graph has one source node and M sink nodes, with M directed edges, one from the source to each sink, and no edges among the sinks.

Each edge carries a sign and a weight; in the classic amplifying case all edges are excitatory (glutamate or, in the periphery, acetylcholine), but neuromodulatory divergence uses paracrine-like volume release (dopamine, noradrenaline, serotonin) in which one axon sprays a transmitter cloud over many targets rather than making tidy one-to-one contacts.

The defining feature is the fan-out ratio M and the divergence gain, the average number of target spikes produced per source spike, which exceeds one whenever each contact is strong enough to help drive its target.

An engineer would redraw this as a single source with M outgoing weighted arrows and, crucially, a note on whether the copies are synchronous (branches of one axon, sub-millisecond spread) or staggered by conduction delay.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The exemplary broadcaster is the midbrain dopamine neuron of the substantia nigra and ventral tegmental area, a slow, pacemaking, sometimes bursting cell whose single axon ramifies into a vast terminal field, so its tonic firing bathes the striatum in a steady modulatory signal and its bursts broadcast a global teaching pulse.

The locus coeruleus noradrenaline neuron is a second archetype: a few thousand such cells project throughout the entire forebrain, so one small nucleus can raise the arousal of the whole brain at once - divergence at its most extreme fan-out.

In fast signalling the thalamic relay cell diverges onto many cortical targets, and the cerebellar granule cell of the other-cells catalogue sends its axon up and then along as a parallel fibre contacting hundreds of Purkinje cells in a row, its tiny fast spikes copied down the beam.

The preganglionic autonomic neuron diverges onto many ganglion cells, and its personality - reliable, high-safety-factor firing - ensures every copy lands, making it the amplifying distribution board of the fight-or-flight response.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

Fast divergence uses glutamate or acetylcholine at conventional axon-terminal synapses, each an independent release site, so the branches are electrically separate copies of one spike.

Neuromodulatory divergence uses varicosities (bead-like swellings along the axon) that release dopamine, noradrenaline, or serotonin into the extracellular space, reaching many receptors by diffusion - a low-address, high-reach broadcast that trades precision for coverage.

Weights on the branches need not be equal; a broadcasting axon can hold strong contacts on some targets and weak ones on others, and these are individually plastic, so the megaphone can learn to whisper to some listeners and shout at others.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One instance is one source cell plus its full axonal arbor, which for a dopamine neuron can extend over cubic millimetres of striatum and support on the order of a hundred thousand to a million release sites.

Fast local divergence is smaller - a thalamic or granule cell contacting hundreds to a few thousand targets within a millimetre or so.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

Like convergence, divergence is nearly universal: any neuron whose axon branches is an instance, so the count approaches the neuron count itself.

The extreme broadcasters are few and precious - roughly 400,000 to 600,000 midbrain dopamine neurons and only about 50,000 locus coeruleus neurons in the human brain - which is why their loss is so consequential.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• The striatum, where midbrain dopamine axons broadcast reward and movement-gating signals to millions of medium spiny neurons.

• The entire forebrain, reached by the locus coeruleus noradrenergic broadcast that sets arousal and gain.

• The cerebellar cortex, where each granule cell's parallel fibre copies its signal along a beam of Purkinje cells.

• The autonomic ganglia, where one preganglionic axon diverges onto many ganglion cells for amplified visceral output.

• The thalamocortical projection, where relay cells fan out to distribute sensory signals across cortical columns.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Delete divergence from the dopamine system and the striatum would lose its global teaching and enabling signal; each spike would inform one cell instead of a million, and the coordinated learning of the basal ganglia would collapse into local noise - clinically, this is Parkinson's disease.

Delete it from the locus coeruleus and the forebrain would lose its single dial for arousal and alertness, so waking, attention, and the emergency amplification of stress would have no common broadcast to ride on.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

In plain words the motif copies one input to many outputs with a gain: one input spike yields M weighted output events, and the total downstream effect is the source rate multiplied by the effective fan-out.

The mathematical form is a multiplication (broadcast gain) in the synchronous case and a spatial convolution with a delay kernel when conduction delays stagger the copies - the same anatomy that broadcasts a value can, with graded delays, lay a signal out across space and time.

For neuromodulatory divergence the transform is better described as a slow scalar field: one source sets a background concentration that biases the gain of every target, the multiplicative context signal formalised in Part Three's gain-modulation motif.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

Synchronous divergence delivers its copies within a fraction of a millisecond (shared axon, common trunk), giving downstream populations a precise shared time-zero.

Neuromodulatory divergence is slow and sustained, with transmitter clouds rising and falling over hundreds of milliseconds to seconds, so its broadcast is a mood rather than a message.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

In tonic mode a broadcaster sets a steady background level (baseline dopamine tone, baseline arousal); in phasic or burst mode it delivers a transient global pulse (a reward-prediction-error burst, an alerting volley).

The switch between tonic and phasic firing, gated by the source cell's own inputs, lets one divergent axon serve both as a slow context dial and a fast global alarm.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

The individual branch weights are plastic, so a broadcaster can be sculpted to favour particular targets, and the source's tonic level itself adapts to context over minutes.

Crucially, divergent neuromodulatory signals are themselves the teaching signal for plasticity elsewhere: dopamine's broadcast gates the strengthening of corticostriatal synapses, so this motif is both a learner and the schoolmaster of other motifs.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

Addressed divergence makes precise one-to-one contacts on many targets (fast relay and parallel-fibre types), preserving timing; volume divergence sprays transmitter to whoever has the receptor (the aminergic and dopaminergic broadcasters), maximising reach.

A third subtype is amplifying divergence at the neuromuscular and ganglionic periphery, where high release safety guarantees that every copy fires its target, converting one central command into many peripheral actions.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

A divergent arbor is grown by axonal branching guided by chemotropic cues and then refined by activity, with target-derived neurotrophic factors deciding how many branches survive.

Broadcasting aminergic systems establish their enormous arbors early and maintain them lifelong, which is part of why their slow attrition (as in Parkinson's) produces such widespread deficits.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

Volume transmission - one cell chemically addressing many - is evolutionarily older than the point-to-point synapse, echoing the paracrine and hormonal signalling of pre-neural tissue, so the neuromodulatory broadcaster is in a sense the endocrine principle wired into the brain.

Fast addressed divergence is the newer refinement, buying timing precision on top of the ancient reach.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Astrocytes shape both forms of divergence: they clear fast transmitter to keep copies distinct, and they set the diffusion distance of neuromodulator clouds by uptake and by the geometry of the extracellular space.

The huge arbors of broadcasting neurons carry a correspondingly huge metabolic and transport burden, one reason these long, thin, poorly myelinated axons are especially vulnerable to degeneration.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Parkinson's disease is the death of the substantia nigra's dopamine broadcasters, and its symptoms are exactly what the loss of a global enabling signal predicts - slowed movement, rigidity, and impoverished learning.

Locus coeruleus degeneration figures in the arousal and attention failures of Alzheimer's disease, and dysregulated dopaminergic and noradrenergic broadcast is implicated in addiction, attention-deficit disorder, and the psychosis of schizophrenia.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ The source cell's own afferents setting its firing mode; typically a few strong drivers plus modulatory context.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ M copies of one spike train, M from hundreds to about a million; effective divergence gain greater than 1.

• STATE.

◦ Source firing mode (tonic versus phasic), per-branch weights, ambient transmitter concentration for volume types.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Fan-out M; per-branch weight; conduction delays 0.1 to several milliseconds; transmitter diffusion radius for volume release.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Fast synaptic copy under 1 millisecond; neuromodulator rise and clearance 100 milliseconds to seconds.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Dopaminergic broadcaster loss in Parkinson's disease; noradrenergic loss in Alzheimer's disease; broadcast dysregulation in addiction and schizophrenia.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

Propose a module named broadcast_fanout_publisher that subscribes to a single source signal and publishes it to a named list of subscribers, each with its own gain, applying either a synchronous copy or a slow decaying scalar field for the neuromodulatory case.

Its closest artificial-intelligence analogue is the publish-subscribe message bus itself, and secondarily the broadcast of a global scalar such as a learning-rate or a reward signal in reinforcement learning.

The biological motif differs in that its broadcast can carry graded per-subscriber gain, can operate in a fast addressed mode or a slow diffuse mode, and doubles as the teaching signal that rewrites other modules' weights - so a faithful implementation exposes both a fast event channel and a slow context channel from the same publisher.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to broadcast one source signal to many targets, applying a per-target gain so the copy also amplifies.

Create a number variable called source spike with the value 1 when the source fires and 0 otherwise.

Create a number variable called divergence gain with initial value 1.5.

Create a list variable called targets holding one entry for each receiving cell.

Create a list variable called gains holding one gain value for each target.

Create a list variable called outputs that starts empty.

For each position in the targets list, perform the following actions.

    Calculate the product of source spike, the gain at this position, and divergence gain.

    Append the result to the outputs list.

End the loop.

Display the outputs list to the console.

The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because broadcast-with-gain is best shown by counting how one input spike multiplies into many output events across a population, which a single list comprehension makes plain.

# Divergence as broadcast copying with gain: one source spike distributed to
# many targets, each contact strong enough that copies exceed the original
# (Matsuda et al., J. Neurosci. 2009, on single-axon dopaminergic arbors).
import random

FANOUT = 20                 # one source contacts 20 targets
P_RELEASE = 0.9             # high safety factor per contact
GAINS = [random.uniform(0.5, 1.5) for _ in range(FANOUT)]

def broadcast(source_spike):
    # each target fires if the copy lands (release) and clears its own threshold
    copies = [source_spike * g * (1 if random.random() < P_RELEASE else 0)
              for g in GAINS]
    fired = sum(1 for c in copies if c >= 0.5)
    return copies, fired

_, downstream_spikes = broadcast(source_spike=1)
print(f"one input spike -> {downstream_spikes} downstream spikes "
      f"(divergence gain = {downstream_spikes/1:.1f})")
# The single event has become a population event: this is amplification by copying.

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

A single cell with one crowded axonal tree and no incoming loop, whose one spike lands as many, so that a private firing becomes a public command - the megaphone that lets one grain-sized neuron be heard by a million.


CHAPTER 3. THE FEEDFORWARD CHAIN (Serial Relay Motif) (The Signal Bucket-Brigade) (NON-COG)

Deep in a peripheral nerve, a touch signal from your fingertip is being handed cell to cell toward your brain like a bucket of water passed down a line of firefighters - each hand receives, each hand passes, none of them changes the water.

That is the feedforward chain, the purest and least glamorous motif in this manuscript: transmission with no loop, no branch that matters, and no computation beyond faithful carry.

It is tagged non-cognitive precisely because its virtue is to do nothing to the message but move it.

Serial names the arrangement: one after another, in a line.

Relay names the act: receive and re-transmit, the job of a relay station.

Bucket-Brigade names the spirit - many hands, one bucket, unchanged from end to end.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

The feedforward chain is the wiring pattern A drives B drives C drives onward, a sequence of cells each exciting the next, with no return connections and no branching loops.

Its computation, strictly speaking, is transmission: it moves a signal from one place to another with delay but without transformation, the substrate role in its clearest form.

Any real chain adds small delay, some filtering, and a refresh of signal strength at each stage, but its defining purpose is faithful carry, not calculation - which is why it anchors the non-cognitive end of the motif spectrum.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The graph is a directed path: node A to node B to node C to node D, with one excitatory edge between each consecutive pair and no other edges, no reciprocal edges, and no edges skipping ahead.

Every edge is positive (excitatory, glutamate or acetylcholine), and the topology is strictly acyclic and linear; an engineer would redraw it as a single line of boxes joined by right-pointing arrows.

The one important quantitative property is the per-stage delay and the safety factor - whether each stage reliably fires the next (a faithful relay) or only sometimes (a probabilistic gate).

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The archetype is the chain of relay neurons in an ascending sensory pathway, for example the dorsal-column pathway carrying touch: first-order afferent to second-order neuron in the medulla to third-order thalamic relay cell to cortex.

Each relay's personality is deliberately faithful - high release probability, fast action potentials, minimal adaptation - so that the message survives the trip; a bursting or strongly adapting cell would distort the bucket and is selected against in these lines.

The thalamic relay cell of the neuron catalogue, in its tonic mode, is the quintessential faithful relay, passing retinal or lemniscal input to cortex with high fidelity (in its burst mode it stops relaying and signals novelty, but that is a different motif).

Peripheral autonomic and enteric relay chains use acetylcholine-releasing neurons with the same premium on reliability.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

The edges are strong, secure glutamatergic or cholinergic synapses, often large and multi-release-site to guarantee suprathreshold drive - the calyx of Held in the auditory brainstem is the extreme example, a giant terminal built for one-to-one, high-fidelity, low-jitter relay.

Fast alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors dominate to keep timing crisp, with relatively little N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) or metabotropic contribution that would blur the signal.

Weights are held high and stable rather than finely plastic, because a relay that learned would cease to be a faithful relay; what plasticity exists mostly maintains reliability (homeostatic) rather than reshapes content.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One instance is a linear cascade of two to a handful of neurons spanning the distance the signal must travel, from millimetres (a local brainstem relay) to nearly a metre (a peripheral-to-cord sensory chain).

The number of stages is small by design - each stage adds delay and a chance of failure, so evolution keeps ascending and descending relays as short as the anatomy allows.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

Feedforward chains are everywhere a signal must be carried faithfully across distance: every sensory afferent pathway, every motor command line, and every peripheral nerve is built of them.

They are countless but individually short, and they dominate the white matter and peripheral nerves rather than the computational grey matter.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• The dorsal-column-medial-lemniscus pathway, relaying fine touch and proprioception from body to cortex.

• The auditory brainstem, where the calyx of Held relays timing information with extreme fidelity.

• The thalamocortical relay, where tonic-mode relay cells pass sensory streams to their cortical areas.

• The peripheral nerves and dorsal-root ganglia, carrying afferent signals from receptor to spinal cord.

• The corticospinal tract and lower motor pathways, relaying movement commands toward the muscle.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Delete the relay chain and a region would be informationally marooned: the cortex could compute brilliantly but would receive nothing from the senses and command nothing to the muscles, because the wires that carry the news would be cut.

A region keeps its faithful relays the way a city keeps its roads - unglamorous, but every clever thing done downtown depends on them.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

In plain words the chain reproduces its input at its output after a fixed delay: output rate approximately equals input rate, shifted in time by the summed per-stage delays.

The mathematical form is the identity with delay (a pure delay line) in the ideal case, and a mild low-pass filter in practice, since each synapse and membrane smooths the fastest fluctuations.

Real numbers: each central relay adds roughly 0.5 to a few milliseconds, and a three-neuron ascending pathway delivers its signal to cortex on the order of 10 to 30 milliseconds after the stimulus.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

The signature is delay without reshaping: a crisp input arrives at the far end slightly later and slightly smoothed, with jitter kept low by strong secure synapses.

In high-fidelity auditory relays the jitter is held to tens of microseconds, because downstream timing computations depend on it.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

The chain has essentially one intended regime - faithful transmission - and its main state variable is whether each stage is currently secure (relaying) or, in the thalamic case, switched into a non-relaying burst mode by hyperpolarisation.

Because it has no loop, it has no attractor states, no oscillation, and no memory; its emptiness of dynamics is exactly its defining feature and the reason for its non-cognitive tag.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

Plasticity is minimised and largely homeostatic, tuned to preserve reliability rather than to learn content, so the chain resists the very changes that make cognitive motifs interesting.

Developmentally, activity refines which relay contacts survive, but the mature chain is a stable pipe.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

Faithful high-safety relays (calyx of Held, tonic thalamic relay) prioritise fidelity; longer polysynaptic chains trade a little fidelity for routing flexibility; and gated relays (thalamic cells switchable to burst mode) can be turned off as a unit, blurring the line toward a controllable gate.

The synfire chain of Part Four is the cognitive cousin of this motif - a feedforward chain of pools that carries a timed packet rather than a rate - showing how the same acyclic geometry becomes computational once it carries synchrony and is made plastic.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

Chains are laid down by axon guidance along stereotyped tracts, then refined by activity to secure reliable stage-to-stage transmission.

Myelination (the fatty insulating wrap made by oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system and Schwann cells in the periphery) is critical here, since a relay's job is speed and fidelity, both of which myelin provides.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

The through-conducting pathway is among the earliest specialisations of nervous systems, present as soon as animals needed to move a signal faster than diffusion across a body larger than a few cells.

It is the motif from which all others are elaborations: close a chain into a loop and you get recurrence, branch it and you get the feedforward loop, and both computational families begin here.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells provide the myelin that gives relays their speed, and their failure (demyelination) directly degrades relay fidelity.

Astrocytes at each synapse maintain the secure, low-jitter transmission by rapid transmitter clearance and ion buffering.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Multiple sclerosis and the peripheral demyelinating neuropathies (such as Guillain-Barre and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease) are diseases of the relay chain: the wire is stripped of insulation, and signals slow, jitter, or fail to arrive.

Conduction block, delayed evoked potentials, and sensory or motor loss are the direct clinical readout of a bucket-brigade that can no longer pass its bucket.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ A single upstream spike train at stage A, secure suprathreshold drive, one strong excitatory input per stage.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ The same spike train at the far end, delayed by the summed per-stage latencies.

• STATE.

◦ Per-stage security (relaying versus failed or burst-mode); myelination status.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Number of stages (2 to about 5); per-stage delay 0.5 to a few milliseconds; conduction velocity 3 to 120 metres per second by fibre calibre and myelin.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Synaptic transmission under 1 millisecond per stage; total pathway latency 10 to 30 milliseconds for a body-to-cortex chain.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Demyelination (multiple sclerosis, Guillain-Barre syndrome, Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease); conduction block; relay failure from axonal injury.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

This section does not apply to this microcircuit type for the reason that this motif serves a substrate or regulatory role rather than a cognitive-computational role, and is tagged (NON-COG).

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

This section does not apply to this microcircuit type for the reason that this motif serves a substrate or regulatory role rather than a cognitive-computational role, and is tagged (NON-COG).

This section does not apply to this microcircuit type for the reason that this motif serves a substrate or regulatory role rather than a cognitive-computational role, and is tagged (NON-COG).

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

A straight line of cells with arrows all pointing one way, no loop anywhere, that delivers its input unchanged but later - the pipe you notice only when it breaks and the news stops arriving.


CHAPTER 4. THE RECURRENT LOOP (Reciprocal Pair) (The Two-Cell Memory Latch) (COG)

Take two cells and let each excite the other, and something new appears that neither had alone: once you nudge the pair into activity, it can keep itself going after the nudge is gone.

That small persistence is the birth of internal state, and internal state is the precondition of memory - the moment a nervous system stops being a pipe and becomes a system that can hold a thought.

The two-cell reciprocal loop is the smallest circuit that can remember, the atom of every attractor and every working-memory assembly later in this manuscript.

Recurrent names the essential move: the signal comes back around instead of only going forward.

Loop names the closed topology - output feeding input.

Latch names the payoff, borrowed from electronics: a circuit that stays in the state you set it to, holding a bit until it is reset.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

The recurrent loop is the wiring pattern in which cell A excites cell B and cell B excites cell A back, the smallest possible feedback loop.

Its computation is the creation of persistent state: reciprocal excitation is positive feedback, and positive feedback can sustain activity that outlasts its trigger, so the pair can latch on and stay on.

This turns a network from a transmission line into a system with memory, because the pair's current state now depends on its own past, not only on its present input.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The graph has two nodes, A and B, and two directed excitatory edges, A to B and B to A, forming a cycle of length two, with no other cells required.

Both edges are positive (glutamatergic), and the loop gain - the product of the two edge strengths and the cells' input-output slopes - is the single number that decides everything: below one the loop is a transient amplifier, at or above one it can self-sustain.

An engineer would redraw this as two boxes joined by arrows pointing both ways, and would immediately ask for the loop gain and for whatever inhibition or adaptation keeps the positive feedback from exploding.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The prototypical players are two excitatory pyramidal cells of the cortex - for example a pair of layer 5 or prefrontal layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons - whose mutual glutamatergic contacts, especially through slow N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors, let their joint activity persist.

The plateau-generating personality matters here: cells that can sustain a long depolarising plateau (through NMDA conductance or intrinsic persistent currents) make robust latches, because each partner keeps firing long enough to re-excite the other.

A second cast appears in the thalamus and its reciprocal partner the cortex, where thalamocortical and corticothalamic cells form a large-scale reciprocal excitatory loop that supports reverberation, though there the loop is braided with inhibition.

In every case a restraining partner - a nearby inhibitory interneuron or the cell's own adaptation current - is implied, because a pure two-cell excitatory latch with no brake is a seizure waiting to happen, the theme of Chapter 6.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

The two edges are glutamate synapses on dendritic spines, and the slow NMDA receptor (decay near 100 milliseconds) is the key component, because its long time constant lets each partner's excitation linger and re-ignite the other - fast alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) alone tends to make the loop oscillate or fizzle rather than latch.

Realistic loops also carry gap junctions between coupled cells in some structures, and always sit near GABAergic terminals whose inhibition sets the loop's stability.

The reciprocal weights are strongly plastic under Hebbian rules (partners that fire together strengthen their mutual synapses), which is exactly how a pair learns to become a stable memory unit.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One idealised instance is two cells, but in tissue the functional latch is a small reciprocally connected group spanning tens to a few hundred micrometres, since two lone cells rarely carry enough loop gain to hold state reliably against noise.

The reciprocally connected pair is nonetheless the countable unit connectome studies measure, and such pairs are found far more often than chance in cortical and invertebrate wiring.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

Reciprocally connected excitatory pairs are statistically over-represented in cortical microcircuitry - paired-recording studies find bidirectional connections between pyramidal cells more common than random wiring predicts, and the same over-representation of reciprocal doublets is reported in the nematode connectome.

They are dense wherever tissue must hold state: prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and higher association areas, and sparser in pure relay structures.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, where reciprocal excitatory pairs and small loops sustain working-memory activity across a delay.

• The hippocampal area CA3, where recurrent collaterals make reciprocal loops the substrate of pattern completion.

• The thalamocortical system, where cortex and thalamus form a large reciprocal excitatory loop underlying reverberation and rhythm.

• The higher association cortices, where reciprocal loops hold context online during ongoing computation.

• The entorhinal and parahippocampal cortices, where persistent-firing cells use reciprocal and intrinsic feedback to bridge time.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Delete the recurrent loop from prefrontal cortex and the region would lose its present tense: information could pass through but nothing could be held, so a cue seen a second ago would be gone, and there could be no keeping anything in mind.

A region with reciprocal loops can carry the past into the present; a region without them lives only in the instantaneous now.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

In plain words the loop is bistable: for the same input it can rest in a low (off) state or a high (on) state, and a transient input can flip it from one to the other, where it then stays.

The established mathematical form is bistability arising from positive feedback with a nonlinear gain, giving a hysteresis loop - the state depends on history, and the threshold to turn on is higher than the threshold to stay on.

Real numbers: with sufficient NMDA-mediated loop gain, a pair can hold firing at a modest persistent rate (often cited near 10 to 50 hertz in prefrontal delay activity) for seconds after a stimulus lasting only a few hundred milliseconds.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

The signature is persistence: a brief input produces an output that outlasts it by hundreds of milliseconds to seconds, far longer than any single synaptic time constant, because the loop keeps re-injecting its own activity.

If the loop gain is tuned high with fast synapses instead of slow ones, the same anatomy rings or oscillates rather than latching - persistence and oscillation are two settings of one dial.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

Below unity loop gain the pair is a transient amplifier that decays after input; at unity it is a perfect integrator; above unity with a saturating nonlinearity it is bistable, holding a discrete on-state.

Add delay and it can become an oscillator; add adaptation and the on-state slowly fades - so this two-cell motif already contains, in miniature, the amplifier, the integrator, the memory latch, and the oscillator.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

The reciprocal synapses potentiate under Hebbian, spike-timing-dependent rules, so co-active pairs deepen their mutual coupling and become more reliable latches - this is how experience carves stable memory assemblies out of initially weak loops.

Runaway potentiation is checked by homeostatic scaling and by the inhibition that shares the tissue, keeping loop gain near the useful edge of bistability rather than in the explosive regime.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

The pure excitatory reciprocal pair is the base case; the excitatory-inhibitory reciprocal pair (one cell excites, the other inhibits back) is instead an oscillator or thermostat and belongs to Part Two; and the electrically coupled reciprocal pair (joined by a gap junction) synchronises rather than latches.

Scaled up, the reciprocal-excitation principle becomes the autoassociative attractor of Part Five, so this chapter is the seed of the memory motifs.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

Reciprocal loops emerge as recurrent collaterals grow and are stabilised by correlated activity, the wiring signature of Hebbian assembly, and their over-representation grows with maturation and experience.

Balancing inhibition develops in parallel (parvalbumin interneurons mature relatively late), which is why the developing cortex is transiently more prone to the runaway version of recurrent excitation.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

The reciprocal loop is the first circuit innovation beyond the relay, appearing wherever an animal needed to bridge a gap in time - to keep responding to a stimulus no longer present.

Its logic is so basic that the same reciprocal-doublet over-representation is seen from the nematode to the mammalian cortex, marking it as an ancient and conserved solution to the problem of memory.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Astrocytes regulate the ambient glutamate and the NMDA-receptor co-agonist supply that set loop gain, so glial state can tune whether a loop latches or lets go.

Because persistent activity is metabolically expensive - firing that continues with no external drive - the loop leans heavily on local blood flow and astrocytic energy delivery to hold its state.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

In schizophrenia, weakened recurrent excitation and disrupted NMDA-receptor function in prefrontal cortex are linked to unstable working memory - loops that cannot hold their state, so thoughts slip.

At the opposite extreme, when the balancing inhibition fails, reciprocal excitation becomes the runaway positive feedback that seeds focal seizures, the disorder treated in full in Chapter 6.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ A transient excitatory set signal 0 to 10 nanosiemens; a transient reset or inhibitory clear signal 0 to 30 nanosiemens.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ A sustained spike train encoding the held state, on-state near 10 to 50 hertz, off-state near 0.

• STATE.

◦ Joint activity level (the held bit), reciprocal synaptic weights, adaptation current, NMDA-channel occupancy.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Loop gain (product of reciprocal weights and gain slopes) near or above 1; NMDA fraction of excitation; ambient inhibition setting stability.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ NMDA decay near 100 milliseconds; persistence seconds; Hebbian weight change minutes to hours.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Unstable working memory in schizophrenia (weak or dysregulated recurrent excitation); runaway feedback seeding focal seizures when inhibition fails.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

Propose a module named persistent_state_latch that subscribes to a set signal and a reset signal and publishes a held activation that remains high after the set signal ends until a reset arrives, implemented as two mutually exciting units with a slow (NMDA-like) integration constant and a stability-limiting gain.

Its closest artificial-intelligence analogue is the recurrent cell of a recurrent neural network, specifically the gated memory cell of a long short-term memory unit, whose constant-error carousel plays the role of the self-sustaining loop.

The biological motif differs in that its persistence emerges from the physics of positive feedback with a slow synapse rather than from a trained gate, and it sits perpetually near the edge of instability, so a faithful module must include an explicit inhibitory or homeostatic term that a standard long-short-term-memory cell hides inside its learned gates.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to hold a bit of memory in a two-cell loop, so that a brief set signal produces activity that persists until a reset signal arrives.

Create a number variable called cell A activity with initial value 0.

Create a number variable called cell B activity with initial value 0.

Create a number variable called loop weight with initial value 0.6.

Create a number variable called set signal with the value 1 only during the moment of setting and 0 otherwise.

Create a number variable called reset signal with the value 1 only during the moment of clearing and 0 otherwise.

Repeat the following actions once for each time step.

    Set cell A activity to the loop weight times cell B activity plus set signal.

    Set cell B activity to the loop weight times cell A activity.

    If cell A activity is greater than 1, then set cell A activity to 1.

    If cell B activity is greater than 1, then set cell B activity to 1.

    If reset signal is equal to 1, then set both cell A activity and cell B activity to 0.

    Display cell A activity to the console.

End the repeat block.

The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because bistability is best seen by running the loop forward in time and watching the activity stay high after the input is removed, which a short update loop makes visible at a glance.

# A two-cell recurrent excitatory loop as a memory latch: a brief pulse sets a
# self-sustaining state that persists until reset (Wang, Trends Neurosci. 2001,
# on NMDA-dependent persistent activity in recurrent networks).
def gain(x):                      # saturating nonlinearity keeps the latch bounded
    return max(0.0, min(1.0, x))

W = 0.75                          # reciprocal synaptic weight (loop gain > 1 region)
a = b = 0.0                       # activities of cells A and B
for t in range(40):
    set_pulse  = 1.0 if 5 <= t < 8  else 0.0   # brief input to set the latch
    reset_pulse = 1.0 if t == 30    else 0.0   # brief input to clear it
    a, b = gain(W * b + set_pulse), gain(W * a)
    if reset_pulse:
        a = b = 0.0
    print(f"t={t:2d}  A={a:.2f}  state={'ON' if a > 0.5 else 'off'}")
# The pulse ends at t=8 but A stays ON until the reset at t=30:
# reciprocal excitation has turned a transient input into a held memory.

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

Two excitatory cells wired mouth-to-tail in a closed ring of length two, whose joint firing outlives the input that started it - the tiny latch that lets a nervous system keep something in mind after the world has moved on.


CHAPTER 5. THE FEEDFORWARD LOOP (Triad Motif) (The Two-Path Change Detector) (COG)

Of all the three-cell wiring patterns a nervous system could use, one appears again and again, in the gut bacterium's genes and the worm's brain and the mammalian cortex alike, far more often than random wiring would ever produce.

It is the feedforward loop: cell A reaches cell C by two routes at once, a fast direct line and a slower detour through cell B, and the disagreement between the two arrival times is what the circuit computes.

Because one path lags the other, the triad can notice the moment a signal starts, ignore a signal that merely persists, and time the gap between events - it is the smallest circuit that cares about change rather than mere presence.

Feedforward names the flow: all arrows point toward C, with no loop back.

Loop names the two-path closure from A to C, the fork and rejoin that defines the motif.

Change Detector names the payoff - a circuit whose natural output is the onset and offset of things, not their steady state.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

The feedforward loop is a three-node motif in which cell A connects to cell C both directly and indirectly through an intermediary cell B, so C receives the same source over two paths with different delays and, often, different signs.

Its computation depends on the signs: a coherent loop (both paths agreeing) filters out brief or noisy inputs and passes only persistent ones, while an incoherent loop (the indirect path opposing the direct one) generates a pulse at onset and detects change.

This is the three-node pattern statistically over-represented in every connectome yet analysed, from bacterial gene regulation to the nematode nervous system, precisely because these two behaviours - persistence filtering and change detection - are so broadly useful.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The graph has three nodes, A, B, and C, and three directed edges: A to B, B to C, and A to C, forming a triangle in which A is the source, C is the target, and B is the intermediary, with no edge returning to A and no reciprocal edges.

The signs of the three edges define the type: if A to C is excitatory and the A to B to C path is net excitatory, the loop is coherent (an AND-gate with delay, a persistence filter); if the indirect path is net inhibitory (A excites B, B inhibits C), the loop is incoherent (a change detector and pulse generator).

The essential quantitative feature is the delay difference: the indirect path is slower by the extra synaptic and conduction delay through B, and that lag, typically a few to tens of milliseconds, sets the width of the window the triad computes over.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

In the incoherent (change-detecting) version the source A is typically an excitatory projection neuron, the target C a principal cell (a cortical pyramidal cell or a thalamic relay cell), and the intermediary B a fast-spiking parvalbumin interneuron of the neuron catalogue whose speed and reliability make its inhibition arrive just after the direct excitation - the anatomy of feedforward inhibition in Part Two, read as a feedforward loop.

The fast-spiking personality of B is the whole trick: because it fires quickly and briefly, it delivers a sharp delayed veto that closes the window opened by the direct path, so C responds only to the leading edge.

In the coherent (persistence-filtering) version B is another excitatory relay, and the target C fires only when both the fast and slow excitatory paths coincide, so a fleeting input that ends before the slow path arrives is ignored - the adapting or high-threshold personality of C sharpens this rejection of transients.

Across the brain the same triad is drawn from whatever local cells fill the three roles, which is why it is generic rather than tied to one cell type.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

The direct A-to-C edge is a fast glutamatergic synapse (alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA)-dominated) for prompt arrival; the indirect path adds one synaptic delay at B and, in the incoherent case, a GABAergic B-to-C synapse placed perisomatically for a decisive, well-timed veto.

The delay difference is built from real components: each extra chemical synapse costs roughly 0.5 to 2 milliseconds, plus the conduction time along B's axon, giving a tunable lag.

Synaptic weights and the precise delay are plastic, so the triad can learn the time-scale of change it is most sensitive to, and short-term synaptic depression at B can make the change-detection adaptive over repeated inputs.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One instance is three cells (or three small pools) within a local circuit, typically spanning tens to a few hundred micrometres, since the intermediary must be close enough to keep its added delay short and reliable.

The motif is so small and so common that a single cortical column contains enormous numbers of overlapping feedforward loops sharing cells among many triads.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

Feedforward loops are among the most abundant three-node motifs in nervous tissue; motif-counting studies of the nematode connectome find specific feedforward triads occurring significantly more often than chance, and the same over-representation recurs across species.

They are dense in every layered sensory and cortical structure, wherever the timing and onset of signals must be extracted, and they overlap heavily, so the count of triads vastly exceeds the count of cells.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• The neocortex, where thalamic input drives both a pyramidal cell and a feedforward interneuron onto it, sharpening responses to stimulus onset.

• The hippocampus, where entorhinal input engages feedforward inhibition to enforce brief, precisely timed principal-cell firing.

• The thalamus, where feedforward triads shape the transient responses of relay cells.

• The cerebellar cortex, where mossy-fibre input to granule cells and Golgi cells forms feedforward loops that time the granule-cell response.

• The retina, where bipolar-to-ganglion direct paths and amacrine detours build change-sensitive responses.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Delete the feedforward loop and a region would lose its sense of onset: it would report that a stimulus is present but not that it just began, so it could not sharpen responses in time, reject slow drift, or measure the interval between events.

A region with feedforward loops sees edges in time the way lateral inhibition lets it see edges in space; without them, cortex would blur every event into a smear of steady firing.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

In plain words the incoherent loop differentiates: its output is large at the onset (and offset) of an input and small during steady input, approximating a temporal derivative or high-pass filter.

The coherent loop instead integrates-then-thresholds over the delay window, passing only inputs that persist longer than the indirect-path delay - a sign-sensitive delay and persistence filter, in the language of the transcription-network literature where this motif was first formalised.

Real numbers: with an indirect-path lag of, say, 5 milliseconds, the incoherent triad passes transients and produces an onset pulse a few milliseconds wide, while rejecting inputs that outlast the lag; the coherent triad conversely rejects inputs shorter than that lag.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

The signature of the incoherent loop is a brief pulse at the start of an input and silence during its steady middle - a crisp onset transient whose width equals the delay difference between the two paths.

The coherent loop's signature is a delayed, all-or-none response that appears only after the input has lasted longer than the lag, giving the circuit a built-in patience.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

The same triangle behaves as a change detector or a persistence filter depending only on the sign of its indirect path, and the width of its operative time window is set by the tunable delay, so one anatomy spans a family of temporal computations.

Short-term synaptic dynamics at the intermediary can shift the triad between more and less adaptive regimes over successive inputs, letting it habituate to repeated events.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

The three weights and the effective delay are adjustable, so the loop can learn which time-scale of change to flag and how strongly to veto persistence.

Spike-timing-dependent plasticity at the direct and indirect synapses can retune the coincidence window, sharpening or broadening the circuit's notion of simultaneous.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

The two great subtypes are the coherent feedforward loop (persistence filter, sign-agreeing paths) and the incoherent feedforward loop (change detector and pulse generator, sign-opposing paths), each with sub-variants by which input logic (AND versus OR) governs the target.

The feedforward-inhibition motif of Part Two is the incoherent feedforward loop viewed through its inhibitory intermediary, showing that the same triad underlies both this chapter and that one.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

The triad assembles as local excitatory and inhibitory cells wire onto shared targets, with the interneuron's fast, reliable connections maturing to provide the precisely timed indirect path.

The lag between paths is tuned developmentally by myelination and synapse maturation, since the computation depends on getting the two arrival times correctly staggered.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

The feedforward loop's ubiquity across kingdoms - it was discovered as an over-represented motif in bacterial gene-regulation networks before being found in nervous systems - argues that it is a convergent solution reinvented wherever a network must filter noise or detect change.

Its persistence across such distant systems marks it as one of the most fundamental computational building blocks known.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Astrocytes at the intermediary's synapses set the timing and reliability of the indirect path by clearing transmitter and buffering ions, so glial state can subtly retune the triad's delay.

Myelination of the intermediary's axon fixes its conduction delay, making oligodendrocytes quiet partners in setting the circuit's time window.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

When the inhibitory intermediary is weakened - as in the parvalbumin-interneuron dysfunction implicated in schizophrenia and some epilepsies - the incoherent loop loses its delayed veto, so principal cells fire imprecisely and cortical timing degrades.

Loss of feedforward inhibition removes the temporal sharpening that keeps excitation brief, contributing to the runaway spread of activity in seizure.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ One source signal delivered over a fast direct edge (0 to 10 nanosiemens excitatory) and a slow indirect edge through the intermediary (excitatory or inhibitory, 0 to 30 nanosiemens).

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ A change signal (onset and offset pulses) for the incoherent type, or a persistence-gated signal for the coherent type.

• STATE.

◦ Intermediary activity, direct-path drive, target voltage, short-term depression level at the intermediary.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Three edge weights and their signs; indirect-path delay 2 to 20 milliseconds; target input logic (AND versus OR).

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Direct synapse near 2 milliseconds; per-stage delay 0.5 to 2 milliseconds; effective detection window a few to tens of milliseconds.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Loss of feedforward inhibition (parvalbumin-interneuron dysfunction) in schizophrenia and epilepsy, degrading temporal precision and change detection.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

Propose a module named feedforward_change_detector that subscribes to a single source stream and publishes an onset-and-offset transient by comparing the source against a delayed, oppositely signed copy of itself routed through an intermediary node.

Its closest artificial-intelligence analogue is a temporal high-pass filter or a residual comparison such as the difference-of-delays used in edge and onset detectors, and, in its coherent form, the sign-sensitive delay used in noise-robust gating.

The biological motif differs in that the delay and signs are physical and locally tunable, the intermediary is a shared node feeding many overlapping triads at once, and short-term synaptic depression makes the comparison adaptive - so a faithful module exposes an explicit delay line and an intermediary that can be reused across many detectors rather than a single fixed subtraction.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to detect change by comparing a signal against a delayed copy of itself sent through an intermediary, so the output pulses when the input starts or stops.

Create a number variable called direct path delay with initial value 0.

Create a number variable called indirect path delay with initial value 5.

Create a list variable called input signal holding the source value at each time step.

Create an empty list variable called output signal.

For each time step index in the input signal, perform the following actions.

    Set the direct term to the input signal at this time step.

    Calculate the earlier index by subtracting indirect path delay from this time step index.

    If the earlier index is less than zero, then set the indirect term to zero.

    Otherwise, set the indirect term to the input signal at the earlier index.

    Set the loop output to the direct term minus the indirect term.

    If the loop output is less than zero, then set the loop output to zero.

    Append the loop output to the output signal list.

End the loop.

Display the output signal list to the console.

The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because the incoherent feedforward loop is exactly a signal minus a delayed copy of itself, and running that over a step input shows the onset pulse and the silence during steady state in a few lines.

# Incoherent feedforward loop as a change detector: the target sees a fast
# excitatory copy of A and a delayed inhibitory copy of A through B, so it
# fires only when the input changes (Mangan & Alon, PNAS 2003, on the FFL).
DELAY = 5   # extra time steps through the intermediary B (indirect-path lag)

# a step input: off, then on for a while, then off again
stim = [0]*5 + [1]*15 + [0]*10

out = []
for t in range(len(stim)):
    direct = stim[t]                          # fast excitatory path A -> C
    indirect = stim[t - DELAY] if t >= DELAY else 0   # slow inhibitory path A -> B -> C
    out.append(max(0.0, direct - indirect))   # C responds to the difference

for t, (s, o) in enumerate(zip(stim, out)):
    print(f"t={t:2d}  input={s}  output={o:.0f}  {'<-- onset pulse' if o else ''}")
# Output pulses at the onset (and would at offset for a signed target) but is
# silent through the steady middle: the triad reports change, not presence.

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

A three-cell triangle in which the source reaches the target twice, once straight and once through a slower middleman of opposite sign, so the target answers only when the world changes - the smallest circuit that can tell now from a moment ago.


CHAPTER 6. RECURRENT (MUTUAL) EXCITATION WITHIN A POPULATION (Self-Amplifying Pool) (The Bonfire Circuit) (COG)

Scale the two-cell latch of Chapter 4 up to a whole pool of excitatory cells, each re-exciting many others, and you get the engine that makes the cortex powerful and the same engine that, unchecked, makes it seize.

Like a bonfire, a population of mutually exciting neurons can take a small spark and build it into a self-sustaining blaze - which is exactly what you want for amplification and memory, and exactly what you fear when the fire jumps its ring.

This motif is the amplifier of the cortex, the substrate of attractor states and persistent working memory, and, when its balancing inhibition fails, the substrate of epileptic seizure - one wiring diagram poised forever between computation and catastrophe.

Recurrent names the closed feedback among the members - activity that comes back around many times over.

Mutual Excitation names the sign - the members feed each other forward, not brake each other.

Bonfire names the dynamics - a spark can catch, self-sustain, and, without a firebreak, run away.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

This motif is a pool of excitatory cells wired so that each cell excites many others in the pool, creating dense positive feedback across a population rather than around a single pair.

Its computation is amplification and self-sustaining activity: weak or brief input can be magnified into strong, prolonged population firing, and with modifiable synapses the pool can settle into stable self-maintaining patterns, the attractor states that store memories and hold information online.

The very feature that gives it power - strong positive feedback - is also its danger, because without adequate inhibition the feedback runs away into the pathological hypersynchrony of a seizure.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The graph is a population of N excitatory nodes with a high density of recurrent excitatory edges among them (each cell connecting to a few percent of the others in a local cortical patch), all positive (glutamatergic), plus an obligatory population of inhibitory nodes (GABAergic interneurons) receiving from and projecting back onto the excitatory pool.

The recurrent excitatory connection probability among nearby cortical pyramidal cells is on the order of a few percent to occasionally higher within dense clusters, and this recurrent input can supply the majority of a cell's excitation - local recurrent connections are estimated to provide well over half of the excitatory drive in a cortical patch.

The single most important quantity is the balance between recurrent excitatory gain and feedback inhibitory gain; an engineer would redraw this as a large positive-feedback excitatory block wrapped in a negative-feedback inhibitory block, and would recognise that stability lives only in a narrow band of that balance.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The members are excitatory pyramidal cells - layer 2/3 and layer 5 pyramidal neurons of the cortex, and the pyramidal cells of hippocampal area CA3, whose extensive recurrent collaterals make CA3 the anatomically proven case of a recurrently connected excitatory pool.

Their regular-firing, sometimes bursting personality with strong N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA)-mediated recurrent synapses is what lets the pool sustain low-rate persistent activity rather than only brief bursts; the slow NMDA component is essential, because it lets the fire smoulder at a stable rate instead of flaring and dying.

The indispensable countercast is the parvalbumin-positive fast-spiking basket cell of the neuron catalogue, whose rapid, powerful, perisomatic inhibition is the firebreak that keeps recurrent excitation from running away - its fast-spiking personality tracks the excitatory pool almost instantly, holding the balance.

When this inhibitory partner is weakened, removed, or overwhelmed, the same excitatory pool that computed a memory becomes the generator of a seizure, so the cast is fundamentally a pairing of an amplifier with its governor.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

The recurrent excitatory edges are glutamate synapses on dendritic spines with a substantial slow NMDA component (decay near 100 milliseconds), the key to stable low-rate persistence, alongside fast alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) for rapid recruitment.

The controlling inhibition is GABAergic, delivered perisomatically by basket cells (fast gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-A receptors) and dendritically by somatostatin-positive Martinotti cells, setting both the gain and the stability of the pool.
