The third node is the target cell (for example the motoneuron), which receives the excitatory edge from the input axon.

The critical edge is therefore interneuron-terminal to afferent-terminal, an inhibitory axo-axonic synapse, and its effect is to shrink the excitatory edge that runs from afferent-terminal to target.

The interneuron is itself driven by other afferents and by descending motor commands, which is how movement recruits the gate.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The input role is played by large myelinated primary afferents, chiefly the group Ia and Ib muscle afferents and low-threshold cutaneous afferents of the dorsal root ganglion (the sensory relay cell of the Layer 6 catalogue); their fast, faithful, high-safety-factor firing is exactly what makes a terminal-level tap valuable, because you cannot easily quieten such a reliable line any other way.

The gate role is played by specialised GABAergic interneurons of the deep dorsal horn and intermediate spinal grey, the axo-axonic (GABA-releasing) interneurons whose entire morphology is built to reach afferent terminals; their tonic, movement-gated firing makes them a continuously adjustable valve rather than an on-off switch.

The target role is played by the alpha motoneuron (Chapter of the neuron catalogue devoted to the final common path), whose large size and integrative personality mean it benefits from having noise trimmed at source rather than fighting it at the soma.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

The gated afferent terminal carries two receptor systems that together produce primary afferent depolarisation (PAD).

Ionotropic GABA-A receptors on the afferent terminal open a chloride channel, but because these terminals actively load chloride inward through the sodium-potassium-chloride cotransporter NKCC1, their chloride reversal potential sits near minus 35 millivolts, so GABA-A opening depolarises rather than hyperpolarises the terminal.

That paradoxical depolarisation still inhibits release, by two routes: it inactivates the terminal's voltage-gated sodium channels so the incoming spike is smaller, and it opens a shunting conductance that short-circuits the spike, both cutting calcium entry and therefore transmitter release.

Metabotropic GABA-B receptors on the same terminals add a second, slower gate: they directly suppress presynaptic calcium channels and reduce release without contributing to the depolarisation, and recent proprioceptive-afferent work shows GABA-B carries a large share of the presynaptic inhibition of Ia fibres.

Characteristic weight is a release reduction of roughly 20 to 40 percent per activated line, graded and rapidly reversible.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One instance is a single gated terminal plus the GABAergic bouton clamped onto it, a structure a few micrometres across (a micrometre is a thousandth of a millimetre), often gathered with others into a glomerular arrangement wrapped by glia.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

The count is astronomical and uncensused; every large primary afferent entering the cord carries presynaptic gates on many of its thousands of terminal branches, so the spinal instances alone run into the many millions, with further large populations in the dorsal column nuclei, thalamus and cerebellar mossy-fibre terminals.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• The spinal cord dorsal horn and intermediate grey, where it gates cutaneous and proprioceptive afferents during movement and filters pain and touch.

• The dorsal column nuclei (gracile and cuneate) of the medulla, where it sharpens tactile signals before they ascend.

• The ventrobasal thalamus, where afferent terminals are gated before relay to cortex.

• The cerebellar granule layer, where mossy-fibre terminals in glomeruli are presynaptically gated by Golgi cells, trimming the input to the expansion recoder.

• The retina and olfactory bulb, where terminal-level gating shapes early sensory transmission.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Remove this motif from the cord and the moving body would drown in its own sensation: every step would fire back a storm of spindle and skin signals that the motor circuits must otherwise suppress, and reflex loops would ring uncontrollably.

The region loses the ability to quieten a chosen input without dimming the receiving cell, so the only remaining brake is the blunt one that silences the whole neuron.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

The transfer function is multiplicative on one line: output release equals baseline release times a gain factor g, where g falls from 1 toward about 0.6 to 0.8 as the gate is activated, with no change to the target cell's other inputs or to its threshold.

This is divisive per-input gating, distinct from the subtractive whole-cell inhibition of postsynaptic motifs; the timescale of the GABA-A component is tens of milliseconds and the GABA-B component hundreds of milliseconds.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

Primary afferent depolarisation rises over about 10 to 20 milliseconds and decays over 100 to 200 milliseconds, so the tap is a slow-closing, slow-opening valve compared with the millisecond veto of perisomatic inhibition, well matched to the timescale of a movement rather than a single spike.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

At rest a tonic background of presynaptic inhibition sets afferent gain; during voluntary movement descending commands sharply increase the gate on the relevant afferents (movement-gated suppression); after spinal cord injury the GABA-B component is reduced, releasing the tap and contributing to spasticity.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

The gate's strength is set developmentally and modulated by descending systems and by injury, but it is not a classic learning synapse; its adjustments are state-dependent gain settings rather than stored associations, which is one reason the motif is tagged non-cognitive.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

The fast GABA-A/PAD variant dominates cutaneous and pain gating; the slow GABA-B variant dominates proprioceptive-afferent gating; a distinct alpha-2-subunit GABA-A variant is implicated specifically in spinal pain control.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

The chloride-loading transporter NKCC1 that makes the depolarising gate possible is expressed early and maintained in afferent terminals into adulthood, unlike central neurons which switch to chloride-extruding KCC2; the axo-axonic interneurons find and wrap afferent terminals during the assembly of the dorsal horn.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

Terminal-level gating is ancient and widespread, present in invertebrate sensory systems and conserved throughout the vertebrate spinal cord, reflecting its role as a basic economy measure for any nervous system that must move without being blinded by the consequences of moving.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Glial wrapping of the synaptic glomeruli confines released GABA and limits spillover, and astrocytic GABA uptake shapes the decay of the gate; the chloride gradient itself is a metabolically maintained resource.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Loss of presynaptic inhibition after spinal cord injury or stroke unmasks afferent input and contributes to spasticity and hyperreflexia; disordered presynaptic gating of pain afferents is implicated in chronic pain and allodynia (pain from normally innocuous touch); dystonia involves reduced spinal and brainstem presynaptic inhibition.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ Afferent spike trains on the gated line (glutamatergic, group Ia/Ib/cutaneous); descending motor commands and other afferents driving the GABAergic gate interneuron.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ Reduced transmitter release from the gated terminal, delivering a fraction (roughly 0.6 to 0.8) of baseline excitation to the target while leaving all other inputs and the target's threshold unchanged.

• STATE.

◦ Terminal membrane potential, terminal chloride concentration (reversal near minus 35 millivolts), per-line gain factor g between 0 and 1.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ NKCC1 chloride load setting reversal near minus 35 millivolts; GABA-A shunt and sodium-inactivation weight; GABA-B calcium-channel suppression weight; release reduction 20 to 40 percent.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Primary afferent depolarisation rise 10 to 20 milliseconds, decay 100 to 200 milliseconds; GABA-B component up to several hundred milliseconds.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Reduced GABA-B-mediated presynaptic inhibition of proprioceptive afferents after spinal cord injury, producing spasticity and hyperreflexia; loss of afferent gating in dystonia and chronic pain.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

The konnectome module is named per_input_gain_gate, a wrapper that sits on one named input channel of a receiving module and scales that channel's message by a factor between zero and one under control of a separate gate signal, without altering the receiving module's threshold or its other channels.

It subscribes to the gated channel's outgoing messages and to a gate command (for example a movement-in-progress flag), and it publishes an attenuated copy of that one channel.

The closest artificial-intelligence analogue is an input-specific multiplicative attention or gating weight, as in a gated recurrent unit's input gate, but the biology differs by acting at the sender's output rather than the receiver's input summation, so it saves the receiver from ever integrating the noise at all.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

This section does not apply to this microcircuit type for the reason that this motif serves a substrate or regulatory role rather than a cognitive-computational role, and is tagged (NON-COG).

CODE SAMPLE:

This section does not apply to this microcircuit type for the reason that this motif serves a substrate or regulatory role rather than a cognitive-computational role, and is tagged (NON-COG).

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

An inhibitory synapse that lands on another axon's terminal rather than on any cell body or dendrite, and that inhibits by depolarising - the only brake in the body that turns down one input line while leaving the receiving neuron and all its other lines completely untouched.


CHAPTER 13. THE PERISOMATIC-DENDRITIC DIVISION OF LABOUR (Two-Site Interneuron Targeting Motif) (The Two-Handed Governor) (COG)

A cortical pyramidal cell is governed by two different hands that never reach for the same place.

One hand grips the neck of the cell, the soma and the axon's starting gate, and can veto the finished thought at the instant it would be spoken.

The other hand rests far out on the fine tips of the dendrites, where it can quietly refuse a particular incoming idea before it is ever added up.

The same principal cell is thus controlled at two addresses that mean two different things: whether it speaks at all, and what it is allowed to listen to.

Perisomatic names the first hand's grip: around (peri) the cell body (soma) and the axon initial segment.

Dendritic names the second hand: out on the branching antennae that gather input.

Division of labour names the discovery that these are two specialised interneuron families, not one, each owning one site.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

This motif is the pairing of two inhibitory control points on a single excitatory principal cell: fast-spiking parvalbumin (PV) interneurons inhibiting the perisomatic region (cell body and axon initial segment), and somatostatin (SST) interneurons inhibiting the distal dendrites.

The computation is a separation of two variables that a one-site inhibitory scheme would confound: perisomatic inhibition sets output gain and spike timing (whether and precisely when the cell fires), while dendritic inhibition sets input selection (which dendritic inputs are allowed to contribute and whether dendritic regenerative events occur).

By placing the two brakes at electrically distant sites, the cortex can gate a cell's inputs and its outputs independently, which is the physical basis of controlling what a neuron computes separately from how loudly it reports the result.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

There is one principal node and two inhibitory nodes, with a characteristic difference in how each is recruited.

The principal node is an excitatory pyramidal cell, glutamatergic, with a soma, an axon initial segment, and a long apical dendrite ending in a distal tuft.

The first inhibitory node is the PV interneuron (basket and chandelier subtypes), with an inhibitory edge onto the pyramidal cell's soma and proximal dendrites (basket) or specifically onto the axon initial segment (chandelier); this node is preferentially driven feedforward, meaning the same external input that excites the pyramidal cell also excites the PV cell.

The second inhibitory node is the SST interneuron (Martinotti subtype), with an inhibitory edge onto the pyramidal cell's distal apical dendrites; this node is preferentially driven feedback, meaning it is excited by the pyramidal cells it inhibits, so its brake grows with local activity.

Both inhibitory edges are GABAergic; the pyramidal cell excites the SST cell (excitatory edge) closing a feedback loop, and external and thalamic afferents excite the PV cell (excitatory edge) forming the feedforward limb.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The perisomatic role is played by the parvalbumin-positive basket cell and the parvalbumin-positive chandelier (axo-axonic) cell of the neuron catalogue; their fast-spiking, non-adapting, minimally delayed personality lets them deliver a millisecond-precise veto exactly when the cell would fire, which is why they set spike timing and pace gamma rhythms, and the chandelier's exclusive grip on the axon initial segment makes it the last possible checkpoint before an action potential leaves.

The dendritic role is played by the somatostatin-positive Martinotti cell, whose axon ascends to layer 1 and spreads across the apical tufts; its facilitating, adapting, late-recruited personality means its brake builds up during sustained pyramidal firing rather than arriving instantly, perfectly suited to a feedback governor that grows with activity and gates dendritic integration and burst firing.

A third, modulating personality belongs to the vasoactive-intestinal-peptide (vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)) interneuron, which preferentially inhibits the SST cell and so lifts the dendritic brake (the subject of Chapter 14), tying this motif to disinhibition.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

All inhibitory edges use gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) acting on postsynaptic GABA-A receptors, fast chloride channels, but their placement gives them opposite computational meanings.

Perisomatic PV synapses land on the soma and axon initial segment where, being electrically close to the spike trigger zone, they exert powerful divisive and timing control with large, reliable, depressing unitary weights.

Dendritic SST synapses land on thin distal dendrites where they are electrically remote from the soma, so they act locally to veto dendritic calcium spikes and gate synaptic integration rather than to time output, with facilitating unitary weights that strengthen during trains.

PV cells are electrically coupled to one another by connexin-36 gap junctions, synchronising the perisomatic net; SST cells are more sparsely coupled.

Cholinergic input facilitates Martinotti-cell dendritic inhibition, linking arousal to input gating.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One instance is a single pyramidal cell together with the handful of PV cells gripping its perisomatic region and the SST cells contacting its distal dendrites, a functional unit spanning a few hundred micrometres vertically from soma to tuft, though each interneuron in fact contacts many pyramidal cells (a PV basket cell may contact hundreds).

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

Every excitatory pyramidal cell of the neocortex and hippocampus carries this dual-site governance, so the number of instances is on the order of the number of cortical pyramidal cells, in the billions; PV and SST cells together make up roughly 60 to 70 percent of all cortical interneurons, split roughly evenly.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• The entire neocortex, all areas and layers, where it governs every pyramidal cell's output gain and dendritic integration.

• The hippocampus (areas CA1, CA3 and dentate), where PV basket cells time principal-cell spikes and SST oriens-lacunosum-moleculare cells gate distal entorhinal input.

• The basolateral amygdala, where perisomatic basket cells control principal-cell output during fear learning.

• The striatum, where fast-spiking PV interneurons provide perisomatic feedforward inhibition to projection neurons.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Strip the perisomatic hand from a region and its principal cells lose temporal discipline: spikes are no longer chopped into precise windows, gamma rhythms collapse, and excitation runs toward seizure.

Strip the dendritic hand and the region loses the ability to gate which inputs a cell integrates and to control dendritic burst firing, so context can no longer selectively silence a branch, and the separation of what-is-computed from how-loudly-it-is-reported is lost; the region degrades from a two-knob controller to a single blunt volume dial.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

Perisomatic inhibition acts largely divisively and as a timing gate: it scales the pyramidal cell's input-output slope and narrows the window in which it may fire, and being near the axon initial segment it can subtract a decisive last-moment veto.

Dendritic inhibition acts locally and often subtractively on a branch, raising the threshold for dendritic calcium spikes and removing specific inputs from the sum without changing the cell's overall gain; the two therefore factorise the transfer function into an input-selection stage (dendrite) followed by an output-gain-and-timing stage (soma).

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

PV perisomatic inhibition is fast: sub-millisecond onset, GABA-A decay near 5 to 10 milliseconds, able to entrain gamma oscillations at 30 to 90 cycles per second.

SST dendritic inhibition is slower to recruit, building over tens of milliseconds during a train because its synapses facilitate, giving it a natural role at theta timescales and in sustained gating.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

In the quiet feedforward regime PV inhibition dominates, enforcing precise, sparse firing; during sustained local activity SST feedback inhibition builds and clamps the dendrites; when VIP cells fire (arousal, reward, movement) the dendritic brake is lifted and the cell's dendrites open for plasticity; runaway excitation appears when PV inhibition fails.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

Both inhibitory synapses are plastic: PV perisomatic synapses onto pyramidal cells undergo their own long-term potentiation and depression that reshape output timing, while lifting SST dendritic inhibition (disinhibition) is a permissive gate for potentiation of the pyramidal cell's excitatory dendritic inputs, so the dendritic hand's release literally licenses learning.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

The perisomatic family splits into basket cells (soma and proximal dendrites) and chandelier cells (axon initial segment only); the dendritic family centres on the Martinotti cell but includes other SST subtypes; regional variants tune the balance, for example the hippocampal oriens-lacunosum-moleculare cell as the dendritic governor of CA1.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

PV and SST interneurons are born in the medial ganglionic eminence and migrate tangentially into the cortex, then sort to their target compartments; PV cells and their perisomatic baskets mature late, and their maturation closes the critical period for sensory plasticity, tying the perisomatic hand's arrival to the end of heightened learning.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

The two-site scheme is conserved across mammals and has ancient roots in the ganglionic-eminence interneuron program; the human version shows enlarged and elaborated interneurons and a distinctive rosehip interneuron not found in rodents, elaborating rather than replacing the basic division of labour.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Perineuronal nets, lattices of extracellular matrix, preferentially enwrap PV cells, stabilising their fast phenotype and their synapses and marking the close of critical periods; astrocytes clear GABA at both sites and supply the metabolic demand of fast-spiking PV cells, which are among the most energetically expensive neurons in the brain.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Reduced perisomatic PV function is a leading substrate of schizophrenia, where loss of parvalbumin and of the GABA-synthesising enzyme GAD67 in these cells degrades gamma rhythms and cognition; PV dysfunction contributes to epilepsy and to autism-spectrum imbalance; SST-cell loss is implicated in depression and in Alzheimer's disease.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ Feedforward thalamic and cortical excitation to PV cells; feedback excitation from local pyramidal cells to SST cells; VIP inhibition onto SST cells; cholinergic modulation of SST cells.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ GABAergic perisomatic inhibition setting pyramidal output gain and spike timing; GABAergic distal-dendritic inhibition setting input selection and dendritic-spike threshold.

• STATE.

◦ Perisomatic conductance (0 to 30 nanosiemens), dendritic conductance, gamma phase, dendritic-calcium-spike enable flag.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ PV synapse near axon initial segment, GABA-A decay 5 to 10 milliseconds, depressing weights; SST synapse on distal tuft, facilitating weights; gamma band 30 to 90 hertz.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Perisomatic inhibition onset under 1 millisecond, decay 5 to 10 milliseconds; dendritic inhibition recruitment tens of milliseconds.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Parvalbumin and GAD67 reduction in perisomatic interneurons in schizophrenia, degrading gamma synchrony; PV failure as a seizure substrate; SST loss in depression and Alzheimer's disease.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

The konnectome module is named output_gain_and_input_selection_governor, wrapping a principal-cell module with two independent inhibitory controllers: an output_timing_gate on the module's spike output and an input_selection_gate on a named subset of the module's input channels.

It subscribes, for the output gate, to feedforward copies of the module's drive and, for the input gate, to feedback copies of the module's own activity and to a permission signal (from a disinhibition module); it publishes a timing-and-gain-scaled output and a per-branch input mask.

The closest artificial-intelligence analogue is factorising a layer into a separate gating of inputs (like a per-feature mask or gated dendritic subunit) and a gain-plus-timing control on outputs (like layer normalisation with a learned scale), but biology differs by making the two gates physically distinct cell types recruited on different loops and timescales, so they can be modulated independently.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to show that inhibiting the dendrite selects which inputs count, while inhibiting the soma sets output gain and timing, and that the two act independently.

Create a list called dendritic inputs holding the incoming synaptic currents on the distal dendrite.

Create a number variable called dendritic inhibition with initial value between 0 and 1, where 1 means the dendritic brake is fully on.

Create a number variable called perisomatic gain with initial value between 0 and 1, where 1 means no perisomatic brake and 0 means full veto.

Create a number variable called selected drive with initial value 0.

For each input current in dendritic inputs, perform the following actions.

    Multiply the input current by the quantity one minus dendritic inhibition.

    Add the result to selected drive.

End the loop.

Create a number variable called soma drive equal to selected drive plus the basal excitation.

Create a number variable called output equal to soma drive multiplied by perisomatic gain.

If output is greater than the firing threshold is true, then perform the following actions.

    Report that the cell fires, at a time set by the perisomatic brake.

Otherwise, perform the following actions.

    Report that the cell is silent.

End the conditional block.

The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because the point is that two knobs at two sites act on two different variables, and a short function with two independent parameters makes that separation self-evident.

# Two-site inhibition of a cortical pyramidal cell.
# Dendritic (SST) inhibition selects which inputs count; perisomatic (PV)
# inhibition sets output gain and timing (Tremblay et al., Neuron 2016).
def pyramidal_output(dendritic_inputs, basal, dend_inh, peri_gain, thresh=1.0):
    # dend_inh in [0,1]: fraction of each dendritic input vetoed at the branch
    selected = sum(i * (1.0 - dend_inh) for i in dendritic_inputs)  # input selection
    soma_drive = selected + basal
    output = soma_drive * peri_gain                                 # output gain
    return output, output > thresh

inputs = [0.4, 0.5, 0.3]   # three distal dendritic inputs
# Same cell, four control settings: note dendrite changes WHAT is summed,
# soma changes HOW MUCH of the result is reported, independently.
for dend_inh, peri_gain in [(0.0, 1.0), (0.8, 1.0), (0.0, 0.3), (0.8, 0.3)]:
    out, fires = pyramidal_output(inputs, basal=0.2, dend_inh=dend_inh, peri_gain=peri_gain)
    print(f"dend_inh={dend_inh}  peri_gain={peri_gain}  output={out:.2f}  fires={fires}")

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

Two GABA-releasing cell families that never share a target site - one fast-spiking family clamping the soma and axon initial segment to time and scale the output, one facilitating family reaching the far dendrites to choose the inputs - so that a single principal cell is governed by two hands that mean two entirely different things.


CHAPTER 14. DISINHIBITION (The Inhibition-of-Inhibition Motif) (The Permission Circuit) (COG)

Most gates in the brain are opened by pushing; this one is opened by removing a guard.

A principal cell sits under a standing inhibitory brake, and rather than exciting the cell directly, this motif silences the interneuron holding the brake, so the cell springs free by default.

It is how the cortex says yes: not by shouting louder, but by momentarily dismissing the sentry that was saying no.

A small, specialised interneuron, tuned to arousal, reward and movement, is the finger that lifts the guard, and its click opens the dendrites of thousands of principal cells for learning.

Inhibition-of-inhibition names the logic: a double negative, which in circuit algebra is a positive.

Permission names the meaning: nothing is added, but something previously forbidden is now allowed.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

Disinhibition is a three-node motif in which one inhibitory interneuron inhibits a second inhibitory interneuron, which in turn inhibits a principal cell, so that activating the first cell releases the principal cell from inhibition.

The computation is a gate: it does not carry content, it grants or withdraws permission for a signal already present to have its effect, implementing a logical AND between an ongoing input and a permission signal.

In the cortex its canonical form is the vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)-to-SST-to-pyramidal circuit, in which vasoactive-intestinal-peptide (VIP) interneurons inhibit somatostatin (SST) interneurons, lifting the dendritic brake on pyramidal cells and opening their dendrites for plasticity - the physical substrate of attention and of learning-when-it-matters.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

There are three inhibitory-or-principal nodes in a chain of alternating signs.

The first node is the disinhibitory interneuron, a GABAergic VIP cell, driven from outside the local circuit by long-range top-down cortical input, by thalamic input, and by neuromodulators (acetylcholine and serotonin); its outgoing edge is inhibitory.

The second node is the target interneuron, a GABAergic SST (Martinotti) cell, receiving the inhibitory edge from the VIP cell; its own outgoing edge is inhibitory and lands on the distal dendrites of the principal cell.

The third node is the principal cell, an excitatory pyramidal neuron, receiving the inhibitory edge from the SST cell on its dendrites and receiving its content-carrying excitatory inputs elsewhere.

The chain of signs is therefore minus-then-minus onto the principal cell: when the VIP cell fires, the SST cell falls silent, and the pyramidal dendrite is released; the net sign from VIP to pyramid is positive (disinhibitory).

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The releaser role is played by the vasoactive-intestinal-peptide-positive interneuron of the neuron catalogue, a slender, irregular-spiking cell sitting in the upper layers; its personality is to be a specialist listener for context - it fires to arousal, locomotion, reward and punishment signals rather than to the local sensory content, which is exactly what a permission cell should key on.

The guard role is played by the somatostatin-positive Martinotti cell, whose adapting, dendrite-targeting personality (Chapter 13) means that removing it specifically unclamps the pyramidal cell's distal dendrites, the very site where top-down inputs and plasticity live.

The freed cell is the pyramidal neuron, whose dendritic calcium spikes - normally suppressed by the SST brake - become possible the moment the guard is lifted, converting permission into a dendritic plateau that tags synapses for strengthening.

A note on a variant cast member: cholinergic ChAT-positive VIP cells excite their neighbours directly rather than disinhibiting, showing the VIP class is not monolithic.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

Both inhibitory edges use gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) on GABA-A receptors; the VIP-to-SST synapse is notable for facilitating at high firing frequencies, so a burst of VIP activity is disproportionately effective at silencing the SST cell.

The SST-to-pyramid synapse is the facilitating distal-dendritic synapse of Chapter 13.

The VIP cell's driving inputs include long-range glutamatergic top-down axons and cholinergic and serotonergic neuromodulatory fibres, the latter acting on nicotinic and serotonin-3 receptors that make VIP cells fire to arousal.

Characteristic effect: modest VIP firing can reduce SST output enough to lift dendritic inhibition by tens of percent, gating dendritic calcium electrogenesis.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One instance is a VIP cell, the SST cell it silences, and the pyramidal dendrites thereby released, a local unit within a cortical column spanning a few hundred micrometres, with heavy convergence and divergence at each stage so that one VIP cell influences many SST cells and, through them, many pyramidal cells.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

VIP cells make up roughly 10 to 15 percent of cortical interneurons and are concentrated in layers 2/3; the disinhibitory motif is present in every cortical area, so instances number in the hundreds of millions, with specialised installations in the amygdala's intercalated clusters and in the striatum.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• The neocortex, all areas, especially superficial layers 2/3, where VIP-SST-pyramid disinhibition mediates attention, arousal-gated processing and learning.

• The primary sensory cortices, where locomotion and arousal recruit VIP cells to boost gain.

• The amygdala's intercalated cell clusters, where disinhibition of the central-amygdala output gate is the mechanism of fear extinction.

• The hippocampus, where VIP interneuron-selective cells disinhibit principal cells to time learning.

• The striatum, where interneuron-to-interneuron inhibition disinhibits projection neurons during action selection.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Without this motif a region can still be excited and still be inhibited, but it loses its permission channel: it can no longer selectively open its principal cells' dendrites in response to context, arousal or reward, so learning can no longer be gated to the moments that matter.

The amygdala without intercalated disinhibition cannot extinguish fear; the cortex without VIP disinhibition cannot let attention and behavioural state selectively license plasticity, so the region becomes a system that reacts but cannot be given permission to change.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

The transfer function is a gate, mathematically a gain that multiplies the effect of the principal cell's other inputs by a permission factor p that rises from near 0 (guard present) toward 1 (guard removed) as the VIP cell fires.

Because the released site is the dendrite, the gate specifically enables dendritic calcium spikes and thereby the plasticity of dendritic inputs; it is a permissive multiplication, implementing logical AND of content and permission rather than adding any signal of its own.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

Disinhibition operates on the timescale of behavioural state and attention, tens of milliseconds to seconds: VIP cells ramp with locomotion and arousal over hundreds of milliseconds, and the facilitating VIP-to-SST synapse means sustained VIP firing progressively deepens the release.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

In the resting inhibited regime the SST guard is on and pyramidal dendrites are clamped; in the aroused or attentive regime VIP firing lifts the guard and dendrites open; the motif can also flip during specific behaviours (a whisking or running bout), and pathological over-disinhibition removes a needed brake and can promote runaway activity.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

Disinhibition is the permissive switch for plasticity rather than the store itself: by opening the dendrite it allows coincident excitatory inputs to trigger the calcium signals that induce long-term potentiation, so the motif gates when the principal cell's synapses are allowed to learn, and its own VIP-SST synapse can facilitate to sharpen that gating.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

The canonical VIP-to-SST cortical variant lifts dendritic inhibition; a VIP-to-PV variant lifts perisomatic inhibition in some circuits; the amygdala intercalated-cluster variant disinhibits an output nucleus for fear extinction; the ChAT-VIP variant excites directly rather than disinhibiting.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

VIP cells arise largely from the caudal ganglionic eminence (unlike PV and SST cells from the medial eminence) and populate the superficial layers late, and the maturation of the disinhibitory motif parallels the emergence of state-dependent and attention-gated learning in the young cortex.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

Interneuron-targeting-interneuron wiring is conserved across mammals, and the caudal-ganglionic-eminence VIP program is an evolutionarily distinct interneuron stream; disinhibition as a design appears wherever a nervous system needs a cheap permission signal rather than a costly direct drive.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Cholinergic and serotonergic neuromodulatory systems are the effective support that recruits the motif, coupling global arousal to local permission; astrocytes clear GABA at both inhibitory synapses and shape the duration of the released window.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Failure of intercalated-cluster disinhibition impairs fear extinction and is implicated in post-traumatic stress disorder and anxiety; disordered cortical disinhibition is implicated in autism-spectrum conditions and in epilepsy when the brake is lifted inappropriately; VIP-circuit dysfunction is linked to attentional deficits.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ Long-range top-down glutamatergic input, thalamic input, and cholinergic and serotonergic arousal signals driving the VIP cell.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ A permission signal: reduced SST output that lifts distal-dendritic inhibition on pyramidal cells, enabling dendritic calcium spikes and plasticity.

• STATE.

◦ VIP firing rate, SST output level, dendritic-inhibition level, per-pyramid permission factor p between 0 and 1.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ VIP-to-SST synapse facilitating; SST-to-dendrite conductance lifted by tens of percent; VIP fraction 10 to 15 percent of interneurons.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Behavioural-state ramp hundreds of milliseconds to seconds; synaptic facilitation over tens of milliseconds.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Impaired amygdala intercalated disinhibition in post-traumatic stress disorder and failure of fear extinction; cortical over- or under-disinhibition in autism and epilepsy.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

The konnectome module is named gate_opening_permission_broker, a three-stage inhibitory chain whose net effect is to enable, on command, a target module's ability to integrate and learn from its inputs without supplying any content itself.

It subscribes to a permission signal (a top-down attention flag, a reward or arousal signal) and publishes a release command that lowers a named inhibitory gate on the target module, specifically its dendritic-input-and-plasticity channel.

The closest artificial-intelligence analogue is a multiplicative gating unit or an attention gate (as in the gate of a long short-term memory cell or a gating network in a mixture of experts), but biology differs by implementing the gate as a double-negative through a dedicated releaser cell keyed to global state, so permission is decoupled from content and can be granted by arousal rather than by the data.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to open a gate by inhibiting the inhibitor, so that a content signal has its effect only when a separate permission signal is present.

Create a number variable called content input with a value representing the excitatory drive to the principal cell.

Create a number variable called permission signal with value 1 if the releaser cell is firing and 0 otherwise.

Create a number variable called guard strength with initial value 1, representing the inhibitory interneuron's brake fully on.

If permission signal is equal to 1 is true, then perform the following actions.

    Set guard strength to 0, because the releaser has silenced the inhibitor.

Otherwise, perform the following actions.

    Set guard strength to 1, because the inhibitor is active.

End the conditional block.

Create a number variable called permitted drive equal to content input multiplied by the quantity one minus guard strength.

If permitted drive is greater than the plasticity threshold is true, then perform the following actions.

    Report that the dendrite is open and learning is allowed.

Otherwise, perform the following actions.

    Report that the dendrite is clamped and learning is blocked.

End the conditional block.

The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because disinhibition is a truth table - content times permission - and a few lines make the double-negative logic and its AND-gate behaviour explicit.

# Cortical disinhibition: VIP silences SST, releasing the pyramidal dendrite.
# The net effect is a logical AND of content and permission (Pi et al.,
# Nature 2013; Pfeffer et al., Nat Neurosci 2013).
def disinhibitory_gate(content, vip_firing, base_guard=1.0):
    # vip_firing in {0,1}: 1 lifts the SST guard toward zero
    guard = base_guard * (1.0 - vip_firing)      # inhibition of the inhibitor
    permitted = content * (1.0 - guard)          # content survives only if guard down
    return permitted

PLASTICITY_THRESHOLD = 0.5
print("content  vip  permitted  learns")
for content in (0.2, 0.8):
    for vip in (0, 1):
        p = disinhibitory_gate(content, vip)
        print(f"  {content:.1f}    {vip}    {p:.2f}    {p > PLASTICITY_THRESHOLD}")
# Note: strong content alone (vip=0) does NOT open the gate; permission is required.

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

An interneuron whose target is another interneuron, so that firing it makes a principal cell more active by removing a brake rather than adding a push - a double negative wired into tissue, keyed to arousal and reward, that hands out permission to learn.


CHAPTER 15. VOLUME (NEUROGLIAFORM) INHIBITION (The Unaddressed GABA-Cloud Motif) (The Fog Brake) (COG)

Every other synapse in this manuscript is a letter with an address; this one is a fog.

A single interneuron, dense with a halo of the finest axon branches in the brain, releases gamma-aminobutyric acid not into targeted clefts but into the open extracellular space, so the transmitter drifts as a slow cloud and settles on every process within reach.

There is no chosen recipient; whatever lies inside the fog is dampened, principal cells and interneurons and even other axons alike.

It is the microcircuit-scale echo of the whole brain's broadcast principle: one sender, no address, a slow blanket that quietens a small patch of tissue for a long moment.

Volume names the delivery: transmission through the shared extracellular volume rather than through a private synapse.

Neurogliaform names the sender: the cell whose glia-like tangle of fine processes gives the motif its shape.

Fog names the effect: diffuse, slow, and indifferent to who is underneath it.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

Volume inhibition is a motif in which a neurogliaform cell releases GABA by volume transmission - non-synaptic release into the extracellular space - producing a slow, spatially diffuse inhibition of all neural processes within its dense axonal cloud.

The computation is a slow spatial low-pass filter and a blanket gain-reduction: it does not select a target or a moment but subtracts a slowly rising, slowly falling inhibitory tone across a small volume, damping and smoothing local excitability the way a leaky spatial damper suppresses sharp transients.

Uniquely among GABA circuits it recruits both fast ionotropic GABA-A receptors and slow metabotropic GABA-B receptors from a single cell's release, so a single neurogliaform spike can produce a combined fast-and-slow, long-lasting inhibition of a whole neighbourhood.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

There is one sender node and a diffuse field of receiver nodes, with an unusual edge type.

The sender node is the neurogliaform cell, a GABAergic interneuron with an extraordinarily dense, fine, spherical axonal arbour and many small boutons that mostly do not form classical synapses.

The edges are non-synaptic (volume) inhibitory connections: released GABA diffuses through the extracellular space and acts on whatever GABA-A and GABA-B receptors lie within the cloud, so the receiver set is defined by geometry (everything within roughly a hundred micrometres) rather than by chosen partners.

Receivers include pyramidal cells (on their dendrites), other interneurons, and even presynaptic terminals bearing GABA-B receptors, so the motif can also produce a form of presynaptic inhibition; neurogliaform cells are additionally coupled to one another and to other interneurons by connexin-36 gap junctions, forming an electrically linked sheet.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The sole active role is the neurogliaform cell of the neuron catalogue (with its close relative the ivy cell), both members of the family expressing neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS); its late-spiking, strongly accommodating personality - it responds to a step of current with a delayed, ramping discharge - means it does not fire fast volleys but instead builds a slow output, perfectly matched to laying down a lingering fog rather than a crisp veto.

Its receivers are the general local population - pyramidal cells whose dendrites are quietened, other interneurons whose activity is damped, and afferent terminals whose release is presynaptically reduced - so the cast on the receiving side is simply the neighbourhood, which is the point of a broadcast brake.

The ivy-cell relative is far more numerous and provides a similar slow tonic dampening closer to somata, extending the motif's reach.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

Release is non-synaptic: neurogliaform boutons form appositions rather than true synapses, and the GABA they release reaches a low peak concentration and lingers, which is what makes the response slow.

That low, prolonged GABA transient activates GABA-A receptors to give an unusually slow GABA-A-slow inhibitory postsynaptic current, and, crucially, is one of the very few sources that reliably activates metabotropic GABA-B receptors coupled to G-protein-gated inwardly rectifying potassium (GIRK) channels, adding a slow hyperpolarisation lasting hundreds of milliseconds to over a second.

Gap junctions (connexin-36) couple neurogliaform and ivy cells into a syncytium; the effective weight is diffuse and distance-dependent, falling off across the cloud, and GABA uptake by transporters and astrocytes sets the fog's spatial extent and duration.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One instance is a single neurogliaform cell and the sphere of tissue its axon cloud saturates, a volume roughly 100 to 200 micrometres across, containing on the order of thousands of neural processes, all of which lie under the same released cloud.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

Neurogliaform and ivy cells together are among the most numerous interneuron types in some regions - ivy cells are the single most abundant interneuron in hippocampal area CA1 - so instances number in the hundreds of millions across the forebrain, densely tiling cortex and hippocampus.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• The neocortex, all layers but prominently layer 1, where neurogliaform cells lay a slow blanket over the apical tufts that receive top-down input.

• The hippocampus (areas CA1 and CA3 and dentate), where neurogliaform and the abundant ivy cells provide slow tonic and phasic dampening of principal cells.

• The basolateral amygdala, where neurogliaform cells are a source of slow phasic inhibition shaping fear circuits.

• The thalamus, where slow, non-synaptic GABA targets extrasynaptic delta-subunit GABA-A receptors on relay cells.

• The striatum, where nNOS-expressing interneurons provide diffuse modulation.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Remove the fog and a region keeps its fast, addressed inhibition but loses its slow, space-filling tone: there is nothing left to set the background excitability of a whole patch, to smooth sharp transients across many cells at once, or to deliver the long GABA-B hyperpolarisation that shapes slow oscillations and gates the apical dendrites of layer 1.

Layer 1 in particular would lose its slow control over top-down input, so the cortex would react to feedback without a damping blanket; the region shifts from having both a spotlight brake and a floodlight brake to having only the spotlight.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

The transfer function is a slow, diffuse, subtractive-and-shunting inhibition applied across space: released GABA produces an inhibitory conductance that rises over tens of milliseconds and decays over hundreds of milliseconds to seconds, spread over a volume, so the output is a spatially smoothed, temporally lagged suppression of local activity.

Mathematically it behaves as a leaky spatial damper or diffusion-plus-decay operator: sharp local activity is blurred and reduced, and the slow GABA-B component adds a long tail, unlike the fast, point-targeted subtraction of a basket cell.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

The neurogliaform inhibitory response is the slowest phasic inhibition in the brain: the GABA-A-slow component peaks over tens of milliseconds and the GABA-B-GIRK component lasts hundreds of milliseconds to more than a second, an order of magnitude slower than perisomatic inhibition, so the fog is measured in the timescale of breaths of network state rather than of single spikes.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

At low activity the cells provide a weak tonic dampening; a burst of neurogliaform firing lays a deep, long-lasting blanket that can transiently silence a patch and reset local oscillatory phase; because the cells are gap-junction-coupled they can act as a sheet, and their slow GABA-B action makes them well suited to shaping slow-wave and up/down state transitions.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

Volume inhibition tunes the slow background against which addressed plasticity occurs and can itself be modulated, but its diffuse, unaddressed nature makes it a setter of regional excitability and gain rather than a store of specific associations; it is tagged cognitive for shaping computation (gating layer-1 input, pacing slow rhythms) not for holding memories.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

The classic neurogliaform cell gives the strongest combined GABA-A-slow-plus-GABA-B response; the ivy cell is a more numerous, somewhat faster-onset relative acting nearer somata; regional variants target extrasynaptic delta-subunit GABA-A receptors (thalamus) or layer-1 apical tufts (cortex).

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

Neurogliaform and ivy cells derive substantially from the caudal and medial ganglionic eminences and the preoptic area, migrate into cortex and hippocampus, and elaborate their dense axonal clouds relatively late; the maturation of extracellular GABA handling and of GABA-B-GIRK signalling sets when the slow blanket becomes effective.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

Volume transmission is an ancient and widespread signalling mode - the default for neuromodulators and for the earliest nervous systems - so the neurogliaform cell can be read as a GABA interneuron that retains the primitive broadcast mode of release, a microcircuit fossil of the same principle that governs whole neuromodulatory systems.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Astrocytes are integral: their GABA transporters set how far the cloud spreads and how long it lasts, so the glial envelope literally shapes the fog's dimensions; the extracellular space geometry and its tortuosity are themselves part of the motif's computational fabric.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Altered slow and tonic GABA signalling of the neurogliaform and ivy type is implicated in epilepsy (where tonic inhibition can be protective or, if lost, permissive of seizures), in absence seizures through thalamic extrasynaptic GABA-A receptors, and in the actions of general anaesthetics and neurosteroids that act on the extrasynaptic and slow GABA systems these cells engage.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ Local and top-down excitation onto the neurogliaform cell; electrical coupling from neighbouring neurogliaform and ivy cells through gap junctions.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ A slow, diffuse cloud of GABA acting on GABA-A-slow and GABA-B-GIRK receptors across a local volume, dampening all processes within roughly 100 micrometres, including presynaptic terminals.

• STATE.

◦ Extracellular GABA concentration in the cloud, slow inhibitory conductance, local excitability tone.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Cloud radius roughly 100 to 200 micrometres; GABA-A-slow decay tens of milliseconds; GABA-B-GIRK duration hundreds of milliseconds to over 1 second; connexin-36 coupling.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Onset tens of milliseconds; GABA-A-slow decay tens of milliseconds; GABA-B component hundreds of milliseconds to more than 1 second.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Disordered tonic and slow inhibition in epilepsy and absence seizures (thalamic extrasynaptic GABA-A receptors); the extrasynaptic and slow GABA systems as the target of anaesthetic and neurosteroid actions.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

The konnectome module is named slow_blanket_excitability_damper, a broadcast inhibitory module with no addressed recipients that subscribes to local activity and publishes a slowly rising, slowly decaying suppression applied to every module within a defined spatial neighbourhood.

It publishes not to named channels but to a spatial region, and its output has a long time constant and a leaky-diffusion spatial profile, so downstream modules experience a smoothed, lagged reduction in gain rather than a targeted veto.

The closest artificial-intelligence analogue is a spatial-and-temporal smoothing or regularisation term - a leaky low-pass filter, a blur kernel, or a slowly decaying global-inhibition bias like the divisive term in normalisation - but biology differs by delivering it through unaddressed chemical diffusion with a distinctive dual fast-and-slow receptor response, so a single event both dampens now and biases the neighbourhood for the next second.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to model slow volume inhibition as a leaky spatial damper, in which GABA released at one point spreads to neighbours and decays slowly over time.

Create a list called activity holding the excitation level of each cell in a small patch, indexed by position.

Create a list called inhibition of the same length, all values starting at 0, holding the slow GABA cloud at each position.

Create a number variable called spread with initial value 0.4, controlling how far the cloud diffuses to neighbours.

Create a number variable called decay with initial value 0.9, controlling how slowly the cloud fades each step (close to 1 means slow).

Create a number variable called release with initial value 0.5, the GABA released per unit of neurogliaform activity.

For each time step, perform the following actions.

    Set source to release multiplied by the neurogliaform cell's firing at this step.

    For each position in the patch, perform the following actions.

        Add source to the inhibition at this position.

        Add spread times the average inhibition of the neighbouring positions to the inhibition at this position.

        Multiply the inhibition at this position by decay.

        Set the output activity at this position to activity minus inhibition, not allowing it below zero.

    End the inner loop.

End the outer loop.

The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because the fog is a diffusion-plus-decay process over space and time, and NumPy lets a few lines show a point release blurring into a slow, spreading blanket.

# Neurogliaform volume inhibition as a leaky spatial damper.
# GABA released non-synaptically diffuses and decays slowly, adding a
# long GABA-B tail (Olah et al., Nature 2009; Overstreet-Wadiche &
# McBain, Nat Rev Neurosci 2015 on ivy/neurogliaform slow inhibition).
import numpy as np
N, STEPS = 21, 12
inh = np.zeros(N)                 # slow GABA cloud along a 1-D patch
SPREAD, DECAY = 0.25, 0.9         # diffusion coefficient; slow decay (GABA-B-like)
release = np.zeros(N); release[N // 2] = 1.0   # one neurogliaform cell in the middle

for t in range(STEPS):
    fire = 1.0 if t == 0 else 0.0            # a single burst at t=0
    inh += release * fire * 0.5              # non-synaptic release into the volume
    lap = np.roll(inh, 1) + np.roll(inh, -1) - 2 * inh   # spatial diffusion
    inh = (inh + SPREAD * lap) * DECAY       # spread, then slow decay
    if t in (0, 2, 5, 11):
        print(f"t={t:2d}  peak={inh.max():.3f}  width~{(inh > inh.max()*0.5).sum()}")
# The cloud starts sharp and narrow, then blurs wider and fades slowly:
# a spatial low-pass filter with a long temporal tail.

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

An interneuron with the densest, finest axon cloud in the brain that releases GABA to no one in particular - a slow, unaddressed fog reaching every process within a hundred micrometres, and the one cell that reliably switches on the slow GABA-B brake with a single spike.


PART THREE. THE COMPETITIVE AND NORMALIZING MOTIFS

Every nervous system faces a problem of abundance: at any instant, thousands of candidate signals clamour for a channel that can carry only a few.

The motifs of this part are the brain's answer, and their shared trick is inhibition used not as a brake but as a referee.

Winner-take-all crowns one candidate, k-winners crowns a sparse committee, divisive normalisation taxes every response by the wealth of its neighbours, gain modulation rescales a whole computation by turning one multiplicative knob, and the push-pull motif splits a single signal into two opposed channels so that neither half of the world's range is wasted.

Together they turn raw activity into selection, and selection is the atom of decision.


CHAPTER 16. WINNER-TAKE-ALL (Mutual-Inhibition Competitive Selection Motif) (The One-Survivor Circuit) (COG)

Somewhere in your cortex right now, two half-formed intentions are strangling each other, and by the time you notice, only one is left alive.

That quiet murder is not pathology but design: the winner-take-all motif is the circuit form of choice itself, installed wherever the brain must commit to exactly one option among many.

It works by arranging candidates so that each one's success is every rival's suffocation, a race in which the prize for pulling ahead is the power to slow everyone else.

The result is a machine that converts graded evidence into categorical commitment, the analogue-to-digital converter of thought.

One names the cardinality of the outcome: however many candidates enter, exactly one representation remains active.

Survivor names the mechanism: victory is not awarded but survived into, by outlasting rivals under shared inhibition.

Circuit marks it as a wiring motif, a diagram installable at many addresses, not a cell or a region.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

Winner-take-all (WTA) is a recurrent circuit in which multiple excitatory candidate populations compete through shared or mutual inhibition until the most strongly driven population remains active and all others are silenced.

The computation is a maximum operation followed by thresholding: from a vector of graded input strengths it publishes the identity of the largest element, discarding the rest.

Framework analyses treat WTA as a canonical cortical operation capable of signal restoration, amplification and max-like selection, and models of perceptual decision implement it as attractor dynamics in which two or more excitatory pools wired with slow recurrent excitation and feedback inhibition settle into one of several stable fixed points, each fixed point being a decision.

It is, in the framework volumes' phrase, the circuit form of decision itself.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The graph has two node roles: N candidate nodes (excitatory principal-cell populations, N typically 2 to hundreds) and one shared inhibitory node (a pool of interneurons), plus in some variants direct candidate-to-candidate inhibitory edges.

Each candidate node sends an excitatory edge to itself (recurrent self-excitation, glutamatergic, which sustains its own activity) and an excitatory edge to the shared inhibitory node.

The shared inhibitory node sends an inhibitory edge (gamma-aminobutyric acid, abbreviated GABA, the brain's principal inhibitory transmitter) back to every candidate node, so that any candidate's activity taxes all candidates including itself.

External evidence enters as one excitatory edge per candidate from upstream afferents.

The topology is a star of inhibition superimposed on a set of self-loops: because self-excitation returns to only one node while inhibition returns to all, a candidate that pulls slightly ahead gains more from its own loop than it loses to the shared brake, and the gap amplifies until rivals are extinguished.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

In neocortex the candidate nodes are played by recurrently connected pyramidal cells, chiefly the layer 2/3 intratelencephalic neuron and the layer 5 cell of the neuron catalogue, whose slow N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor kinetics give the race the seconds-long integration time that turns noisy evidence into stable commitment.

The shared inhibitory node is played by the parvalbumin-expressing basket cell of the neuron catalogue, whose fast-spiking, non-adapting personality lets it report the summed excitation of the field within a millisecond or two and clamp somata without lag, which is exactly what a fair referee requires.

Somatostatin-expressing Martinotti cells join in slower contests, and their facilitating, adapting personality means the inhibitory tax grows the longer the race runs, forcing eventual settlement.

In the superior colliculus and basal ganglia versions, medium spiny neurons and collicular premotor cells play the candidates, and the basal ganglia implement the inhibitory referee as tonic GABAergic output from the substantia nigra pars reticulata that only the winner's channel can lift.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

Candidate self-excitation uses glutamate on alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors (decay about 2 milliseconds) and NMDA receptors (decay about 100 milliseconds), the NMDA component supplying the slow reverberation that stabilises the winner.

Excitation of the referee lands on parvalbumin basket cell dendrites through fast AMPA synapses with high release probability and depressing short-term plasticity.

The referee's GABAergic output targets candidate somata and proximal dendrites through GABA-A receptors (decay 5 to 10 milliseconds), placed where they can veto spiking rather than merely attenuate dendrites.

Parvalbumin interneurons are additionally coupled to each other by gap junctions built from connexin 36, which synchronise the referee pool so the tax is applied evenly.

Connection probability between nearby layer 2/3 pyramidal cells and basket cells runs 40 to 60 percent in each direction in paired recordings, far denser than pyramidal-to-pyramidal probability of roughly 5 to 10 percent, which is why the inhibitory star is reliable.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

A minimal cortical instance is two candidate assemblies of 50 to 200 pyramidal cells each plus 20 to 60 shared basket cells, spanning 100 to 300 micrometres of cortex, roughly the footprint of a minicolumn cluster.

Large instances, such as the collicular motor map choosing one saccade target, span millimetres and hundreds of candidate loci.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

Uncountable in the strict sense because instances overlap and share interneurons, but on the order of 10 million to 100 million distinguishable competitive neighbourhoods across the neocortex alone, low confidence, plus discrete high-stakes instances in the colliculus, basal ganglia and amygdala.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• Dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, where competing evidence streams race to become the reported percept or the chosen plan.

• Lateral intraparietal area and frontal eye fields, where candidate saccade targets compete and the attractor's settling time is read out as reaction time.

• Superior colliculus, whose motor map runs a spatial winner-take-all so that the eyes can point at only one place at a time.

• Basal ganglia (striatum through substantia nigra pars reticulata), where action channels compete by disinhibition and the winner alone is released.

• Primary sensory cortices, where local winner-take-all sharpens orientation and feature selectivity by max-like selection.

• Amygdala and hypothalamic behavioural-state circuits, where mutually inhibitory populations force one behavioural mode (freeze versus flee, feed versus flee) to own the animal at a time.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Strip this motif from a region and graded ambivalence replaces commitment: prefrontal cortex would report weighted blends of incompatible percepts, the colliculus would drive the eyes toward the average of two targets rather than either one, and the basal ganglia would release fragments of several actions at once.

Every hosting region owes to this motif its ability to mean one thing at a time.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

The transfer function is a hysteretic max operation: for input vector x, the steady-state output approximates a one-hot vector selecting argmax(x), with the losing channels driven to near zero.

Settling time depends on the evidence gap, roughly 100 to 300 milliseconds for large differences and up to 1 to 2 seconds for near ties, matching the reaction-time distributions of two-alternative choice tasks.

Below a critical recurrent gain the circuit is a graded amplifier; above it, bistability appears and the winner persists even after inputs are withdrawn, which is working memory by another name.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

Ramping firing in candidate populations at 10 to 50 hertz rising over hundreds of milliseconds, a sharp divergence point at commitment, then sustained winner activity and suppressed losers, often riding a gamma rhythm (30 to 80 hertz) contributed by the basket-cell referee.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

Three regimes: subcritical (graded, reversible competition), attractor (categorical choice with hysteresis) and oscillatory near-tie states in which candidates alternate, seen behaviourally as perceptual rivalry alternating every 1 to 10 seconds.

Neuromodulators move the circuit between regimes by scaling recurrent gain, so the same wiring is a soft comparator when relaxed and a hard latch when aroused.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

Hebbian long-term potentiation on the winner's input synapses and heterosynaptic depression on losers implement learned biases, which is why practised choices settle faster.

Inhibitory plasticity onto candidates rebalances the race, and modelling shows paired excitatory and inhibitory plasticity is required to keep winner-take-all dynamics stable rather than letting one habitual winner annex the circuit.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

Hard WTA (one survivor), the k-winners softening of Chapter 17, hysteretic WTA (attractor working memory), spatial WTA on continuous maps (the collicular and ring-attractor form) and disinhibitory WTA (basal ganglia style, where the resting state is all-suppressed and winning means release).

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

The excitatory scaffold wires first; parvalbumin interneurons mature late, their fast-spiking phenotype and perineuronal nets consolidating through childhood, so the sharpness of competition is one of the last cortical parameters to be set, into adolescence.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

Ancient beyond the vertebrates: mutually inhibitory command neurons choose between escape swims in molluscs, and lateral-inhibitory selection appears in the arthropod optic lobe, so the one-survivor diagram predates the cortex by several hundred million years and was re-installed there.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Fast-spiking basket cells are the most metabolically expensive neurons per gram in the circuit, dense in mitochondria and wrapped in perineuronal nets that buffer ions and protect against oxidative stress; astrocytes clear the glutamate surges of the race and supply lactate to the sprinting referee.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

When the referee weakens, as in the parvalbumin-interneuron deficits documented in schizophrenia, competition fails to resolve: percepts and thoughts blend rather than exclude, a plausible circuit account of thought disorder and of the gamma-band abnormalities seen in patients.

Overly strong or sticky competition contributes to perseveration after prefrontal damage and to the action-selection freezing of Parkinson disease, where no channel can win release from pathologically synchronised basal ganglia inhibition.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ Per-candidate evidence currents, typically 0 to 500 picoamperes equivalent drive per population, from sensory or associative afferents.

◦ Neuromodulatory gain signals (dopamine, noradrenaline, acetylcholine) scaling recurrent strength by roughly 10 to 50 percent.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ A near one-hot activity vector: winner population at 20 to 60 hertz, losers below 2 hertz.

◦ Commitment time, 100 milliseconds to 2 seconds, implicitly published as output latency.

• STATE.

◦ Per-candidate firing rates; referee pool rate; attractor occupancy (which basin, if any).

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Recurrent excitatory gain 0.8 to 1.5 (dimensionless loop gain); inhibitory coupling covering all N candidates; spiking threshold near minus 40 millivolts.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ AMPA 2 milliseconds; GABA-A 5 to 10 milliseconds; NMDA 100 milliseconds; population settling 100 to 2,000 milliseconds.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Unresolved competition in schizophrenia (parvalbumin deficit); perseverative locking in prefrontal injury; selection paralysis in Parkinson disease.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

Propose the module winner_take_all_selector, subscribing to a candidate-evidence vector topic and to a neuromodulatory gain topic, and publishing a selected-option identifier plus a confidence value derived from settling time.

The closest artificial intelligence analogue is argmax with hysteresis, or a hard attention gate; the biological motif differs in that selection is a temporal process whose duration encodes difficulty, and in that the same module doubles as working memory when its loop gain crosses the attractor threshold, a two-for-one that argmax does not offer.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to run a race between two mutually inhibiting candidate populations until one winner silences the other.
Create a number variable called rate one with initial value 0.1.
Create a number variable called rate two with initial value 0.1.
Create a number variable called evidence one with initial value 1.0.
Create a number variable called evidence two with initial value 0.9.
Create a number variable called self excitation with initial value 1.2.
Create a number variable called mutual inhibition with initial value 1.5.
Repeat the following actions two hundred times.
    Calculate the product of self excitation and rate one, then add evidence one, then subtract the product of mutual inhibition and rate two.
    If the result is less than 0 is true, then set the result to 0.
    End the conditional block.
    Move rate one ten percent of the way toward the result.
    Calculate the product of self excitation and rate two, then add evidence two, then subtract the product of mutual inhibition and rate one.
    If the result is less than 0 is true, then set the result to 0.
    End the conditional block.
    Move rate two ten percent of the way toward the result.
End the repetition block.
If rate one is greater than rate two is true, then display that candidate one is the winner.
Otherwise, display that candidate two is the winner.
End the conditional block.
The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because the whole argument is a short iterated map whose printout shows a near tie diverging into one survivor, and Python states the map in a dozen honest lines.

# Winner-take-all by mutual inhibition: a 10 percent evidence edge
# becomes total victory (competitive selection framework: Mysore and
# Kothari, eLife 2020; attractor decision models: Wang, Neuron 2002).
import numpy as np

W_SELF, W_INH, DT = 1.2, 1.5, 0.1        # loop gain, cross-inhibition, step
evidence = np.array([1.0, 0.9])          # candidate 1 leads by 10 percent
rate = np.array([0.1, 0.1])              # both candidates start equal

for step in range(200):
    drive = W_SELF * rate + evidence - W_INH * rate[::-1]
    rate += DT * (np.maximum(drive, 0.0) - rate)   # rectified relaxation
    if step % 40 == 0:
        print(f"step {step:3d}  rates = {rate.round(3)}")

print(f"final rates = {rate.round(3)}")
print("winner:", "candidate 1" if rate[0] > rate[1] else "candidate 2")
# The loser is driven to zero: graded evidence became a categorical choice.

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

A star of shared inhibition wrapped around self-exciting candidates, ramping activity that suddenly forks into one sustained survivor and silenced rivals, and a settling time that lengthens as the options approach a tie: no other motif turns a vector into a verdict.


CHAPTER 17. SOFT WINNER-TAKE-ALL AND SPARSE CODING (k-Winners Competitive Thinning Motif) (The Few-Survivors Circuit) (COG)

The dentate gyrus, gatekeeper of memory, keeps 95 to 98 percent of its cells silent at any moment, and that silence is the point.

Where the hard winner-take-all of Chapter 16 crowns one survivor, this gentler cousin crowns a small committee: the k most strongly driven cells fire, and everyone else is held under a blanket of global inhibition.

The prize is a sparse code, in which each experience is written by a tiny, nearly non-overlapping subset of cells, so that similar inputs are pushed apart into distinct engrams rather than smeared together.

It is the circuit that lets you keep yesterday's parking spot and today's from merging into one useless average.

Few names the outcome: not one winner but a small fraction, typically 1 to 5 percent of the population.

Survivors names the mechanism, shared with Chapter 16: those who fire are those who outlast a rising tide of inhibition.

Circuit marks it as a wiring motif installed at several addresses, not a cell or a region.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

Soft winner-take-all, or k-winners-take-all, is a competitive circuit in which global feedback inhibition scales with total population activity and permits only the k most strongly driven principal cells to remain above threshold.

The computation is sparsification with pattern separation: it maps a dense, overlapping input vector to a sparse output vector in a much larger cell population, reducing the overlap between similar inputs (orthogonalisation) so that downstream associative memories store them without interference.

Experimental estimates put the active fraction of dentate gyrus granule cells in a given context at roughly 2 to 5 percent, and cerebellar granule cells are comparably sparse, which is the biological signature of this motif at work.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

Node roles: a large expansion population of principal cells (the coding field), a small pool of global inhibitory interneurons (the thermostat), and an input population whose fibres diverge onto the coding field.

Input axons make divergent excitatory (glutamatergic) edges onto many principal cells and also excitatory edges directly onto the interneurons (feedforward inhibition).

Every principal cell sends an excitatory edge to the interneuron pool, and the interneuron pool sends inhibitory GABAergic edges back onto essentially all principal cells (feedback inhibition), closing a negative-feedback loop whose gain sets k.

Unlike Chapter 16, principal cells have little or no recurrent self-excitation, so there is no attractor latching: the committee is re-elected afresh with each input.

The topology is expansion plus a single global brake: many-to-few convergence onto the interneurons, few-to-all divergence back.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The coding field in the hippocampal instance is the dentate granule cell of the neuron catalogue, whose reluctant, hyperpolarised, low-excitability personality (resting near minus 85 millivolts, sparse firing below 1 hertz) means only cells receiving a conspiracy of coincident inputs can clear threshold at all, a personality that pre-sparsifies before inhibition even acts.

The thermostat is played by parvalbumin basket cells, whose fast-spiking personality makes the brake proportional and prompt, and by somatostatin-expressing hilar cells (HIPP cells), whose adapting, dendrite-targeting personality tightens sparsity during sustained input and is required for contextual discrimination.

In the cerebellar instance the coding field is the cerebellar granule cell, the most numerous neuron in the brain, with Golgi cells as the thermostat, their slow-adapting inhibition regulating the sparse mossy-fibre recode.

Hilar mossy cells add a seasoning of feedback excitation whose own sparse, adaptive firing redistributes drive across the granule field.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

Input synapses (entorhinal perforant path onto granule dendrites; mossy fibres onto cerebellar granule claws) are glutamatergic onto alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) and N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors, individually weak so that firing requires coincidence.

Feedback inhibition uses gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-A synapses on somata and proximal dendrites (basket cells) and on distal dendrites (HIPP and Golgi cells), the dendritic component controlling sparsity by capping dendritic amplification.

Granule cells also receive tonic GABA current through extrasynaptic delta-subunit GABA-A receptors, a standing tax that further raises the entry fee.

Basket cells are gap-junction coupled through connexin 36, and perforant-path synapses show Hebbian long-term potentiation gated by theta rhythm.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

The human dentate instance holds roughly 15 million granule cells per hemisphere against on the order of only tens of thousands of inhibitory interneurons, a ratio that makes the global brake astonishingly cheap; the cerebellar instance is the largest circuit in the brain, roughly 50 billion granule cells.

A functional neighbourhood, one interneuron's sphere of influence, spans 300 to 500 micrometres and contains tens of thousands of granule cells.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

Two flagship installations (dentate gyrus and cerebellar granule layer), plus sparse-coding neighbourhoods in the piriform cortex, the mushroom-body analogue logic of which is conserved from insects, and softer k-winners operation throughout the neocortical superficial layers.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• Dentate gyrus of the hippocampal formation, where it performs pattern separation so that similar episodes are stored as distinct memories.

• Cerebellar granule cell layer, where it recodes mossy-fibre input into a sparse, high-dimensional format that makes Purkinje cell learning linearly easy.

• Piriform (olfactory) cortex, where odours are written as sparse distributed ensembles readable against a combinatorial background.

• Neocortical layer 2/3, where soft competition keeps population sparseness high (a few percent strongly active) and codes energy-efficient.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Without this motif the dentate gyrus becomes a photocopier instead of a filing clerk: similar experiences overwrite each other, and behaviourally the animal loses contextual discrimination, confusing the dangerous chamber with the safe one.

The cerebellum without its sparse recode would face an intractable learning problem, and the piriform cortex would lose the combinatorial capacity that lets a few million cells encode trillions of odour mixtures.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

The transfer function is a competitive threshold: each output approximates the input drive minus a global inhibition term proportional to total population activity, rectified at zero, with the loop gain adjusting until roughly k cells survive.

Quantitatively, dentate output sparseness is 2 to 5 percent active per context against input (entorhinal) activity fractions several-fold denser, and overlap between the representations of two similar environments falls below the overlap of their inputs, the defining signature of separation.

The expansion (about 4 to 5 entorhinal-to-granule cell number ratio in humans, far higher in cerebellum) plus sparsening is the biological form of dimensionality expansion followed by thresholding.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

Granule cells fire in brief, reliable bursts phase-locked to the theta rhythm (4 to 8 hertz) during exploration, with gamma-paced inhibition slicing each theta cycle into competitive rounds; most cells stay silent for minutes to hours.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:
