Estimates and models put a functional chain at tens to a few hundred principal neurons per pool and tens to hundreds of pools in series, so one chain encoding a behaviour of about a second may involve on the order of tens of thousands of neurons; songbird HVC contains roughly 40,000 of the relevant projection neurons, each firing at one point in the roughly one-second song, tiling the whole duration.

Each pool's volley lasts a few milliseconds, and successive pools are spaced a few milliseconds apart, so a chain of a few hundred pools clocks out a behaviour lasting hundreds of milliseconds to seconds.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

There is no census; the hypothesis is that learned motor and cognitive sequences are each carried by one or more embedded chains, so the count would scale with the number of skilled sequences an animal knows.

In the songbird there is a well-defined chain (or family of chains) per song; in humans the proposal is that speech, music and skilled serial action are each supported by such chains in premotor and motor cortex and their loops, though the anatomical proof achieved in birds has not yet been matched in mammals.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• The avian premotor nucleus HVC (the songbird analogue of premotor cortex), the proven installation, clocking the syllable sequence of learned song.

• The premotor and supplementary motor cortex, the proposed human installation for sequencing speech articulation and skilled serial movements such as typing and playing an instrument.

• The primary motor cortex and its loops with the basal ganglia and cerebellum, where learned action sequences are assembled and timed.

• The hippocampus, where precisely-ordered sequences of place-cell firing (replay and theta sequences) may be carried by synfire-like feedforward structure - a proposed cognitive installation for episodic sequence.

• The prefrontal cortex, a candidate substrate for chains that clock out learned sequences of thought and planned action.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Delete this motif from the songbird HVC and the bird loses its song's sequence: the individual syllables might still be producible, but their precise ordering and timing - the melody - is gone, because there is no longer anything to clock them out.

A region that hosts a synfire chain gains the ability to produce and store a precisely-timed, reliably-repeatable sequence, which is what turns a set of possible actions into an ordered skill; strip it out and the region could still generate elements but not their exact serial order in time.

For the proposed human installations, the up-layer consequence would be the loss of fluent, correctly-sequenced speech and skilled serial action - the difference between knowing the notes and being able to play the tune.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

The transform is: one trigger in, a precisely-timed ordered sequence of pool activations out - a delta pulse expanded into a stereotyped spatiotemporal barcode.

The key quantitative properties are temporal precision (spike timing jitter held to about 1 to a few milliseconds across the whole chain, because convergence averages out noise) and stability (the volley converges to a fixed pulse-packet width and firing fraction rather than dying out or exploding, provided the pool size and synaptic weight exceed critical values).

There is a threshold effect: a pool must contain enough co-firing cells (roughly tens, depending on synaptic strength) for the volley to ignite the next pool; below that critical number the packet decays and the sequence stalls - and the same margin above the critical number is exactly what buys dropout tolerance.

The mathematical description is stable propagation of a synchronous pulse packet along a feedforward network, an attractor in the space of packet width and spike count.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

Millisecond-precise, stereotyped, repeatable timing: the same sequence unrolls the same way trial after trial, with each pool firing at its fixed latency from the trigger.

The unmistakable signature is a wave of synchronous volleys marching at fixed inter-pool delays with very low jitter, tiling a behaviour of hundreds of milliseconds to seconds - the sparse, one-burst-per-cell, time-locked firing seen in HVC is the textbook fingerprint.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

Three regimes set by pool size and synaptic weight: propagation (a stable travelling packet), decay (the packet shrinks and dies, sequence aborts), and saturation or synchronous explosion (the volley recruits too many cells and the whole network fires at once, a pathological runaway resembling a seizure).

Healthy chains sit in the propagation regime, held there by the inhibitory scaffold; too little inhibition tips toward explosion, too little excitation toward decay.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

This is a learning motif, and its learning is its point: synfire chains are thought to self-organise from initially unstructured recurrent networks through spike-timing-dependent plasticity, which selectively strengthens forward links whenever one group reliably fires just before another, gradually carving a stable feedforward sequence out of noise.

In the songbird the chain is built during a sensorimotor learning period under the guidance of auditory feedback and basal-ganglia-mediated reinforcement (the teaching signal), and once formed the chain is stable and replayed to produce the crystallised song - the same logic proposed for how humans consolidate a skilled sequence with practice.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

By topology: simple linear chains (one-shot sequence), looped chains (repeating sequence, as in a repeated song motif), and branching or diverging chains (sequences that fork).

By sharing: isolated chains versus overlapping chains embedded in one network that share neurons, allowing a limited set of cells to encode many sequences (with a capacity limit and a risk of cross-talk if chains overlap too much).

A related variant replaces pure synchrony-propagation with sequences carried by spatiotemporal patterns of inhibition, a inhibition-based cousin proposed for HVC that achieves the same ordered timing by a different means.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

In the songbird the chain assembles during the juvenile learning phase, when HVC connectivity is sculpted by practice and feedback into the mature sequence; before learning the connectivity is unstructured, and the chain is literally grown by the plasticity rule.

The general developmental principle is that recurrent excitatory networks with STDP and adequate inhibition will, given repeated driven sequences, condense feedforward chains - the assembly is experience-dependent, not purely genetic.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

Precisely-timed sequence generation is an old need - courtship songs, escape sequences, feeding movements - and feedforward synchrony-propagating architecture is a natural and possibly convergent solution, well documented in the avian song system and proposed as a general cortical strategy.

The songbird and mammalian premotor systems are not homologous in detail, so the synfire chain may be a case of the same computational motif independently arrived at wherever precise learned sequences are needed - old logic, re-derived.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Fast-spiking parvalbumin interneurons are the obligatory partners that keep the chain sharp and safe, as above; astrocytes clear glutamate fast enough to preserve the millisecond precision the chain depends on and buffer the potassium of the volleys; and neuromodulatory systems (dopamine for reinforcement, acetylcholine for gating plasticity) supervise the learning that builds and maintains the chain.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Because the chain is a sequence-timing motif, its failures are disorders of sequence and timing: stuttering and apraxia of speech can be read as failures to clock out the articulatory sequence; dysfluent or disordered skilled action follows premotor damage.

The saturation regime - an excitatory chain losing its inhibitory restraint and firing as one synchronous explosion - is a microcircuit picture of the transition to epileptic hypersynchrony; and disorders of the parvalbumin interneuron scaffold (implicated in schizophrenia) would blur the timing on which any such chain depends.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ A trigger/start command onto the first pool (a single event, not a rhythm); a teaching/reinforcement signal during learning (dopaminergic, low-rate); neuromodulatory gating of plasticity.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ An ordered sequence of pool activations at fixed latencies - the timed command stream driving downstream motor or cognitive targets.

• STATE.

◦ Current position of the travelling packet along the chain; packet width and spike count; the learned synaptic weights that define the chain.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Pool size (must exceed a critical number, roughly tens of cells, to propagate); feedforward synaptic weight; inhibitory gain; number of pools (sets sequence duration); inter-pool delay (a few milliseconds).

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Per-pool volley a few milliseconds; inter-pool delay 3 to 10 milliseconds; total sequence hundreds of milliseconds to seconds; STDP learning window about 20 milliseconds; consolidation over the days to weeks of practice.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Sub-critical pool size or weak links cause packet decay and the sequence stalls (a substrate for stuttering and apraxia); loss of inhibition causes synchronous explosion (a substrate for seizure and for the hypersynchrony seen when parvalbumin control fails).

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

Propose the module name synchronous_sequence_clocker. It would subscribe to a start trigger and a reinforcement signal, and publish an ordered stream of timestamped activations that downstream modules use as a learned script and clock; internally it would hold a bank of feedforward pools with plastic links tuned by a spike-timing rule. The closest artificial-intelligence analogues are the hidden state of a recurrent neural network unrolled in time and the positional-timing structure a transformer imposes on a sequence - the biological chain differs by carrying order in the physical travelling wave of synchrony rather than in a learned position embedding, by being explicitly dropout-tolerant through convergent redundancy, and by self-organising its sequence from unstructured connectivity through local timing-dependent plasticity rather than global gradient descent.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to propagate a synchronous packet of spikes from pool to pool along a feedforward chain, firing each pool only when enough of the previous pool fired, and to keep marching even when some cells drop out.

Create a number variable called number of pools with initial value 10.

Create a number variable called cells per pool with initial value 100.

Create a number variable called ignition threshold with initial value 30.

Create a number variable called dropout fraction with initial value 0.2.

Create a list variable called active count with one entry per pool, each initial value 0.

Set the active count of pool one to the full cells per pool, representing the trigger volley.

Create a number variable called current pool with initial value 1.

Repeat the following actions while current pool is less than number of pools.

    Create a number variable called survivors with initial value 0.

    For each cell that fired in the current pool, perform the following actions.

        Draw a random number between 0 and 1.

        If the random number is greater than dropout fraction is true, then perform the following actions.

            Add 1 to survivors.

        End the conditional block.

    End the loop over cells.

    Check if survivors is greater than or equal to ignition threshold.

    If survivors is greater than or equal to ignition threshold is true, then perform the following actions.

        Set the active count of the next pool to the full cells per pool, representing a fresh synchronous volley.

    Otherwise, perform the following actions.

        Set the active count of the next pool to 0, meaning the packet has died and the sequence stalls.

        Stop the loop early.

    End the conditional block.

    Add 1 to current pool.

End the loop over pools.

Display the active count of every pool to the console, showing how far the wave travelled.

The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because the essential claim - that a synchronous packet either propagates cleanly or dies at a critical pool size, and tolerates dropout as long as it stays above threshold - is a few lines of counting and randomness, and Python shows the threshold and the robustness with no ceremony.

# Synfire-chain propagation of a synchronous pulse packet with dropout tolerance.
# A pool ignites the next only if enough of its cells survive to co-fire; convergent
# redundancy is what lets the volley keep its timing despite lost spikes.
# (Abeles, Corticonics, 1991; Diesmann, Gewaltig & Aertsen, Nature 1999; HVC: Long,
#  Jin & Fee, Nature 2010.)
import random

NUM_POOLS       = 12     # links in the chain
CELLS_PER_POOL  = 100    # neurons per pool
IGNITION        = 30     # co-firing cells needed to light the next pool (critical number)
DROPOUT         = 0.20   # fraction of spikes randomly lost between pools (noise/failure)

def propagate(dropout):
    active = [CELLS_PER_POOL]          # pool 0 gets the full trigger volley
    for _ in range(NUM_POOLS - 1):
        survivors = sum(1 for _ in range(active[-1]) if random.random() > dropout)
        if survivors >= IGNITION:
            active.append(CELLS_PER_POOL)   # clean, re-synchronised volley
        else:
            active.append(0)                # packet decays: sequence stalls
            break
    return active

random.seed(1)
for d in (0.0, 0.20, 0.60, 0.75):
    trace = propagate(d)
    reached = sum(1 for a in trace if a > 0)
    print(f"dropout {d:>4}:  reached {reached:2d}/{NUM_POOLS} pools  ->  {trace}")

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

Pools of excitatory cells wired in a one-way series so that a single synchronous volley marches pool to pool at fixed millisecond delays, its timing sharpened and its losses covered by convergent redundancy - a bucket-brigade of spikes that clocks out a learned sequence, proven in the singing of birds and proposed for the speaking and skilled acting of humans.


PART FIVE. THE MEMORY AND ATTRACTOR MOTIFS

Every motif so far has shaped a signal while the signal was present; the four motifs of this part do something stranger, for they keep going after the input stops.

Their shared trick is recurrence: excitation fed back into the very population that produced it, tuned so that certain patterns of activity become self-sustaining.

Mathematicians call such a self-sustaining pattern an attractor, a state the system falls into and holds, and the nervous system builds attractors in at least three geometries - the isolated point, the continuous line, and the closed ring.

Between them these circuits give the brain its memory of the recent past, its ability to hold a thought, its running totals, and its inner compass.

They are also the motifs that most directly anticipate the recurrent networks of artificial intelligence, which is why every konnectome note in this part points at a machine that already half-exists.


CHAPTER 29. THE AUTOASSOCIATIVE ATTRACTOR NETWORK (Recurrent Pattern-Completing Excitatory Pool) (The Cue-To-Memory Circuit) (COG)

Hum three notes of a song and the whole chorus arrives unbidden; smell one spice and a kitchen from childhood assembles itself around you.

That everyday miracle is pattern completion, and the circuit that performs it is a pool of principal cells wired back onto themselves through modifiable synapses, so that any fragment of a stored pattern re-excites the rest.

Hippocampal area CA3, whose pyramidal cells send recurrent collaterals to one another, is the anatomically proven case, predicted by theory in the 1970s and confirmed synapse by synapse since.

It is the closest thing biology has to an addressable memory in which the address and the content are the same thing.

Cue names the fragment that starts recall.

To names the direction of the computation, from part to whole.

Memory names the stored pattern that is returned.

Circuit marks it as a wiring motif installed in tissue, not a single cell.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

The autoassociative attractor network is a population of excitatory principal cells in which each cell synapses, through modifiable connections, onto many other cells of the same population, with feedback inhibition holding the total activity in bounds.

Learning strengthens the connections among cells that fire together, so each stored experience becomes a cell assembly whose members excite one another.

The computation is pattern completion: present a partial or noisy version of a stored pattern and the recurrent excitation drives the population state to the nearest stored attractor, returning the whole memory.

Formally it computes a nearest-neighbour lookup over stored binary or graded patterns, the operation John Hopfield formalised in 1982 and David Marr assigned to CA3 in 1971.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The nodes are one large pool of excitatory principal cells, a smaller pool of feedback inhibitory interneurons, and two external input lines.

Every principal cell sends excitatory (glutamatergic) recurrent collaterals onto the dendrites of a sparse, spatially uniform random sample of other principal cells, with connection probability near 1 percent in rodent CA3, forming the dense-in-effect but sparse-in-anatomy recurrent web.

Principal cells excite the inhibitory interneurons, which return inhibition (gamma-aminobutyric acid, GABA) onto the somata and dendrites of the principal pool, a negative feedback loop that normalises total activity.

One external excitatory line, the detonator input (in CA3 the mossy fibres from dentate granule cells), imposes new patterns during storage; a second external excitatory line, the cue input (in CA3 the direct perforant path from entorhinal cortex), delivers fragments during recall.

The output edge is the principal cells' projection out of the pool (in CA3, the Schaffer collaterals to CA1), excitatory.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The principal role is played by the CA3 pyramidal cell of the neuron catalogue, a burst-capable cell whose tendency to fire complexes of two to five spikes makes each recall event a strong, synapse-driving volley rather than a whisper.

Its long apical dendrite receives the perforant-path cue distally and the recurrent collaterals proximally, so the cell literally stacks the question below the answer.

The feedback brake is the parvalbumin-expressing basket cell of the neuron catalogue, whose fast-spiking, non-adapting personality lets it track the excitatory pool cycle by cycle and clamp total activity within a single gamma period.

The cholecystokinin basket cell adds a slower, mood-sensitive inhibition, and the dentate granule cell of the neuron catalogue supplies the sparse detonator input whose giant mossy terminals can fire a CA3 cell almost single-handedly, which is exactly what a teacher input must do.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

The recurrent collateral synapses are glutamatergic, acting on alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors for fast drive and N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors for coincidence detection, placed on proximal and mid-apical dendrites in stratum radiatum.

Unitary recurrent connections are weak and economical, typically one or two synaptic contacts, so recall must be a population vote, not a relay.

The mossy fibre teaching synapse is a giant multi-release-site bouton on the most proximal dendrite, showing enormous frequency facilitation.

Basket cell synapses deliver GABA onto perisomatic receptors of the A type, and the recurrent synapses obey Hebbian NMDA-receptor-dependent long-term potentiation and depression, the storage rule itself.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

A functional instance is the whole recurrent pool of one hippocampus: roughly 0.3 million CA3 pyramidal cells per side in the rat and roughly 2.7 million per side in the human, each receiving on the order of 12,000 recurrent synapses from perhaps 1 percent of the population.

Physical extent is the full septotemporal length of CA3, several centimetres of curved tissue in the human, because the recurrent collaterals run remarkably far along the axis.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

Two canonical instances, left and right CA3, with partial replicas wherever dense recurrent excitation with plastic synapses occurs: recurrent circuits of the neocortex (especially in layers 2 and 3 of association and olfactory areas), the lateral amygdala for fear memories, and area CA2 with its own recurrent connections.

Confidence is high for CA3 and piriform cortex, moderate for the neocortical and amygdalar replicas.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• Hippocampal area CA3, both hemispheres - the proven autoassociator, storing episodic patterns and completing them from cues.

• Hippocampal area CA2 - a smaller recurrent pool specialised for social memory.

• Piriform (olfactory) cortex - completes odour objects from partial receptor patterns, the oldest cortical autoassociator.

• Lateral and basal amygdala - recurrent excitation binds conditioned stimulus fragments to stored threat patterns.

• Association neocortex, layers 2 and 3 - weaker, distributed autoassociation supporting semantic memory retrieval.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Without this motif the hippocampus would still register experience but could never be reminded: a partial cue would evoke only a partial response, and recollection as humans know it - the whole scene returning from a fragment - would not exist.

Piriform cortex would smell mixtures without recognising odours, and the amygdala would need the entire original threat, not a hint of it, to raise the alarm.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

Input is a cue vector over the principal cells; output, after a few tens of milliseconds of recurrent settling, is the stored pattern vector nearest to that cue.

The transfer function is iterated threshold-linear feedback with divisive-plus-subtractive inhibitory normalisation, converging to a fixed point.

Real numbers: rodent CA3 recall completes within roughly one theta cycle (125 to 250 milliseconds) and often within one to two gamma cycles (10 to 30 milliseconds), and behavioural experiments show mice recalling whole contexts from degraded cues at above 70 percent fidelity when NMDA receptors in CA3 are intact and near chance when they are deleted.

Theoretical capacity is about 0.14 patterns per recurrent synapse per cell in the classic Hopfield limit, giving tens of thousands of separable patterns for CA3-scale connectivity, a number to treat as an order-of-magnitude guide, not a measurement.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

Settling into an attractor takes one to a few gamma cycles; recall events ride the theta rhythm (4 to 8 cycles per second) during exploration and are replayed in compressed form inside sharp-wave ripples (110 to 200 cycles per second) during rest and sleep.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

Three regimes: a storage regime, when dentate detonator input dominates and plasticity is enabled; a recall regime, when perforant-path cues dominate and the recurrent web settles patterns; and a replay regime, when the network free-runs stored sequences during sharp-wave ripples.

Acetylcholine biases the network toward storage by suppressing recurrent transmission, and low acetylcholine during slow-wave sleep releases the web for replay.

The pathological regime is runaway recurrence: CA3 is the most seizure-prone tissue in the brain precisely because of this wiring.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

Learning is the motif: NMDA-receptor-dependent Hebbian potentiation of the recurrent collateral synapses writes each pattern, spike-timing rules operating within tens of milliseconds set direction of change, and homeostatic scaling plus inhibitory plasticity keep the pool below the seizure line.

Mossy fibre synapses use a different, NMDA-independent presynaptic potentiation, fitting their teaching role.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

CA3 itself is graded: proximal CA3 (near the dentate) has sparser recurrence and behaves more like a pattern separator, while distal CA3 has richer recurrence and stronger completion.

The piriform variant lacks a detonator input and stores odours directly from bulb input; the amygdalar variant couples its attractors to hard-wired defensive outputs.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

CA3 pyramidal cells are born in the ventricular zone, migrate into the curving hippocampal plate during mid-gestation in the human, and extend recurrent collaterals that are initially exuberant and then pruned; NMDA-receptor-dependent refinement during the first postnatal years tunes the web.

Adult neurogenesis in the neighbouring dentate keeps supplying new teacher cells throughout life.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

Autoassociative recurrence appears wherever a cortex-like sheet exists: the reptilian medial cortex, homologue of the hippocampus, already shows recurrent excitation, and the olfactory autoassociator is likely the ancestral installation, with the hippocampal one a specialisation for space and episode.

The mathematics was rediscovered by evolution long before Hopfield wrote it down.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Astrocytes in stratum radiatum clear the glutamate flood of every recall volley through excitatory amino acid transporters, and their poor performance under ischaemia is one reason CA3 and its neighbour CA1 die early in oxygen starvation.

Microglia prune recurrent synapses using complement tags, and the dense local capillary bed answers the high metabolic bill of recurrent firing.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Temporal lobe epilepsy is the motif's signature disease: mossy fibre sprouting adds pathological recurrent excitation and the autoassociator becomes a seizure generator.

In Alzheimer's disease the perforant-path cue line degenerates early, so patterns remain stored but cannot be addressed, matching the clinical picture of cueing failure.

Ketamine and other NMDA blockers impair new storage while sparing old recall, and hippocampal sclerosis deletes the pool outright.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ Cue vectors from entorhinal cortex layer 2 via the perforant path, roughly 4,000 synapses per CA3 cell.

◦ Teaching patterns from dentate granule cells via mossy fibres, roughly 50 giant boutons per CA3 cell.

◦ Cholinergic storage-versus-recall bias from the medial septum.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ Completed pattern vectors to CA1 via Schaffer collaterals, at 10 to 30 millisecond settling latency.

◦ Compressed replay sequences during sharp-wave ripples at 110 to 200 cycles per second.

• STATE.

◦ The current activity vector over roughly 2.7 million principal cells per human hemisphere, sparseness 2 to 5 percent active.

◦ The recurrent weight matrix, roughly 12,000 modifiable synapses per cell.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Recurrent connection probability near 1 percent; unitary contacts one to two; storage capacity on the order of 0.14 patterns per synapse per cell.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ AMPA decay 2 milliseconds; NMDA decay 50 to 150 milliseconds; settling 10 to 30 milliseconds; theta cycle 125 to 250 milliseconds; synaptic weight lifetime days to decades.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Temporal lobe epilepsy from runaway recurrence; cueing failure in early Alzheimer's disease; storage blockade under NMDA antagonists such as ketamine.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

Propose the module name autoassociative_pattern_completer, subscribing to cue_fragment messages and a store_pattern teaching channel, and publishing completed_pattern messages with a confidence score derived from settling energy.

The closest artificial intelligence analogue is the Hopfield network and its modern-continuous descendants, which are mathematically equivalent to the attention operation of transformers.

The biological motif differs in its sparse 1 percent connectivity, its separate detonator pathway for writing, and its acetylcholine-gated switch between storage and recall, all three worth copying.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to recall a complete stored pattern from a fragment, using Hebbian weights and repeated recurrent updates.
Create a list variable called stored patterns containing the patterns to remember, each a list of values that are either one or negative one.
Create a table variable called weights with all entries set to 0.
For each pattern in stored patterns, perform the following actions.
    For each pair of different positions i and j in the pattern, perform the following actions.
        Calculate the product of the value at position i and the value at position j.
        Add the result to the entry of weights at row i and column j.
    End the inner loop.
End the outer loop.
Create a list variable called state and set it to the cue fragment, with unknown positions set to 0.
Repeat the following actions ten times.
    For each position i in state, perform the following actions.
        Calculate the sum over all positions j of the entry of weights at row i and column j multiplied by the value of state at position j.
        If the sum is greater than or equal to 0 is true, then set the value of state at position i to 1.
        Otherwise, set the value of state at position i to negative 1.
        End the conditional block.
    End the inner loop.
End the repetition block.
Display state to the console as the recalled pattern.
The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because a Hopfield network is two matrix operations, and Python with numpy states them in two lines each and shows convergence plainly.

# Autoassociative pattern completion, Hopfield style, as attributed to
# hippocampal CA3 recurrent collaterals (Marr 1971; Hopfield, PNAS 1982;
# Guzman et al., Science 2016: sparse ~1% recurrent connectivity suffices).
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
N, P = 200, 5                          # cells, stored patterns
patterns = rng.choice([-1, 1], size=(P, N))

W = (patterns.T @ patterns) / N        # Hebbian outer-product learning
np.fill_diagonal(W, 0.0)               # no self-synapses

target = patterns[0]
cue = target.copy()
flip = rng.choice(N, size=N // 2, replace=False)
cue[flip] = rng.choice([-1, 1], size=N // 2)   # corrupt half the cue

state = cue.copy()
for step in range(8):                  # recurrent settling
    state = np.sign(W @ state)
    state[state == 0] = 1
    overlap = float(state @ target) / N
    print(f"step {step + 1}: overlap with stored memory = {overlap:+.2f}")

print("recalled correctly:", bool(np.array_equal(state, target)))

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

A pool of excitatory cells wired sparsely back onto itself through plastic synapses, guarded by fast feedback inhibition, that answers a fragment with the whole: no other motif returns more information than it was given.


CHAPTER 30. THE POINT ATTRACTOR OF PERSISTENT ACTIVITY (Recurrently Sustained Delay-Period Ensemble) (The Working Memory Cell Assembly) (COG)

Read a telephone number, close your eyes, and dial: for those few seconds the number exists nowhere in the world except as a pattern of neurons firing in your prefrontal cortex, activity outliving its cause.

This is persistent activity, the physical present tense of keeping something in mind, discovered by Fuster and by Kubota and Niki in 1971 as prefrontal cells that kept firing through a delay between cue and response.

The circuit is recurrent excitation balanced against inhibition, tuned so that a brief input can switch a cell assembly from a quiet stable state to an active stable state, where it stays until switched off.

Mathematically each memory is a point attractor: one fixed pattern of elevated firing that the network holds against noise.

Working names the memory's job: temporary storage in the service of an ongoing task.

Memory names what is held, an item no longer present in the senses.

Cell Assembly names the physical carrier, Hebb's term for a group of neurons that sustain one another's firing.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

The point attractor of persistent activity is a recurrently connected population of principal cells, sharing tuning for a particular item or location, whose mutual excitation is strong enough to sustain firing after the stimulus ends, with lateral and feedback inhibition preventing spread and runaway.

It computes sample-and-hold: a short-term, activity-based memory register that stores one item as an elevated firing state of 10 to 50 spikes per second for seconds, readable at any moment by downstream circuits.

The same machinery computes the delay-bridging that links a perception to a later action, which is the core of deliberation.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The nodes are several pools of excitatory pyramidal cells, one pool per stored item or direction, one shared pool of fast-spiking inhibitory interneurons, plus a cue input line and a readout line.

Within each pyramidal pool, dense recurrent excitatory (glutamatergic) connections link cells of similar tuning, the sustaining edges.

All pyramidal pools excite the shared interneuron pool, which returns broad inhibition (gamma-aminobutyric acid, GABA) onto every pyramidal pool, so pools compete: this lateral inhibition keeps only one attractor active and sharpens tuning during the delay.

Cue inputs excite one pool transiently; a nonspecific external drive or a strong distractor volley to the interneurons serves as the off switch.

Dopaminergic fibres from the midbrain form a modulatory edge onto both cell classes, tuning the depth of the attractor.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The sustaining role is played by layer 3 and layer 5 pyramidal cells of dorsolateral prefrontal cortex from the neuron catalogue - the delay cells - whose regular-spiking, weakly adapting personality suits multi-second holding, since a strongly adapting cell would talk itself out of the attractor.

Their long recurrent horizontal axons in layer 3 stitch same-tuned microcolumns together.

The competition role is played by the parvalbumin basket cell, whose fast-spiking personality lets inhibition track excitation without lag, stabilising the balance on which persistence depends.

The Martinotti-type somatostatin interneuron gates the pyramidal dendrites against distractors arriving in layer 1, and the dopaminergic neuron of the ventral tegmental area, a slow pacemaker with burst mode, sets the inverted-U modulation that makes the memory neither too rigid nor too fragile.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

The recurrent synapses are glutamatergic with an unusually heavy reliance on N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors, including the slow NR2B subtype concentrated in prefrontal layer 3: their 50 to 150 millisecond decay smooths recurrent drive across spike intervals, and blocking them - even a 30 percent reduction in NMDA conductance in models - collapses persistent firing.

alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors contribute fast drive, basket synapses deliver GABA-A inhibition at the soma, and Martinotti synapses deliver GABA at the apical dendrite.

Dopamine D1 receptors on spines and interneurons scale both excitation and inhibition, and hyperpolarisation-activated cyclic-nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels on the same spines leak the circuit when cyclic adenosine monophosphate rises under stress.

Weights show short-term facilitation, which some theories use to hold memories silently between spikes.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One attractor pool is on the order of thousands to tens of thousands of pyramidal cells spanning a few hundred micrometres to a few millimetres of cortex, linked by horizontal axons of up to several millimetres; a full working memory map, such as the spatial map of area 46, holds many overlapping pools within one cortical area of a few square centimetres.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

Dozens of installations across the cortical mantle and beyond, wherever delay activity is recorded: prefrontal areas hold the most robust and distractor-resistant instances, with parietal, frontal eye field, inferotemporal and even entorhinal instances holding more labile copies, and subcortical loops through the mediodorsal thalamus sustaining the cortical ones.

Confidence is high that persistence is distributed, moderate on how much any single area could sustain alone.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• Dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (area 46) - the canonical spatial working memory store, most resistant to distraction.

• Frontal eye fields - holds intended saccade targets across delays.

• Posterior parietal cortex - holds spatial and numerical quantities, more easily overwritten by new input.

• Inferotemporal cortex - holds object identity across delays in visual memory tasks.

• Mediodorsal thalamus - the loop partner whose drive keeps prefrontal attractors alive.

• Entorhinal cortex - persistent firing supports bridging of temporal gaps in episodic memory.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Strip this motif from the prefrontal cortex and perception would still occur and habits would still run, but the present moment would shrink to the width of the stimulus: no held goal, no mental arithmetic, no sentence comprehension that spans its own clauses.

The prefrontal cortex would become a stimulus-response tissue, which is a fair description of what strong distraction, sleep loss, or excess stress hormones temporarily make it.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

The transformation is bistable sample-and-hold: below a cue threshold the pool rests near baseline (0.5 to 5 spikes per second); a cue exceeding threshold flips it to the elevated fixed point (10 to 50 spikes per second), where it remains after the input ends; a sufficiently strong global inhibitory volley or reward-signalled response command flips it back.

The transfer function is a saturating recurrent gain crossing unity, creating two stable fixed points separated by an unstable one - mathematical bistability.

Real numbers: monkey delay cells hold rates of roughly 10 to 30 spikes per second for delays of 2 to 30 seconds, and information about the cue can be decoded from population activity throughout.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

Switch-on within 100 to 200 milliseconds of cue; holding for seconds to tens of seconds, often with slow drift and gamma-band ripples riding on the plateau; switch-off within about 100 milliseconds of the response signal.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

The baseline regime, the memory regime, and a fragility spectrum in between: dopamine at intermediate levels deepens the attractor, while too little (fatigue) or too much (acute stress) shallows it, the famous inverted-U.

Some instances hold information not as a fixed point but as a rotating trajectory or in facilitated synapses with silent periods; the honest summary is that the point attractor is the proven backbone with activity-silent mechanisms layered on top.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

The attractor landscape itself is learned: training on a working memory task strengthens recurrent connections among cells with shared tuning, and delay activity grows with practice.

Short-term synaptic facilitation over hundreds of milliseconds provides a hidden memory buffer, and dopamine-gated plasticity slowly reshapes which items the region can hold well.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

Discrete-item variants (object memory, with well-separated point attractors) and continuous variants (spatial memory, where the points blur toward a ring or sheet of attractors and stored locations drift measurably during the delay, the drift matching human response scatter).

Thalamocortical variants lean on the mediodorsal loop; entorhinal variants use intrinsic cellular plateau currents as well as circuit recurrence.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

Prefrontal recurrent circuitry matures remarkably late: layer 3 connectivity, NMDA subunit composition, and inhibitory tuning continue changing through adolescence into the mid-twenties in humans, and working memory capacity rises in parallel.

The assembly rule is activity-dependent: pools form among cells co-activated by shared inputs.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

Delay activity exists in birds (nidopallium caudolaterale) with no layered cortex at all, so the attractor is a circuit solution evolution has reached at least twice.

The primate elaboration is the expansion of layer 3 recurrent networks and their NMDA-rich synapses, which is also the tissue most altered in schizophrenia - the price of the upgrade.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Persistent firing is metabolically brutal, and the prefrontal capillary and astrocyte lattice runs near its ceiling during long delays; astrocytic glutamate clearance and lactate supply are rate-limiting, which is one reason working memory fails early in hypoglycaemia and hypoxia.

Perineuronal nets around the parvalbumin cells stabilise the mature inhibitory tuning.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Schizophrenia is the motif's signature disorder: layer 3 pyramidal cells of area 46 lose about 23 percent of their spines, delay-period activity and working memory performance fall, and NMDA blockers such as ketamine reproduce both.

Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder involves shallow, distractible attractors improved by drugs that raise prefrontal catecholamines; acute stress collapses the attractor through excess cyclic adenosine monophosphate opening HCN channels; ageing shows the same channel-mediated leak.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ Cue volleys from sensory association cortex, 100 to 200 milliseconds long.

◦ Sustaining drive from the mediodorsal thalamus.

◦ Dopamine level from the ventral tegmental area, optimal at intermediate D1 receptor occupancy.

◦ Response and reward signals that command switch-off.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ The held item, readable continuously as a population rate code of 10 to 50 spikes per second.

◦ Top-down bias to sensory cortex and motor plans to premotor circuits.

• STATE.

◦ Which pool, if any, is at its elevated fixed point, plus drift of the stored value at roughly 1 to 3 degrees of visual angle per second in spatial tasks.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Recurrent gain just above unity; cue threshold; inhibitory pool weight; D1 occupancy setting attractor depth.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ NMDA decay 50 to 150 milliseconds, the load-bearing constant; membrane 10 to 20 milliseconds; holding 2 to 30 seconds; switch-off about 100 milliseconds.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Working memory deficit of schizophrenia with layer 3 spine loss near 23 percent; distractibility of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder; stress-induced prefrontal collapse; ketamine-induced loss of delay firing.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

Propose the module name working_memory_holding_register, subscribing to item_cue, distractor_alert, and neuromodulator_state messages and publishing held_item messages continuously plus a memory_released event at switch-off.

The closest artificial intelligence analogues are the gated recurrent cell (long short-term memory) and the key-value cache of a transformer.

The biological motif differs in holding the item as ongoing activity that every subscriber can read at any instant without a query, in its capacity limit of roughly three to four items, and in a fragility dial (dopamine) that trades stability against updatability - a control knob artificial systems mostly lack.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to hold a memory as self-sustained firing, switched on by a cue and switched off when a distractor or stop signal exceeds a threshold.
Create a number variable called firing rate with initial value 1.
Create a number variable called recurrent gain with initial value 2.
Create a number variable called saturation rate with initial value 40.
Create a number variable called inhibition with initial value 15.
Create a number variable called cue strength with initial value 0.
Create a number variable called stop strength with initial value 0.
Create a number variable called stop threshold with initial value 20.
Repeat the following actions once for each time step of the task.
    Set cue strength to the cue input at this time step.
    Set stop strength to the distractor or stop input at this time step.
    Calculate the product of recurrent gain and firing rate.
    Add cue strength to the result.
    Subtract inhibition from the result.
    Subtract stop strength from the result.
    If the result is greater than saturation rate is true, then set the result to saturation rate.
    End the conditional block.
    If the result is less than 1 is true, then set the result to 1.
    End the conditional block.
    Move firing rate one tenth of the way from its current value toward the result.
    If stop strength is greater than stop threshold is true, then set firing rate to 1.
    End the conditional block.
End the repetition block.
Display firing rate at each step to the console.
The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because bistability is best believed by watching one variable stay up after its cause is removed, and a short numpy loop shows exactly that.

# Bistable persistent activity: a cue switches the assembly on, firing
# outlives the cue, and a suprathreshold distractor volley switches it off
# (Fuster & Alexander, Science 1971; Wang, J Neurosci 1999: NMDA-dominated
# recurrence is required for the stable elevated state).
import numpy as np

dt, tau = 1.0, 100.0                 # milliseconds; NMDA-slow effective tau
T = 3000
r = np.zeros(T); r[0] = 1.0          # spikes per second, baseline

def f(x, r_max=40.0):                # saturating recurrent transfer
    return r_max * max(x, 0.0) ** 2 / (20.0 ** 2 + max(x, 0.0) ** 2)

cue = np.zeros(T);  cue[500:700] = 30.0        # brief cue at t = 0.5 s
stop = np.zeros(T); stop[2200:2400] = 35.0     # distractor at t = 2.2 s
STOP_THRESHOLD = 20.0

for t in range(1, T):
    drive = 1.9 * r[t - 1] + cue[t] - 12.0     # recurrence + input - inhibition
    if stop[t] > STOP_THRESHOLD:
        drive -= 60.0                          # global inhibitory volley
    r[t] = r[t - 1] + dt / tau * (f(drive) - r[t - 1] + 1.0)

for ms in (400, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2600):
    print(f"t = {ms/1000:.1f} s  rate = {r[ms]:5.1f} Hz")
print("held after cue ended:", r[2000] > 15.0, "| released:", r[2600] < 5.0)

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

A population whose firing outlives its stimulus by seconds, sitting at one of two stable rates and flipped between them by brief inputs: the only motif whose defining recording is what the cells do after the world has gone quiet.


CHAPTER 31. THE LINE ATTRACTOR (Velocity-To-Position Recurrent Integrator) (The Neural Integrator) (NON-COG)

Look to your left and stop: your eyes stay put, though the command that moved them is finished.

Something in the brainstem is holding the total of every velocity command ever issued, and that something is a recurrent network tuned so precisely that every level of activity is stable - not one attractor point but a continuous line of them.

Such a network adds its inputs over time and holds the running sum, which is the mathematical operation of integration performed in flesh.

The horizontal oculomotor integrator of the nucleus prepositus hypoglossi is the classic instance, and its honest imperfection - a slow leak with a time constant near 25 seconds - is measurable in every human gaze.

Neural marks the substrate.

Integrator names the computation, the summing of a signal over time, borrowed directly from calculus and control engineering.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

The line attractor is a recurrent excitatory network whose feedback gain is tuned to almost exactly unity, so that activity neither grows nor decays but persists at whatever level input has pushed it to; a continuum of stable states replaces the isolated points of Chapter 30.

It computes temporal integration: output equals the accumulated sum of past input, converting eye-velocity commands into eye-position holding, head-velocity signals into position estimates, and, in its cognitive installations, momentary evidence into a decision total.

This chapter is tagged (NON-COG) for its canonical motor role, with the honest note that the identical motif accumulates evidence in decision circuits.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The nodes are two mirror pools of excitatory integrator neurons, one per side of the brainstem, each with recurrent excitatory (glutamatergic) connections within the pool tuned near unity gain.

Commissural inhibitory (glycinergic and GABAergic) edges cross the midline, each pool suppressing its mirror, so the two sides encode eye position as a push-pull difference.

Input edges carry brief excitatory velocity bursts from saccadic burst neurons and vestibular velocity signals; output edges are excitatory and inhibitory projections to the abducens and oculomotor nuclei.

A cerebellar edge from the flocculus continuously trims the feedback gain, the plumber of the leak.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The integrator role is played by neurons of the nucleus prepositus hypoglossi and medial vestibular nucleus from the neuron catalogue, tonic regular-firing cells whose rate is linearly proportional to eye position at roughly 1 to 4 spikes per second per degree - a personality of steadiness, since a bursting or adapting cell would corrupt the stored sum.

Saccadic burst neurons of the paramedian pontine reticular formation supply the violent input transients, their high-frequency bursts (up to 1,000 spikes per second) personifying the derivative that the network integrates.

Floccular Purkinje cells, with their exquisitely modifiable simple-spike output, play the calibrator, and abducens motor neurons read the sum out into muscle.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

Recurrent and input synapses are glutamatergic on alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) and N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors; commissural inhibition uses glycine and gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA); some integrator neurons are coupled by connexin 36 gap junctions, which smooth the population toward a single shared value.

The load-bearing property is precision of weights: models show the recurrent gain must be tuned to within a fraction of a percent of unity to achieve the observed 25 second persistence from 10 to 100 millisecond cellular time constants, and this tuning is maintained by cerebellar-dependent plasticity driven by retinal slip error.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

The horizontal integrator on one side comprises on the order of a few thousand neurons within a nucleus a few millimetres long; the larval zebrafish version, where the motif has been imaged whole, does the same job with roughly one hundred neurons.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

A handful of proven motor instances - horizontal (nucleus prepositus hypoglossi with medial vestibular nucleus), vertical and torsional (interstitial nucleus of Cajal), head-and-neck and limb posture integrators of the spinal cord and brainstem - plus cognitive installations in parietal and frontal decision circuits where firing ramps with accumulated evidence.

Confidence is high for the oculomotor cases, moderate for evidence accumulation being the same circuit mechanism rather than the same mathematics differently implemented.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• Nucleus prepositus hypoglossi, with the medial vestibular nucleus - the horizontal eye-position integrator.

• Interstitial nucleus of Cajal - the vertical and torsional eye-position integrator.

• Cerebellar flocculus - not the integrator itself but its gain calibrator, without which the leak worsens tenfold.

• Vestibular nuclei velocity-storage network - integrates and prolongs head-velocity estimates.

• Posterior parietal cortex (lateral intraparietal area) and frontal eye fields - ramping evidence accumulators for decisions, the cognitive re-use.

• Spinal and brainstem postural networks - hold tonic posture commands between movement bursts.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Without this motif every gaze would slide home: eyes could move but not hold, producing gaze-evoked nystagmus, the tell-tale drift-and-reset seen when the integrator is damaged or drugged.

Upstream, the parietal cortex would lose its running totals, and decisions requiring accumulated evidence would have to be made from the last instant alone.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

Output rate equals the time integral of input rate, held with a decay time constant near 25 seconds in intact humans; after lesions of the nucleus prepositus hypoglossi the time constant falls to roughly one tenth of normal, and the mechanics of the orbit alone would give only about 200 milliseconds.

The transfer function is leaky integration: perfect integration is the ideal, unity-minus-epsilon feedback is the reality.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

Input bursts last tens of milliseconds; the stored value persists for tens of seconds; the cerebellar recalibration loop operates over minutes to days.

In darkness the leak is visible as centripetal eye drift of a fraction of a degree per second.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

The tuned regime (time constant tens of seconds), the leaky regime (drift back to centre, as in alcohol intoxication or cerebellar disease), and the unstable regime (gain above unity, activity grows and the eyes ratchet outward, seen in some congenital nystagmus).

Recent work shows the effective time constant is itself adjustable by behavioural context, so the leak is partly a setting, not only an error.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

The integrator is continuously self-calibrating: retinal image slip during attempted fixation is the error signal, the flocculus converts it into adjustments of synaptic gain, and wearing magnifying or minifying lenses retunes the integrator within hours - one of the cleanest demonstrations of supervised learning in the vertebrate brain.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

Single-dimension oculomotor variants; the velocity-storage variant, which integrates with a deliberate 15 to 20 second leak; bilateral push-pull versus unilateral implementations; and the cortical ramping variant whose integration is bounded by decision thresholds.

Zebrafish work suggests the line attractor may be realised as a chain of small bistable clusters approximating a line, an honest complication to the smooth textbook picture.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

The circuit assembles prenatally from hindbrain rhombomeres, but its gain is tuned postnatally by visual experience; infants show poor gaze holding that matures over the first months, and dark-reared animals never tune the leak properly.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

Every vertebrate with mobile eyes has this integrator, from lamprey onward, making it one of the oldest attractor circuits in the vertebrate brain; the goldfish and zebrafish versions are so conserved that they serve as the experimental models for the human one.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Tonic firing at up to 100 spikes per second for a lifetime demands steady astrocytic metabolic support and robust mitochondria; the nucleus sits beside the fourth ventricle, and its neurons are bathed by cerebrospinal fluid influences, a location that makes it vulnerable to Wernicke's thiamine-deficiency lesions.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Gaze-evoked nystagmus is the motif's signature failure, produced by cerebellar degeneration, alcohol, anticonvulsant toxicity, and lesions of the nucleus prepositus hypoglossi; congenital nystagmus includes unstable-gain forms; downbeat nystagmus reflects vertical integrator miscalibration in floccular disease.

In the cognitive installations, impulsive decisions can be read as premature escape from an accumulation that should have run longer.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ Eye-velocity bursts from saccadic burst neurons, up to 1,000 spikes per second for tens of milliseconds.

◦ Head-velocity signals from the vestibular apparatus.

◦ Gain-correction signals from the cerebellar flocculus.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ Eye-position command to abducens and oculomotor nuclei, roughly 1 to 4 spikes per second per degree of eccentricity.

• STATE.

◦ One continuous scalar per axis, the current integrated position, carried as the bilateral firing-rate difference.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Feedback gain within a fraction of a percent of unity; position sensitivity per neuron; commissural inhibition weight.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Cellular membrane 10 to 100 milliseconds; network persistence about 25 seconds intact, about 2 seconds after lesion, about 0.2 seconds from orbital mechanics alone; recalibration minutes to days.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Gaze-evoked nystagmus from a leaky integrator; unstable congenital nystagmus from excess gain; alcohol and antiepileptic drug intoxication as reversible chemical leaks.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

Propose the module name velocity_to_position_integrator, subscribing to velocity_command and calibration_error messages and publishing position_estimate continuously.

The closest artificial intelligence analogues are the accumulator of a drift-diffusion decision model and the cell state of a long short-term memory unit with its forget gate pinned near one.

The biological motif differs in maintaining its unity gain by an online supervised calibration loop (the cerebellum) rather than by design, a self-repairing property worth stealing for any long-horizon artificial memory.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

This section does not apply to this microcircuit type for the reason that this motif serves a substrate or regulatory role rather than a cognitive-computational role, and is tagged (NON-COG).

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

A recurrent network whose every activity level is a resting place, recognisable in one recording: tonic firing proportional to position that persists for tens of seconds after a burst lasting hundredths of one, and whose failure is visible to any clinician as drifting eyes.


CHAPTER 32. THE RING ATTRACTOR (Circular Continuous Attractor With Local Excitation And Long-Range Inhibition) (The Inner Compass Circuit) (COG)

Close your eyes and turn on the spot, and you still know roughly which way you face: something in your brain is carrying a heading signal that no sense is currently supplying.

The carrier is a ring attractor - cells arranged, functionally or literally, in a circle, each exciting its neighbours and inhibiting cells far around the ring, so that exactly one bump of activity survives, and velocity inputs push the bump around like a compass needle.

Theorists drew this circuit in the 1990s to explain mammalian head-direction cells; two decades later imaging of the fruit fly's ellipsoid body showed the ring built in actual anatomy, neuron for neuron where the mathematics said it should be.

It is the clearest case in all neuroscience of a computational structure predicted on paper and then found in tissue.

Inner names the signal's independence from the outside world: the compass runs in darkness.

Compass names the computation, a maintained estimate of heading.

Circuit marks the wiring motif, installed in flies and in the mammalian brainstem-thalamus-cortex head-direction stream alike.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

The ring attractor is a population of cells with a circular topology of preferred directions, wired with local mutual excitation and broad mutual inhibition, so the stable states are single localised bumps of activity - one for every possible heading, a continuous circular family of attractors.

It computes maintained orientation with angular path integration: the bump position is the current heading estimate, angular velocity inputs rotate the bump at the speed of the head, and landmark inputs correct the accumulated drift.

The same geometry serves any circular variable, from heading to the phase of a rhythm.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The nodes are a ring of excitatory compass cells ordered by preferred direction, a pool of inhibitory cells, and two mirror sets of rotation cells, one for each turning direction.

Excitatory (glutamatergic, or cholinergic in the fly) edges connect each compass cell to its near neighbours on the ring; inhibitory edges - either broad global inhibition from the interneuron pool or, in the fly, GABAergic ring neurons - suppress cells distant on the ring, enforcing a single bump.

Each rotation cell set receives the bump plus an angular-velocity signal from the vestibular system (or fly self-motion signals) and projects back onto the ring with a systematic offset, leftward-shifted for one set and rightward for the other, so unequal velocity drive drags the bump around.

Landmark edges from visual cells synapse onto the ring with plastic weights, pinning the bump to the world.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

In the mammal the compass role is played by head-direction cells of the anterodorsal thalamic nucleus, presubiculum and lateral mammillary nucleus from the neuron catalogue, tonic cells firing up to 100 spikes per second at their preferred direction with a tuning width near 90 degrees - steadiness again, since the bump must idle without decaying.

The rotation role falls to angular-velocity cells of the dorsal tegmental nucleus, whose firing personality is velocity-proportional rather than position-holding.

Parvalbumin-type fast-spiking interneurons of the thalamic reticular nucleus and local circuits supply the long-range suppression.

In the fly the cast is anatomically explicit: the ellipsoid-body-protocerebral-bridge (E-PG) compass neurons form the ring, P-EN neurons are the two offset rotation sets, and GABAergic ring neurons personify the global inhibition; the fly cast is cited here because it is the ground truth against which the mammalian cast is interpreted.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

Mammalian ring edges are glutamatergic on alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) and N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors with gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-A inhibition; the fly ring uses acetylcholine for excitation and GABA for the ring-neuron inhibition.

The landmark synapses onto compass cells follow an anti-Hebbian plasticity rule in the fly, weakening inputs that fire with the bump so that the most reliable visual cue comes to steer it - a measured learning rule, not a conjecture.

Offset connections from rotation cells are the geometric heart of the fabric: their systematic angular shift is what converts a speed signal into bump motion.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

The fly instance is astonishingly small: roughly 16 functional wedges built from about 50 E-PG neurons, a complete working compass in under a hundred cells.

The mammalian instance is distributed: on the order of tens of thousands of head-direction cells across the lateral mammillary nucleus, anterodorsal thalamus (where roughly 60 percent of cells are head-direction tuned) and presubiculum, functionally but not anatomically arranged as a ring.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

At least one full instance per hemisphere pair for heading, with strong evidence for further ring-geometry codes: grid cell modules of the entorhinal cortex behave as twisted-torus continuous attractors (a ring generalised to two dimensions), and sleep recordings show the head-direction ring keeps circulating with the bump intact when all sensory input is gone, the decisive evidence that the attractor is internal.

Confidence is very high for the fly, high for the mammalian head-direction system, moderate for other circular variables.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• Dorsal tegmental nucleus and lateral mammillary nucleus of the brainstem and hypothalamus - the generative core of the mammalian compass, where the velocity-to-bump conversion begins.

• Anterodorsal thalamic nucleus - the relay ring, the densest concentration of head-direction cells.

• Presubiculum (postsubiculum) - the cortical stage, where landmark correction is strongest.

• Retrosplenial cortex - integrates the compass with visual scenes and routes.

• Medial entorhinal cortex - imports the heading signal for grid-cell path integration, and hosts the twisted-torus generalisation.

• Insect central complex ellipsoid body - cited as the anatomical ground truth of the motif, though outside the human map.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Without this motif the mammillary-thalamic-presubicular stream would carry no heading, grid cells downstream would lose their orientation and the cognitive map would spin freely: navigation would reduce to beacon-following, and dead reckoning in darkness would be impossible.

The felt sense of which way one faces - and its failure, the sudden conviction that north is the wrong way - are this circuit speaking.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

Input is angular head velocity plus landmark bearing; output is estimated heading, read as the angular position of the bump.

The transformation is integration on a circle with attractor stabilisation: bump speed matches head turning speed with near-unity gain across at least plus and minus several hundred degrees per second, and in darkness the estimate drifts by a few degrees per minute until a landmark resets it.

Tuning curves are unimodal with widths near 60 to 90 degrees, and the population vector tracks true heading within a few degrees when cues are available.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

The bump updates continuously with vestibular latency of roughly 10 to 40 milliseconds - thalamic head-direction cells actually lead the head by tens of milliseconds, anticipating direction; landmark corrections complete within a few hundred milliseconds; drift in darkness accumulates over minutes.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

The cue-anchored regime (bump pinned to landmarks), the path-integration regime (bump driven by velocity alone, slowly drifting), the teleport regime (conflicting cues make the bump jump discretely to a new bearing rather than fade), and sleep, where the bump wanders the ring under internal dynamics - each regime observed in recordings.

The failure regime is a split or extinguished bump, seen transiently under cue conflict in the fly.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

Landmark control is learned: plastic synapses from visual cells onto the ring, anti-Hebbian in the fly, let an arbitrary new landmark capture the compass within minutes.

The velocity gain is also calibrated by experience, and in mammals the head-direction map in a novel environment inherits its orientation from the old one via the attractor, then re-anchors.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

The literal anatomical ring of the insect ellipsoid body; the functionally ringed but anatomically scattered mammalian version; the two-dimensional twisted-torus variant of grid cell modules; and proposed ring codes for circular variables beyond heading, such as angular phase in motor rhythms - the last held at low confidence.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

Head-direction tuning is the earliest spatial signal to mature in the rodent, present and organised before the eyes open, implying the ring self-assembles from internal activity and vestibular input rather than from vision; landmark control is added after eye opening.

The correlation structure of the adult network - cells with nearby preferred directions covarying under all conditions - is precisely what a rigid attractor predicts.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

Insects and mammals separated more than 550 million years ago, yet both carry ring attractor compasses; whether this is deep homology of an ancestral heading circuit or stunning convergence on the one good solution is unresolved, and either answer flatters the motif.

The mammalian implementation trades the insect's anatomical elegance for redundancy across many nuclei.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

The thalamic and mammillary stations depend on tightly regulated tonic firing and are early casualties of thiamine deficiency: astrocytic and vascular fragility of the mammillary bodies underlies their destruction in Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, taking the compass's core with them.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Lesions anywhere along the dorsal tegmental-mammillary-anterodorsal-presubicular chain abolish or degrade head-direction tuning and impair path integration; Korsakoff syndrome destroys the mammillary link; vestibular failure unmoors the bump, and the transient disorientation of vestibular disease is partly a drifting compass.

Topographical disorientation after retrosplenial stroke - patients who recognise landmarks yet cannot derive heading from them - is the human clinical signature.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ Angular head velocity from the vestibular semicircular canals, resolved within 10 to 40 milliseconds.

◦ Landmark bearing from visual cortex via retrosplenial and presubicular routes.

◦ Motor efference copies that let the bump anticipate the head by tens of milliseconds.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ Current heading estimate as bump position, tuning width 60 to 90 degrees per cell, population accuracy within a few degrees.

◦ Heading reference to entorhinal grid modules and retrosplenial route planning.

• STATE.

◦ One circular variable, the bump's angular position, plus its anchoring status (cue-anchored or free-running).

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Local excitation width; inhibition strength (one bump enforced); rotation gain near unity; landmark synapse weights.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Update latency 10 to 40 milliseconds; landmark reset a few hundred milliseconds; dark drift a few degrees per minute; landmark learning minutes.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Loss of head-direction signal after anterodorsal thalamic or mammillary lesions; Wernicke-Korsakoff destruction of the mammillary core; heading disorientation after retrosplenial stroke; drift and vertigo in vestibular failure.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

Propose the module name heading_ring_attractor_compass, subscribing to angular_velocity, landmark_bearing, and motor_efference_copy messages and publishing heading_estimate messages with a drift-uncertainty field that grows in the absence of landmark corrections.

The closest artificial intelligence analogues are the circular latent spaces that emerge in recurrent networks trained on path integration, and phase representations in complex-valued networks.

The biological motif differs in enforcing exactly one bump by construction, in fusing dead reckoning with landmark correction through a learned, anti-Hebbian anchoring rule, and in running honestly in the dark with quantified drift - a built-in confidence model most artificial estimators lack.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to hold a bump of activity on a ring of cells and move it in proportion to an angular velocity input.
Create a number variable called cell count with initial value 32.
Create a list variable called activity with cell count entries, all set to 0.
Set a small group of neighbouring entries of activity to 1 to form the initial bump.
Repeat the following actions once for each time step.
    Create a list variable called new activity with cell count entries, all set to 0.
    For each cell position on the ring, perform the following actions.
        Calculate the sum of the activity of the cell and its immediate neighbours on the ring, weighted most for the cell itself.
        Subtract a global inhibition value equal to a constant multiplied by the total activity of the whole ring.
        Add the angular velocity input multiplied by the difference between the activity of the neighbour behind and the neighbour ahead.
        If the result is less than 0 is true, then set the result to 0.
        End the conditional block.
        Set the entry of new activity at this cell position to the result.
    End the inner loop.
    Divide every entry of new activity by the largest entry of new activity.
    Set activity to new activity.
    Calculate the position of the largest entry of activity.
    Display the result to the console as the current heading.
End the repetition block.
The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because a moving bump is a picture drawn in numbers, and a numpy ring updated in a loop lets the reader watch the compass needle travel.

# Ring attractor: local excitation plus global inhibition holds one bump;
# asymmetric velocity drive rotates it, as in fly E-PG compass neurons and
# mammalian head-direction cells (Zhang, J Neurosci 1996; Seelig & Jayaraman,
# Nature 2015; Kim et al., Science 2017).
import numpy as np

N = 32                                     # cells around the ring
theta = np.arange(N) * 2 * np.pi / N
W = np.cos(theta[:, None] - theta[None, :])  # local excite, distant inhibit
r = np.exp(np.cos(theta - np.pi))          # initial bump at 180 degrees
r /= r.max()

def step(r, velocity):
    shifted = np.roll(r, -1) - np.roll(r, 1)   # asymmetric drive
    drive = W @ r / N + velocity * shifted - 0.30 * r.sum() / N
    r_new = np.maximum(r + 0.5 * (drive - 0.1), 0.0)
    return r_new / max(r_new.max(), 1e-9)      # normalise: one bump survives

def bump_deg(r):
    return np.degrees(np.angle(np.sum(r * np.exp(1j * theta)))) % 360

velocity_input = [0.0] * 20 + [0.15] * 60 + [0.0] * 20   # turn, then stop
for t, v in enumerate(velocity_input):
    r = step(r, v)
    if t % 20 == 19:
        print(f"step {t + 1:3d}  velocity {v:5.2f}  heading {bump_deg(r):6.1f} deg")

print("bump held after rotation stopped:", r.max() > 5 * r.mean())

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

A closed loop of cells holding exactly one bump of activity that turns when the head turns and stands still in the dark: the only circuit in neuroscience that was drawn by theorists first and then photographed, ring and all, in a living brain.


CHAPTER 33. THE EXPANSION RECODER (Sparse High-Dimensional Recoding Motif) (The Overlap-Breaker) (COG)

Take a handful of overlapping signals, throw them onto a crowd a hundred times larger, and let a fierce brake keep almost everyone quiet: the few who fire are a new code, and inputs that looked nearly identical now light up almost non-overlapping sets.

This is David Marr's oldest gift to computational neuroscience, and the brain installs it twice, once for remembering episodes and once for calibrating movement.

It is the circuit that makes two similar mornings storable as two different memories.

Expansion names the geometry: a small input population fans out onto a much larger one.

Recoder names the job: the same information is rewritten in a new, sparser alphabet.

Overlap-Breaker names the payoff: similar inputs are pushed apart so later stages can tell them apart.


WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

The expansion recoder is a feedforward motif in which a modest number of input fibres project, with sparse and quasi-random convergence, onto a very large population of small granule-type neurons that a powerful inhibitory system holds to a low firing fraction.

Its computation is pattern separation: it maps input vectors to higher-dimensional, sparse output vectors so that the overlap (correlation) between two outputs is smaller than the overlap between the two inputs that produced them.

In plain words, it takes things that resemble each other and makes their brain-codes resemble each other less, which is the precondition for storing them as distinct memories or associating them with distinct actions.


THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The graph has four node roles: input fibres, granule cells, a feedforward or feedback inhibitory interneuron, and downstream reader cells.

Each input fibre sends excitatory (glutamatergic, positive-sign) edges to a small, sparse, effectively random subset of the granule population, and each granule cell collects only a few such edges (in the cerebellum famously about four).

A single inhibitory interneuron receives excitatory edges from the input fibres and from granule cells and returns inhibitory (gamma-aminobutyric acid, or GABA, negative-sign) edges broadly across the granule field, implementing a threshold that only a small fraction of granule cells can cross.

The granule cells then send excitatory edges onward to reader cells, and in most installations the granule axon also carries the sparse code to the site of plasticity downstream.

The defining topological facts are the fan-out ratio (many more granule cells than input fibres) and the low convergence per granule cell (few inputs each), which together make each granule cell a coincidence detector for a rare conjunction of inputs.


THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

In the dentate gyrus the recoder cell is the dentate granule cell of the neuron catalogue, a small, quiet neuron with an exceptionally negative resting potential and a high firing threshold, so it stays silent unless several entorhinal inputs coincide - this reluctance is exactly what enforces sparseness.

Its brake is the parvalbumin-positive fast-spiking basket cell, the same fast, non-adapting, hard-hitting interneuron seen in the lateral-inhibition and gamma-timing motifs, whose speed lets one cell veto thousands of granule cells within a millisecond.

In the cerebellum the recoder cell is the cerebellar granule cell, the four-input granule cell of the catalogue and the most numerous neuron in the human brain, again a small high-threshold coincidence detector.

Its brake is the Golgi cell, a slower, tonically active, broadly projecting inhibitory neuron whose sustained output sets the granule field's baseline gain and holds the active fraction low.

The input roles are played by entorhinal layer II stellate and pyramidal cells (dentate case) and by mossy-fibre-carrying precerebellar neurons such as pontine cells (cerebellar case).


THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

The input-to-granule synapse is glutamatergic onto granule dendrites, using AMPA (alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid) receptors for fast transmission and NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate) receptors for coincidence-gated plasticity; in the cerebellum this synapse sits inside the glomerulus, a glial-wrapped tangle where one mossy-fibre rosette contacts many granule dendrites.

The inhibitory synapses use GABA acting on GABA-A receptors, placed on granule somata and dendrites; in the cerebellar glomerulus the Golgi terminal also drives a slow tonic GABA-A conductance that continuously sets threshold.

Characteristic weights are small and numerous, and the key plastic synapse in the dentate is the input-to-granule contact (NMDA-dependent long-term potentiation), while in the cerebellum the granule axon's downstream synapse onto the Purkinje cell carries the learning (see Chapter 35).


SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One dentate instance in a human hemisphere involves on the order of hundreds of thousands to a few million entorhinal input fibres fanning onto roughly fifteen million granule cells per hemisphere, a fan-out of several-fold to an order of magnitude.

One cerebellar functional instance (a patch of granule layer under a microzone) receives a few mossy-fibre channels and expands them across a local granule population numbering in the millions.

The unifying quantitative signature is that the active fraction of granule cells at any moment is low, on the order of one to five percent in the dentate and only a few percent in the cerebellum.
