The layer 5 ET body-commanding neuron plays the estimate unit for action: its bursting personality, triggered by agreement between basal evidence and apical expectation, makes it a literal coincidence detector of prediction and data, and its subcortical axon turns settled estimates into commands - perception and action minimising the same error.

The layer 6 CT input-tuning neuron plays the precision setter at the source: its slow, sparse, modulatory personality suits a cell whose job is to tell the thalamus which evidence to amplify before it even arrives.

The parvalbumin basket cell lends the prediction its minus sign at the soma and paces the gamma band in which errors are broadcast; its non-adapting speed keeps the subtraction current with the signal.

The somatostatin Martinotti cell subtracts predictions where they land, on the apical tufts, and its facilitating, slowly recruiting personality means the more insistently the column fires, the more firmly expectations press down - an automatic explaining-away.

The vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) interneuron implements attention's precision boost: by silencing the Martinotti and basket cells it releases the error units, which is the circuit-level meaning of attending to a channel.

The chandelier cell vetoes error emission at the axon initial segment, a final gate on which surprises are allowed to propagate.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

Ascending error edges are glutamatergic, alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA)-dominated and fast, consistent with their transient, high-frequency content.

Descending prediction edges are glutamatergic but N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA)-rich and slower, often targeting distal dendrites through voltage-dependent receptors - a fabric suited to sustained, modulatory expectation rather than punctate evidence.

The subtraction is implemented by gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-A synapses from basket cells at the soma and Martinotti synapses on the tuft, and precision weighting is carried by muscarinic and nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, alpha adrenergic receptors and dopamine D1 receptors that multiply gain rather than adding current.

Plasticity follows the error: spike-timing-dependent potentiation in superficial layers strengthens connections that transmit persistent errors, which in the theory is exactly how the generative model learns, and homeostatic scaling keeps mean error activity near a low set point.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One instance is one hierarchical level's loop within one column, on the order of 10,000 to 100,000 neurons, of which the error population in layers 2/3 numbers a few thousand and the estimate population in layers 5/6 a comparable few thousand.

A full perceptual stack, retina to inferotemporal cortex, chains 4 to 8 such levels with loop delays of 10 to 40 milliseconds per level.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

If the reading is correct, the count is the count of Chapter 37: one to two million column instances, organised into the dozen or so hierarchies (visual, auditory, somatic, interoceptive, motor) that anatomists have charted by laminar connection patterns.

Honest note: this is the book's most theory-laden chapter, and the confidence is moderate; the anatomy is settled, the mapping of error and estimate onto superficial and deep layers is supported but not proven, and rival readings of the same tile exist.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• The visual hierarchy from primary visual cortex through V2, V4 and inferotemporal cortex, where end-stopping and extra-classical surround suppression behave exactly like explained-away errors.

• The auditory hierarchy, where the mismatch negativity - a scalp potential at 100 to 250 milliseconds to any deviant sound - is the motif's most robust human signature.

• The somatosensory hierarchy, where predicted touch is attenuated, which is why you cannot tickle yourself.

• The motor hierarchy, where on the active-inference reading descending signals are predictions of proprioceptive input that reflexes then fulfil.

• The interoceptive hierarchy through the insula, where predictions about the body's internal state are held to underlie emotion.

• The frontal hierarchies, where slower, more abstract predictions - contexts, rules, narratives - sit at the top of the stack.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Without this motif each hierarchy would forward raw signal at full bandwidth, and the cortex would drown in the expected: predictive coding is the brain's compression scheme, spending spikes only on news.

Its regional colouring is visible as attenuation of the predicted (self-touch, one's own voice), as filling-in of the unsampled (the blind spot, occluded contours), and as illusion whenever a strong prior outvotes weak evidence - the hollow-mask illusion is the motif working correctly on misleading input.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

At each level: error equals precision times the difference of evidence and prediction, a subtractive comparison with multiplicative gain; estimate integrates ascending error minus descending constraint, a leaky integration.

The stack as a whole performs gradient descent on summed squared precision-weighted error, settling in 100 to 200 milliseconds for a static scene.

Quantitatively, predictable stimuli evoke responses reduced by roughly 30 to 50 percent in sensory cortex (repetition suppression), and unexpected omissions - input below prediction - evoke responses to nothing at all, the transformation's most diagnostic output.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

Errors travel upward fast and rhythmically in the gamma band, 30 to 80 hertz, from superficial layers; predictions travel downward in the alpha and beta bands, 8 to 30 hertz, from deep layers - a spectral asymmetry confirmed by laminar recordings in monkey and human.

A surprise produces a stereotyped cascade: early sensory response within 50 milliseconds, mismatch signal at 100 to 250 milliseconds, and, for globally rule-breaking events, a P300 wave near 300 to 400 milliseconds as the top of the stack revises.

Adaptation to a repeated stimulus - the error dying away over 2 to 5 presentations - is the motif's learning visible in real time.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

The normal regime is balanced inference, priors and evidence weighted by their true reliabilities.

Turn precision up on priors and the system hallucinates, perceiving what it expects; turn precision up on evidence and every repetition stays surprising, nothing ever becomes familiar.

Rapid eye movement dreaming is prediction running with the evidence stream gated off; ketamine and psychedelic states are pharmacological precision manipulations, ketamine blunting error via NMDA blockade and classical psychedelics loosening priors via serotonin 2A receptors on deep-layer pyramids.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

Learning is the slow half of the same descent: whatever error settling cannot remove, synaptic change absorbs, updating the generative model so tomorrow's prediction is better.

This makes the motif's learning rule locally Hebbian yet globally normative - each synapse adjusts by locally available pre- and postsynaptic activity, yet the ensemble descends a global objective, a trick artificial intelligence backpropagation achieves only with biologically awkward weight transport.

Precision itself is learned, as attention schemas and confidence calibration, largely through neuromodulatory plasticity.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

Sensory variants weight evidence heavily at the bottom of the stack; frontal variants weight priors and run slower.

Active inference is the motor variant, in which the error is cancelled by moving the body rather than revising the estimate.

Hierarchical temporal variants predict sequences rather than states, and interoceptive variants predict the body's milieu; rival formulations differ on whether errors are signed by separate populations or by deviations from baseline firing.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

The wiring assembles with the column (Chapter 37), but the generative model is installed by experience: infants show mismatch responses to sound deviants before birth is a month old, and priors deepen through childhood as the statistics of the world are absorbed.

The laminar asymmetry of feedforward and feedback connections emerges in the same developmental window that myelinates the long feedback fibres, and the slow maturation of prefrontal priors into the third decade parallels the slow maturation of judgement.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

Prediction is older than cortex: the retina already subtracts its own spatiotemporal predictions, and the cerebellum's forward models (Chapter 42 territory) predict the sensory consequences of action.

What the mammalian cortex added is stacked, learnable, bidirectional prediction - a hierarchy deep enough to predict causes of causes - and the human elaboration of its upper storeys may be why our species alone is routinely surprised by ideas.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

The motif inherits the column's glia and vasculature, with one specific dependence worth naming: precision signalling leans on the diffuse cholinergic and monoaminergic systems, so the health of the basal forebrain and locus coeruleus is the health of the brain's confidence estimates.

Astrocytes, which sense noradrenaline and gate synaptic gain, are increasingly implicated as cellular participants in precision itself.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Schizophrenia is the motif's flagship disorder on current theory: weakened or misweighted precision lets priors run unchecked (hallucination) and lets noise masquerade as news (delusion as learning from false surprise), and patients show reliably reduced mismatch negativity with effect sizes near 1 standard deviation, one of the most replicated biological findings in psychiatry.

Autism spectrum conditions are modelled as the opposite imbalance, over-precise evidence and shallow priors, matching sensory overwhelm and the insistence on sameness.

Functional neurological disorders are read as over-precise priors seizing the motor and interoceptive stacks, and chronic pain as a pain prior that evidence can no longer revise.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ Ascending evidence from the level below, gamma-band spiking into layer 4, loop delay 10 to 40 milliseconds per level.

◦ Descending predictions from the level above, alpha and beta band, onto layer 1 tufts and layer 6.

◦ Precision signals: acetylcholine, noradrenaline and dopamine levels, plus attentional VIP disinhibition, multiplying error gain by roughly 0.5 to 2.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ Precision-weighted prediction error, upward from layers 2/3, transient, sparse and news-only.

◦ Predictions, downward from layers 5/6, sustained, and to subcortical effectors as action commands.

• STATE.

◦ Current estimate vector per level, residual error vector, precision weights, and the slow synaptic state that is the generative model itself.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Learning rate on estimates roughly 0.05 to 0.5 per iteration equivalent; 4 to 8 levels per stack; repetition suppression 30 to 50 percent; mismatch negativity latency 100 to 250 milliseconds.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Error transmission under 10 milliseconds; perceptual settling 100 to 200 milliseconds; adaptation over 2 to 5 repetitions; model learning hours to decades.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Psychosis under aberrant precision, with reduced mismatch negativity in schizophrenia; sensory overload profiles in autism spectrum conditions; ketamine-induced dissociation as pharmacological error blockade.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

Propose the module name predictive_coding_error_minimiser.

Each instance subscribes to an ascending_evidence topic and a descending_prediction topic plus a precision_weight topic, and publishes a prediction_error_message upward and a prediction_message downward; a stack of instances is a perception service.

The closest artificial intelligence analogues are the variational autoencoder and diffusion-style iterative denoising, and modern predictive-coding networks provably approximate backpropagation with purely local rules; the biological motif differs in running inference and learning simultaneously and continuously, in weighting every message by learned confidence, and in cancelling some errors with muscles instead of mathematics.

Konnectome should treat precision as a first-class message field, because most of the interesting failure modes live there.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to run a two-level predictive coding loop that perceives an input by minimising prediction error.
Create a number variable called evidence holding the sensory input value.
Create a number variable called estimate with initial value 0.
Create a number variable called prior with the higher level's expectation as its value.
Create a number variable called sensory error with initial value 0.
Create a number variable called prior error with initial value 0.
Create a number variable called sensory precision with initial value 1.
Create a number variable called prior precision with initial value 0.5.
Create a number variable called learning rate with initial value 0.2.
Repeat the following actions until the errors become negligibly small.
    Calculate the difference of evidence and estimate.
    Multiply the result by sensory precision.
    Set sensory error to the result.
    Calculate the difference of estimate and prior.
    Multiply the result by prior precision.
    Set prior error to the result.
    Calculate the difference of sensory error and prior error.
    Multiply the result by learning rate.
    Add the result to estimate.
    Publish sensory error to the level above.
    Publish estimate to the level below as the new prediction.
End the repetition block.
The perceived value is the final value of estimate.
The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because gradient descent on prediction error is a five-line loop, and printing the error each step shows perception literally settling.

# Two-level predictive coding: an estimate (deep layers) is revised
# until precision-weighted prediction errors (superficial layers)
# vanish (Rao & Ballard, Nat Neurosci 1999; Bastos et al., Neuron 2012).
def perceive(evidence, prior, pi_sens=1.0, pi_prior=0.5,
             rate=0.2, steps=25):
    estimate = 0.0
    for t in range(steps):
        e_sens = pi_sens * (evidence - estimate)    # L2/3 error, upward
        e_prior = pi_prior * (estimate - prior)     # error against prior
        estimate += rate * (e_sens - e_prior)       # deep-layer update
        if t % 4 == 0:
            print(f"t={t:2d}  estimate={estimate:6.3f}  "
                  f"sensory_error={e_sens:7.3f}")
    return estimate

print("balanced precision - percept lands between evidence and prior:")
p = perceive(evidence=1.0, prior=0.2)
print(f"settled percept: {p:.3f}  (Bayesian blend of 1.0 and 0.2)")
print()
print("prior precision cranked up - the circuit 'hallucinates' its prior:")
p = perceive(evidence=1.0, prior=0.2, pi_prior=5.0)
print(f"settled percept: {p:.3f}  (dragged toward the expectation)")

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

A hierarchy in which the fast, shallow, gamma-carrying channel runs upward bearing only what was not foreseen, while the slow, deep, beta-carrying channel runs downward bearing the forecast - find a stack whose upward traffic dies away exactly as its guesses improve, and you have found the expectation-correcting circuit, whether in a cortex or in a machine.


CHAPTER 39. THE THALAMIC RELAY TRIAD WITH RETICULAR GATE (Relay-Interneuron-Reticular Composite) (The Searchlight Gate) (COG)

Every sense you have, save smell, reaches your cortex through one narrow doorway, and this chapter is the circuit of the doorkeeper.

The thalamus is not a cable: each of its relay cells sits inside a three-way synaptic knot with a local interneuron, and the whole relay sheet is wrapped in a thin shell of inhibitory neurons - the thalamic reticular nucleus - that listens to every message passing in either direction and answers with silence, aimed.

Francis Crick, in 1984, guessed that this shell steers an attentional searchlight, brightening the relays the cortex cares about and dimming the rest; forty years of experiment have largely agreed.

The same gate, closed rhythmically, is what disconnects the cortex from the world every night: sleep is this circuit's other setting.

Searchlight names Crick's image, attention as a beam steered across the relay sheet.

Gate names the mechanism, transmission granted or withheld by inhibition, and honours its second duty as the gate of sleep.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

The motif is a composite of three cell roles: the thalamocortical relay neuron, which receives a driving input (from retina, medial lemniscus, inferior colliculus, cerebellum or cortical layer 5) and projects it to cortex; the local GABAergic (gamma-aminobutyric acid releasing) interneuron, which forms an unusual dendrodendritic triad with the driver and the relay dendrite; and the neurons of the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN), a shield-shaped sheet of purely inhibitory cells wrapped around the thalamus, through which every thalamocortical and corticothalamic axon passes and leaves an excitatory copy.

Its computation is selective, state-dependent gating with gain control: the triad linearises and sharpens each relayed signal in time, and the reticular shell, steered chiefly by cortical layer 6, selects which relays transmit faithfully (tonic mode), which respond only with exclamatory bursts (burst mode) and which fall silent.

It is the physical implementation of selective attention at the brain's input stage, and, run rhythmically, the implementation of sensory disconnection in sleep.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The node roles are driver terminal, relay cell, local interneuron, reticular cell and cortical layer 6 feedback.

The driver terminal makes a strong excitatory glutamatergic synapse on the proximal dendrite of the relay cell; in the same encapsulated glomerulus - a synaptic cluster wrapped in glial sheet - the same driver terminal excites a dendritic terminal of the local interneuron (an F2 terminal), and that interneuron dendrite makes an inhibitory GABAergic synapse onto the very same relay dendrite: three synapses, one knot, the triad.

The interneuron also inhibits the relay cell conventionally through its axon (F1 terminals), and interneurons couple to each other by gap junctions.

The reticular cell receives excitatory collaterals from the relay cell's axon on its way to cortex and from cortical layer 6 axons on their way back, and sends an inhibitory GABAergic projection onto relay cells, with a centre-surround flavour: a relay's own reticular sector inhibits it and its neighbours, so active channels can suppress rivals through the shell.

Reticular cells inhibit one another through GABAergic synapses and synchronise through connexin 36 gap junctions.

Cortical layer 6 excites both relay and reticular cells (modulatory, ten-to-one over the driver in synapse count), and brainstem arousal fibres - acetylcholine, noradrenaline, serotonin, histamine - depolarise relay cells and hyperpolarise or retune reticular cells, setting the mode of the whole gate.

The topology is thus a feedforward line (driver to relay to cortex) crossed by two inhibitory loops, a fast local one through the interneuron and a longer selective one through the reticular shell, with the cortex holding the steering wheel of the second.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The thalamocortical relay neuron of the neuron catalogue is the star, and its personality is the famous two-mode switch: depolarised, it relays faithfully, spike for spike; hyperpolarised for 100 milliseconds or more, its low-threshold T-type calcium channels de-inactivate and the next input triggers a 2 to 7 spike burst riding a calcium crest - a wake-up call rather than a message.

The thalamic local interneuron is the oddity of the cast: its dendrites are also outputs, releasing GABA from F2 terminals without any spike, so it computes locally, synapse by synapse; its personality of distributed, graded, spikeless processing gives each relay dendrite its own private gain control and keeps relay transfer near linear.

The reticular neuron is a dedicated inhibitory specialist with even stronger burst personality than the relay cell - its T-type channels make it a rhythmic machine-gunner - and its position athwart both directions of traffic makes it the only cell in the motif that reads the conversation both ways; it is, in Crick's phrase, ideally placed to steer the searchlight.

The cortical layer 6 corticothalamic (CT) input-tuning neuron of Chapter 37 completes the cast from outside: slow, sparse and modulatory, it whispers gain and focus instructions to relay and shell alike, closing the loop that lets the cortex tune its own input.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

Driver synapses are glutamatergic, large, multi-release-site, proximal, depressing, acting on alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) and N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors - few in number (a handful of retinal axons per geniculate relay cell) but contributing the message itself.

Layer 6 feedback synapses are glutamatergic, small, distal, facilitating, with strong metabotropic glutamate receptor components - vastly more numerous but individually faint, the anatomy of modulation.

The triad's inhibitory synapses (F2 dendrodendritic) and the interneuron's axonal F1 synapses use GABA-A receptors; reticular synapses onto relay cells use GABA-A plus slower GABA-B, whose 100 to 200 millisecond inhibition is precisely what primes T-type burst.

Gap junctions of connexin 36 knit both the interneuron and reticular populations; brainstem modulators act through muscarinic, adrenergic and histamine receptors that close or open resting potassium leak channels, sliding the relay between modes.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One triad occupies a single glomerulus a few micrometres across; one relay channel - a relay cell, its share of interneuron dendrites and its reticular sector - spans perhaps 100 to 300 micrometres.

The human lateral geniculate nucleus holds roughly 1 to 1.5 million relay neurons; the whole human thalamus holds on the order of 10 million neurons per side, of which interneurons are 20 to 30 percent in most human nuclei (unlike rodents, where most nuclei lack them), and the reticular shell wraps the lot in a sheet a few hundred micrometres thick.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

Counting relay channels, the motif is installed on the order of 10 million times per hemisphere, once for every relay neuron of every thalamic nucleus.

Distribution is universal across the thalamus but graded: triads are rich in first-order sensory nuclei (visual, somatosensory) and sparser in some higher-order and motor territories, while the reticular gate covers every nucleus without exception.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• The lateral geniculate nucleus, gating vision; the classic triad territory and the site of Crick's original searchlight.

• The medial geniculate nucleus, gating hearing on the way to auditory cortex.

• The ventral posterior nuclei, gating touch, proprioception and taste from the body and face.

• The ventral anterior and ventral lateral nuclei, gating basal ganglia and cerebellar traffic to motor cortex.

• The pulvinar, the huge higher-order nucleus relaying cortex to cortex, where the gate arbitrates between cortical areas rather than between senses.

• The mediodorsal nucleus, gating limbic and prefrontal traffic, implicated in schizophrenia.

• The anterior nuclei, gating the hippocampal-mammillary memory circuit.

• The intralaminar and midline nuclei, the arousal-and-consciousness channels, whose gating helps set whether there is any experience at all.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Without the triad, relay would be raw: transfer would saturate, temporal precision would blur, and the cortex would receive a louder but stupider copy of the senses.

Without the reticular gate, everything would transmit always - no attentional selection at the source, no spindles, no sensory disconnection - and sleep as we know it, with the cortex talking to itself behind a closed door, would be impossible.

For every cortical area of Chapter 37, this motif decides what its layer 4 gets to hear; it is the volume knob and the channel selector of the entire thalamocortical system.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

In tonic mode the transformation is approximately linear with divisive gain control: relay output tracks driver input spike for spike at 30 to 90 percent transfer ratio, the triad subtracting a scaled copy of the input's own recent history, which sharpens timing to millisecond precision and emphasises change.

In burst mode the transformation is a thresholded differentiator: sustained input is ignored, but an input arriving after 100 or more milliseconds of inhibition fires a 2 to 7 spike, 150 to 400 hertz burst - low fidelity, high detectability.

The reticular loop imposes selection across channels: attended channels run tonic at raised gain (attention modulates geniculate transmission by roughly 10 to 30 percent in primates), unattended channels are damped, and in deep sleep rhythmic reticular volleys drive the whole sheet through spindle and slow oscillations, transfer falling toward zero.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

Retina to cortex through this gate costs only a few milliseconds; the triad's disynaptic inhibition arrives about 1 millisecond after the excitation it tracks.

The signature rhythm is the sleep spindle, 11 to 16 hertz waxing-and-waning volleys lasting 0.5 to 3 seconds, born in the reticular nucleus and sculpted by the reticular-relay loop; the delta rhythm of deep sleep, 1 to 4 hertz, emerges when relays hyperpolarise further.

The pathological signature is the 3 hertz spike-and-wave of absence epilepsy, the same loop resonating in daylight.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

Waking is the open regime: brainstem modulators depolarise relays into tonic mode and the gate applies graded, attention-steered gain.

Drowsiness and non-rapid-eye-movement sleep progressively close it: spindles at sleep onset, then delta, then the slow oscillation, each stage a deeper rhythmic lockdown of transfer.

Burst firing is not sleep's property alone - occasional wake bursts flag novel stimuli for attention, an exclamation mark before the prose - and general anaesthetics hyperpolarise the same relays, closing the gate pharmacologically.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

The gate's synapses are plastic on several timescales: driver synapses show short-term depression that adapts transfer within tens of milliseconds, layer 6 feedback synapses facilitate and undergo long-term plasticity, and reticular synapses are remodelled by experience and by sleep itself.

Spindles are not idle: they gate calcium into cortical dendrites and are among the best-evidenced physiological vehicles of sleep-dependent memory consolidation, so this motif participates in writing memory, not merely in guarding input.

Developmental plasticity is dramatic - retinal waves drive segregation of eye-specific geniculate layers before vision begins.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

First-order variants relay the world (retina, lemniscus, colliculus); higher-order variants such as the pulvinar relay cortex to cortex, their drivers being cortical layer 5, making the thalamus an obligatory way-station even inside cortical conversation.

The interneuron-rich human pattern contrasts with rodent nuclei that outsource all inhibition to the reticular shell; magnocellular, parvocellular and koniocellular geniculate channels run the motif at different gains and speeds.

The reticular nucleus itself is subdivided into sensory sectors, each a crude map of its nucleus, plus limbic sectors with distinct spindle behaviour.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

Relay nuclei arise from the diencephalic thalamic anlage while reticular cells arise separately from the prethalamus, and the two must find each other as thalamocortical axons grow through the reticular sheet in a handshake with corticothalamic axons descending the other way.

Spontaneous retinal waves, before any vision, sculpt the geniculate; triads assemble postnatally as interneuron dendrites invade the glomeruli.

Spindles appear in the electroencephalogram by about 2 months after birth, evidence the gate's rhythmic machinery matures early.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

The thalamus is ancient vertebrate equipment, present in fish and amphibians, but the reticular shell in its full form and the burst-tonic switch are amniote elaborations that flowered with cortex itself.

The searchlight is thus younger than the doorway: as cortex grew and its areas multiplied, the shell that samples all its traffic became the natural arbiter of what deserves cortical audience, and the human expansion of the pulvinar - gating cortex to cortex - tracks the expansion of association cortex it serves.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

The glomerulus is a glial invention as much as a neuronal one: astrocytic sheets wrap each triad, containing its glutamate and GABA and defining its privacy.

Relay axons are heavily myelinated for speed; the thalamus's blood supply through the posterior circulation is famously vulnerable, and bilateral paramedian thalamic stroke can abolish consciousness outright - the clearest lesion evidence that these gates carry it.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Absence epilepsy is the gate's signature disease: GABA-B-primed T-type bursts lock the reticular-relay loop into 3 hertz spike-and-wave, and the child simply stops, awake but absent, for seconds at a time; T-type calcium channel blockers such as ethosuximide treat it by disarming the burst.

Schizophrenia shows reduced sleep spindles and reticular abnormalities, a candidate mechanism for its sensory gating deficits; fatal familial insomnia destroys anterior and mediodorsal thalamus and with it sleep itself.

Thalamocortical dysrhythmia - relays stuck in burst - is implicated in central pain, tinnitus and tremor, and general anaesthesia and disorders of consciousness converge on this gate from opposite directions.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ Driver input: a handful of axons (for example 1 to 5 retinal ganglion axons per geniculate relay), strong, proximal, depressing.

◦ Cortical layer 6 feedback: thousands of weak facilitating synapses, roughly 10 times the driver count, latency 5 to 15 milliseconds.

◦ Reticular inhibition: GABA-A and GABA-B, 100 to 200 millisecond envelopes.

◦ Brainstem state broadcast: acetylcholine, noradrenaline, histamine, serotonin, setting resting potential over a roughly 10 to 15 millivolt range.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ Tonic relay to cortical layer 4 at 30 to 90 percent transfer, millisecond precision.

◦ Burst exclamations of 2 to 7 spikes at 150 to 400 hertz.

◦ Excitatory copies of all traffic to the reticular sheet.

• STATE.

◦ Relay membrane potential and mode flag (tonic versus burst), T-type channel de-inactivation level, reticular sector activity map, spindle phase, arousal level.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Mode threshold near minus 65 to minus 70 millivolts; T-type de-inactivation requires roughly 100 milliseconds below threshold; attentional gain change 10 to 30 percent; spindle band 11 to 16 hertz.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Relay latency 1 to 2 milliseconds; triadic inhibition lag about 1 millisecond; GABA-B inhibition 100 to 200 milliseconds; spindle waxing 0.5 to 3 seconds; sleep cycle about 90 minutes.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Absence epilepsy's 3 hertz spike-and-wave; spindle deficits in schizophrenia; thalamocortical dysrhythmia in central pain and tinnitus; loss of consciousness in bilateral paramedian thalamic stroke.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

Propose the module name thalamic_relay_attention_gate.

It subscribes to a driving_sense_data topic, a cortical_feedback_tuning topic and a global_arousal_state topic, and publishes a gated_sense_data topic to the matching canonical_cortical_column_processor instances plus a salience_burst_flag topic when a silenced channel is struck by strong input.

The closest artificial intelligence analogues are the attention gate and the mixture-of-experts router - learned multiplicative selection of which inputs reach the expensive processor - but the biological gate differs in being steered by its own consumer (cortex tunes its own input stream), in having a hard offline setting used nightly for consolidation, and in signalling novelty on closed channels by a distinct burst code rather than by silence.

Konnectome should implement the sleep setting; an architecture that can never close its gates can never consolidate in peace.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to gate several sensory channels through thalamic relays whose reticular inhibition, steered by cortical attention, selects which channel transmits faithfully, and which relays answer strong input only with an alerting burst.
Create a list variable called channel inputs holding the current driver signal of each sensory channel.
Create a list variable called attention weights holding the cortical layer six attention value for each channel, between 0 and 1.
Create a list variable called membrane potentials holding one relay membrane potential per channel, each starting at the waking resting value.
Create a number variable called burst threshold with the value of the hyperpolarised boundary between tonic mode and burst mode.
Repeat the following actions for each channel in the list of channels.
    Calculate the difference of 1 and the channel's attention weight.
    Multiply the result by the maximum reticular inhibition strength.
    Subtract the result from the channel's membrane potential to obtain the gated potential.
    If the gated potential is above burst threshold, then perform the following actions.
        Multiply the channel's input by the channel's attention weight.
        Publish the result to the cortex as faithful tonic relay for this channel.
    Otherwise, perform the following actions.
        If the channel's input is greater than the salience threshold, then perform the following actions.
            Publish a fixed burst message to the cortex as an alert for this channel.
        Otherwise, perform the following actions.
            Publish nothing for this channel.
        End the conditional block.
    End the conditional block.
End the repetition block.
The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because a gate over parallel channels is a natural loop over a list, and the tonic, silent and burst outcomes print as three legible rows.

# Thalamic relay with reticular gate: cortex-steered inhibition selects
# which channels relay tonically; hyperpolarised relays answer strong
# input only with T-type bursts (Crick, PNAS 1984; Sherman & Guillery,
# Exploring the Thalamus 2006).
REST, BURST_THRESH = -60.0, -68.0   # millivolts
MAX_INHIB = 12.0                    # mV of reticular hyperpolarisation
SALIENCE = 0.8                      # drive needed to burst through

def reticular_gate(inputs, attention):
    out = []
    for drive, attn in zip(inputs, attention):
        v = REST - (1.0 - attn) * MAX_INHIB      # unattended -> inhibited
        if v > BURST_THRESH:                     # tonic mode: faithful
            out.append(("tonic", round(drive * attn, 2)))
        elif drive > SALIENCE:                   # burst mode: alert only
            out.append(("burst", 5))             # stereotyped 5-spike call
        else:
            out.append(("silent", 0))            # gate closed
    return out

inputs = [0.6, 0.6, 0.9]                    # three equal-ish scenes
print("attention on channel 0:",
      reticular_gate(inputs, attention=[1.0, 0.1, 0.1]))
print("attention on channel 1:",
      reticular_gate(inputs, attention=[0.1, 1.0, 0.1]))
print("asleep (no attention)  :",
      reticular_gate(inputs, attention=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0]))

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

A relay wrapped in the only sheet of neurons that reads traffic in both directions and answers everything with aimed inhibition, a three-synapse knot in which a dendrite is also an output, and a two-mode cell that switches nightly from messenger to metronome - find the circuit that is at once attention's searchlight and sleep's closed door, and you have found the thalamic gate.


CHAPTER 40. THE BASAL GANGLIA SELECTION MOTIF (Disinhibitory Channel-Release Composite) (The Permission Machine) (COG)

Every action you might take at this moment is already prepared somewhere in your cortex, and every one of them is being held down by a continuous, tonic clamp of inhibition.

The basal ganglia do not command movement; they grant permission, lifting the clamp from exactly one prepared channel while pressing harder on all the rest.

A direct pathway says go to the chosen channel, an indirect pathway says stay down to its competitors, and a hyperdirect line can shout stop to everything at once, all of it tutored by dopamine's running commentary on how the last choice turned out.

Permission names the logic: nothing happens by excitation here, only by the selective removal of a standing veto.

Machine names the scale: this is winner-take-all built not from three cells but from five nuclei and hundreds of millions of neurons, replicated across parallel loops for movement, gaze, habit, and thought.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

The basal ganglia selection motif is a composite microcircuit spanning the striatum, the external and internal segments of the globus pallidus, the subthalamic nucleus, the substantia nigra, and the thalamus, and it computes action selection: given many candidate channels of activity, release exactly one from tonic inhibition while deepening the inhibition of the rest.

It is the outline's winner-take-all motif (entry 16) rebuilt at composite scale, with the crucial inversion that the default state is all channels off, so that selection is disinhibition rather than excitation.

Because dopamine adjusts the ease of future selections according to reward, the same circuit is simultaneously the brain's choosing machine and its habit-forming machine.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The node roles are the cortical candidate channels, the striatal input layer split into a direct population and an indirect population, an external pallidal relay, a subthalamic amplifier, an output layer formed by the internal pallidal segment together with the substantia nigra pars reticulata, the thalamic target, and the dopaminergic teacher in the substantia nigra pars compacta.

Cortex projects excitatory glutamatergic edges onto both striatal populations and, by the hyperdirect edge, straight onto the subthalamic nucleus.

The direct striatal population sends a monosynaptic inhibitory gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) edge to the output layer, which itself holds a tonic inhibitory edge onto the thalamus, so two inhibitions in series make a disinhibition: cortical drive through the direct path releases the thalamus.

The indirect striatal population sends an inhibitory edge to the external pallidum, which sends inhibitory edges to the subthalamic nucleus and to the output layer; the subthalamic nucleus sends a divergent excitatory edge back to both pallidal segments, so cortical drive through the indirect path ultimately excites the output layer and deepens thalamic inhibition.

The hyperdirect edge from cortex to subthalamic nucleus reaches the output layer in one excitatory synapse, faster than either striatal route, and broadcasts a brief global brake.

The pars compacta sends dopaminergic paracrine edges onto both striatal populations with opposite signs of effect, and the thalamus closes the loop with an excitatory edge back to the originating cortex.

Topologically the whole graph is a set of parallel channels sharing one broad subthalamic stop signal, a focused centre of disinhibition inside a surround of deepened inhibition.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The direct-pathway medium spiny neuron of the neuron catalogue, bearing the D1 dopamine receptor, plays the go role; its personality is a deeply hyperpolarised down state near minus 85 millivolts from which it must be lifted by convergent cortical evidence into an up state before it fires at all, making each striatal vote a coincidence-detected, evidence-thresholded event rather than a reflex.

The indirect-pathway medium spiny neuron, bearing the D2 receptor, is anatomically its twin and plays the stay-down role, and its slightly higher intrinsic excitability biases the resting circuit toward suppression, which is why the default answer of the basal ganglia is no.

The external pallidal prototypic neuron is a fast tonic pacemaker near 60 spikes per second whose personality turns the indirect pathway into a subtractive relay: striatal votes are read out as pauses in its unceasing firing.

The subthalamic projection neuron is likewise an autonomous pacemaker at 20 to 30 spikes per second with rebound-burst tendencies, a personality that makes the stop signal fast, diffuse, and prone to oscillation when its pallidal partner is disturbed.

The output neurons of the internal pallidum and the substantia nigra pars reticulata are relentless tonic pacemakers at 60 to 80 spikes per second, and this personality is the whole point: the clamp never needs to be commanded, because these cells inhibit the thalamus by default and forever unless actively paused.

The dopaminergic neuron of the pars compacta, the slow broadcasting teacher of the neuron catalogue, fires tonically near 4 spikes per second with phasic bursts and dips that encode reward prediction error, and its slow, volume-transmitting personality suits a signal meant to grade every channel at once rather than address any single synapse.

The cholinergic striatal interneuron, the tonically active giant of the catalogue, pauses precisely when dopamine bursts, and that pause opens the plasticity window; the parvalbumin fast-spiking striatal interneuron enforces feedforward timing on the spiny cells.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

Corticostriatal synapses are glutamatergic, landing on the spines of medium spiny neurons through alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) and N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors, with roughly 5,000 to 15,000 spines per cell and individually weak weights so that tens of coincident inputs are needed to reach threshold.

All striatal, pallidal, and nigral projection synapses use GABA on GABA-A receptors, placed on somata and proximal dendrites for strong division of the target's firing.

Dopamine acts through G-protein-coupled D1 receptors, which raise the excitability and plasticity of direct-pathway spines, and D2 receptors, which lower those of indirect-pathway spines, released largely by volume transmission into the extracellular space rather than at addressed synapses.

The plasticity rule is three-factor: corticostriatal weights change only when presynaptic activity, postsynaptic depolarisation, and a dopamine burst or dip coincide within about one second, the eligibility-trace window.

Gap junctions couple striatal parvalbumin interneurons through connexin-36, synchronising the feedforward brake.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One functional channel is on the order of a cortical column's worth of input mapped onto a few thousand spiny neurons converging roughly 100 to 1 onto tens of output pallidal neurons.

The full human apparatus contains roughly 100 million striatal neurons, about 95 percent of them medium spiny neurons, funnelling onto only about 160,000 internal pallidal neurons in each hemisphere, one of the sharpest convergences in the brain.

A single selection episode spans roughly 15 to 30 milliseconds from cortical drive to thalamic release.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

There is one basal ganglia apparatus per hemisphere, but it runs at least five largely parallel loops - motor, oculomotor, dorsolateral prefrontal, lateral orbitofrontal, and limbic - and within each loop the channel structure repeats for every selectable option, so the motif as a selection template is instantiated thousands of times across the two hemispheres.

Confidence in the loop count is moderate; the segregation is real but the borders between loops leak by design, which is how motivation reaches movement.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• The dorsal striatum (caudate nucleus and putamen), the input layer where cortical candidates are voted on.

• The ventral striatum (nucleus accumbens), where the same diagram selects among goals and appetites rather than movements.

• The globus pallidus, external and internal segments, the relay and output clamps.

• The subthalamic nucleus, the hyperdirect brake and pacemaker amplifier.

• The substantia nigra, pars reticulata as a second output clamp governing gaze and orienting, pars compacta as the dopamine teacher.

• The ventral anterior and ventral lateral thalamus and the mediodorsal thalamus, the clamped targets whose release is the motif's product.

• The superior colliculus, released by the pars reticulata to permit each saccadic eye movement.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Without this motif the frontal cortex would keep every plan it generates: nothing would rank the candidates, and behaviour would be either frozen by the unrelieved clamp or fragmented by all channels running at once.

The thalamus would lose its gatekeeper for action just as surely as the reticular nucleus gates it for sensation.

The colliculus would never receive permission to look, and the limbic loop would never convert wanting into pursuit.

Parkinson's disease is the experiment nature runs: remove the dopamine bias and the same tissue reweights toward the indirect pathway, and the person's intentions remain intact while permission is withheld.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

The transfer function is a biased winner-take-all implemented by double inhibition: output channel firing equals tonic rate minus direct-path votes plus indirect-path and subthalamic drive, and the thalamic channel whose output clamp is pushed below roughly 40 percent of its tonic rate escapes into activity.

Selection is therefore threshold-linear on the difference between a channel's own evidence and the pooled evidence of its competitors, with dopamine multiplying the gain of the go term and dividing the gain of the no-go term.

The hyperdirect term is a fast global additive brake with about a 5 to 8 millisecond lead over the striatal routes.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

Hyperdirect stop signals arrive at the output layer in 5 to 8 milliseconds, direct-path release in 15 to 20 milliseconds, and indirect-path suppression in 25 to 30 milliseconds, so each selection is a stereotyped triphasic sequence: brake, release, sculpt.

Dopamine prediction-error bursts last 100 to 200 milliseconds, and the eligibility window for learning extends about one second behind each action.

The healthy circuit shows broadband desynchronised firing; excessive beta-band oscillation at 13 to 30 cycles per second is its signature of failure.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

The motif runs in a deliberative regime, where selection is slow, dopamine-sensitive, and goal-directed through the associative loop, and a habitual regime, where overtrained corticostriatal weights in the sensorimotor loop select without deliberation.

Low dopamine tips the whole apparatus into a hypokinetic regime of raised selection thresholds, and excess dopamine into a hyperkinetic regime where weak candidates win.

During sleep the loops disengage from behaviour but continue to replay, consolidating the day's selections into skill.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

Corticostriatal synapses undergo dopamine-gated long-term potentiation and depression with opposite signs in the two pathways: a dopamine burst strengthens active direct-path synapses and weakens active indirect-path synapses, teaching the circuit to repeat rewarded selections, and a dip does the reverse.

This is reinforcement learning in tissue, the temporal-difference algorithm's actor trained by the pars compacta's critic.

Habit formation is the slow transfer of a learned policy from the dopamine-hungry associative loop to the automatised sensorimotor loop.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

The dorsal motor variant selects movements; the oculomotor variant, exiting through the pars reticulata to the colliculus, selects gaze targets; the prefrontal variant selects working-memory contents and strategies; the limbic variant, with the accumbens as striatum and the ventral pallidum as clamp, selects goals.

A patch-and-matrix microvariant tiles the striatum itself, the patches talking preferentially to the dopamine teacher and the matrix to the output clamps.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

Medium spiny neurons are born in the lateral ganglionic eminence and migrate radially into the striatum, choosing direct or indirect identity under transcription factors before birth, while pallidal and subthalamic neurons arise from separate hypothalamic and eminential sources.

Dopamine axons arrive early and their innervation matures through adolescence, which is one reason adolescent selection favours reward over caution.

The loops myelinate and segregate through childhood, and habit circuitry matures last.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

The motif is at least as old as the lamprey, in which every component nucleus, both pathways, and the dopamine bias are already present and already used to select among locomotor programs, making this perhaps the most conserved large circuit in the vertebrate brain, on the order of 560 million years old.

Evolution scaled its input layer with the cortex it serves but never redesigned the diagram, a strong hint that disinhibitory selection is close to optimal for the problem.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Striatal astrocytes clear glutamate and dopamine and shape the eligibility window; oligodendrocytes myelinate the hyperdirect and pallidothalamic axons whose speed the triphasic sequence depends on.

The striatum is among the most energy-hungry structures per gram in the brain because tonic pacemaking never rests, and its dense capillary bed and iron-rich metabolism make the pallidum visibly dark in imaging.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Parkinson's disease is degeneration of the pars compacta teacher, with symptoms appearing after roughly 50 to 60 percent of nigral dopamine neurons are lost: selection thresholds rise, movements shrink, and pathological beta oscillation locks the pallidal-subthalamic loop.

Huntington's disease kills indirect-pathway spiny neurons first, releasing competitors into chorea, the anti-Parkinsonian failure.

Deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus treats Parkinsonism by jamming the oscillating stop line.

Tourette syndrome, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and addiction are each, in circuit terms, selection faults: tics as unwanted winners, compulsions as un-cancellable selections, addiction as a dopamine teacher hijacked into overvaluing one channel.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ Cortical candidate activity from essentially all of frontal cortex and much of parietal and temporal cortex, glutamatergic, converging tens of thousands of axons per spiny neuron.

◦ Thalamic intralaminar input announcing salient events, 5 to 15 percent of striatal excitation.

◦ Dopamine prediction-error signal from the pars compacta, tonic near 4 spikes per second, phasic bursts to 20 spikes per second and dips to 0.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ Tonic GABAergic clamp of 60 to 80 spikes per second onto motor and prefrontal thalamus and superior colliculus, with selection expressed as pauses of 50 to 200 milliseconds in single channels.

• STATE.

◦ Per-channel corticostriatal weight vectors, up-down state of each spiny population, pallidal and subthalamic tonic rates, current dopamine tone.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Spiny neuron down state minus 85 millivolts and threshold near minus 45 millivolts; output tonic rate 60 to 80 spikes per second; convergence roughly 100 million striatal neurons onto roughly 160,000 internal pallidal neurons per hemisphere.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Hyperdirect latency 5 to 8 milliseconds; direct-path release 15 to 20 milliseconds; indirect sculpting 25 to 30 milliseconds; dopamine burst 100 to 200 milliseconds; eligibility trace about 1 second; habit consolidation weeks.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Parkinson's disease: dopamine loss, rigidity, bradykinesia, pathological 13 to 30 cycle per second beta synchrony.

◦ Huntington's disease: indirect-path loss, chorea.

◦ Addiction and obsessive-compulsive disorder: mis-taught or stuck selection.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

Propose the module name tonic_inhibition_action_selector, subscribing to candidate_action_proposals, salience_events, and reward_prediction_error, and publishing selected_action_channel plus a global_stop signal.

The closest artificial intelligence analogue is an actor-critic reinforcement-learning agent whose policy head ends in a softmax, but the biological motif differs in defaulting to all-off, selecting by removing inhibition rather than adding activation, and running a separate fast stop line that can veto after the race has started - a feature most artificial agents lack and demonstrably need.

The three-factor eligibility-trace rule is also more local and cheaper than backpropagation, and konnectome should implement it as such.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to select one action channel from several by disinhibition, with dopamine biasing the go and no-go votes.
Create a number variable called tonic clamp with initial value 70.
Create a number variable called dopamine with initial value 1.0.
Create a list variable called cortical evidence with initial values 30, 55, 40.
Create an empty list variable called output rates.
Create a number variable called total evidence with initial value 0.
For each value in cortical evidence, add the value to total evidence.
For each channel index from 1 to the length of cortical evidence, perform the following actions.
    Calculate the product of dopamine and the channel's cortical evidence, and call it the go vote.
    Calculate the difference of total evidence and the channel's cortical evidence.
    Divide the result by dopamine, and call it the no go vote.
    Calculate the value of tonic clamp minus the go vote plus one fifth of the no go vote.
    If the result is less than 0 is true, then perform the following actions.
        Set the result to 0.
    End the conditional block.
    Append the result to output rates.
End the loop.
For each channel index from 1 to the length of output rates, perform the following actions.
    If the channel's output rate is less than 40 percent of tonic clamp is true, then perform the following actions.
        Display the channel index and the word released to the console.
    Otherwise, perform the following actions.
        Display the channel index and the word clamped to the console.
    End the conditional block.
End the loop.
The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because the essence here is a race among a handful of numbers under a bias, and Python lets the race, the bias, and the verdict fit on one screen.

# Basal ganglia selection: channels released from tonic inhibition,
# direct path (go) scaled up by dopamine, indirect path (no-go) scaled down
# (Albin, Young & Penney 1989; Mink 1996; Frank 2005, J Cogn Neurosci).
TONIC = 70.0          # spikes/s, GPi/SNr pacemaker clamp
RELEASE = 0.4 * TONIC # thalamus escapes below 40% of tonic rate

def select(evidence, dopamine):
    total = sum(evidence)
    rates = []
    for e in evidence:
        go = dopamine * e                       # D1 direct path vote
        no_go = (total - e) / dopamine * 0.2    # D2 surround suppression
        rates.append(max(0.0, TONIC - go + no_go))
    winners = [i for i, r in enumerate(rates) if r < RELEASE]
    return rates, winners

evidence = [30.0, 55.0, 40.0]                   # cortical candidate drive
for da, label in [(1.0, "normal dopamine"),
                  (0.4, "parkinsonian dopamine"),
                  (1.8, "excess dopamine")]:
    rates, winners = select(evidence, da)
    print(f"{label:22s} GPi rates {[round(r,1) for r in rates]}"
          f"  released channels {winners}")
# Normal tone releases only the best channel; low tone releases none
# (bradykinesia); high tone releases extras (hyperkinesia).

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

No other circuit in the nervous system makes its decisions entirely in the currency of removed inhibition: a hundred million voting cells that are silent by default, an output layer that never stops firing, and a verdict that consists of one brief, purchased silence.


CHAPTER 41. THE HIPPOCAMPAL TRISYNAPTIC TEMPLATE (Series-Composed Memory Loop) (The Memory Assembly Line) (COG)

Three of the memory motifs of Part Five - the expansion recoder, the autoassociative attractor, and the comparator - could each stand alone, and elsewhere in the brain they do.

In the hippocampus evolution bolted them together in series, one-way, in a fixed order: separate the pattern, store the pattern, compare the pattern against the world.

The result is a production line that takes in the cortex's summary of the present moment and ships out an indexed, addressable episode, once per theta cycle, for the rest of your life.

Memory names the product.

Assembly line names the architecture: stations in fixed order, each performing one operation, with the conveyor running in only one direction.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

The hippocampal trisynaptic template is the serial composition of three microcircuits already catalogued in this manuscript: entorhinal cortex projects to the dentate gyrus, which performs expansion recoding and pattern separation (entry 33); the dentate projects to area CA3, which performs autoassociative storage and pattern completion (entry 29); and CA3 projects to area CA1, which compares the memory-derived prediction against a direct entorhinal copy of the present (entry 34).

What the whole computes is episodic memory encoding and retrieval: the transformation of a current cortical state into a stored, separable, cue-recallable index, and the detection of novelty whenever recall and reality disagree.

The composition matters more than the parts, because separation before storage prevents overwriting, and comparison after recall prevents hallucination.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The node roles are the entorhinal source layers, the dentate separator, the CA3 store, the CA1 comparator, and the subicular and entorhinal return stations.

Layer 2 of entorhinal cortex sends the excitatory glutamatergic perforant path, which divides to reach both the dentate granule cells and, running further, the distal dendrites of CA3; layer 3 sends a separate excitatory temporoammonic edge directly to the distal dendrites of CA1.

Dentate granule cells send the mossy fibre edge, excitatory and unusually powerful, onto the proximal dendrites of a small number of CA3 pyramidal cells, with side branches onto mossy cells and inhibitory interneurons.

CA3 pyramidal cells send massive excitatory recurrent collaterals onto one another, roughly 2 percent pairwise connectivity, forming the attractor, and send the excitatory Schaffer collateral edge onto the proximal and middle dendrites of CA1.

CA1 pyramidal cells project excitatorily to the subiculum and back to layer 5 of entorhinal cortex, closing the loop, and the loop is strictly one-way: no station projects backward.

Inhibitory interneurons at every station form feedforward, feedback, and lateral edges, and the dentate mossy cells add an excitatory associational edge linking distant dentate levels.

Topologically the graph is a ring with one diameter shortcut, the temporoammonic path, which is precisely what lets CA1 compare the ring's output with its input.

THE CELLULAR CAST AND THEIR PERSONALITIES:

The dentate granule cell of the neuron catalogue is the separator: tiny, hyperpolarised near minus 85 millivolts, reluctant to fire, and present in vast excess, roughly 15 million per hemisphere against about 1.1 million entorhinal layer 2 inputs, and its silent, sparse personality is the algorithm, because a code in which under 1 percent of cells are active barely ever reuses a pattern.

The CA3 pyramidal cell is the store: a bursting cell whose recurrent collaterals contact thousands of its neighbours, and its willingness to fire complex bursts makes it a natural attractor unit, able to ignite a stored ensemble from a fragment.

The hilar mossy cell, the excitatory oddball of the dentate, relays granule output back across the dentate's levels; its noisy, spontaneously active personality keeps the separator calibrated and is among the first casualties in epilepsy.

The CA1 pyramidal cell is the comparator: a regular-spiking, adapting cell whose distal dendrites receive entorhinal reality while its proximal dendrites receive CA3 memory, and whose dendritic plateau potentials fire hardest when the two agree in a specific way, or flag mismatch when they do not; it is also the hippocampus's principal export cell.

The parvalbumin basket cell of the catalogue paces each station at theta and gamma, its fast-spiking, non-adapting personality supplying the metronome that turns the assembly line into a clocked pipeline.

The oriens-lacunosum-moleculare interneuron gates the entorhinal input to CA1's distal tufts, deciding on each theta phase whether reality or memory dominates the comparator.

THE SYNAPTIC AND JUNCTIONAL FABRIC:

Perforant-path synapses onto granule cells are glutamatergic, spine-borne, individually weak, alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) and N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) mediated, and plastic by classic NMDA-dependent long-term potentiation, the synapse at which potentiation was discovered.

The mossy fibre terminal is a giant, a bouton of 3 to 5 micrometres engulfing complex spines on proximal CA3 dendrites, with a low resting release probability, enormous frequency facilitation, and an NMDA-independent presynaptic plasticity rule; a granule cell burst can drive a CA3 cell to spike one-for-one, the detonator synapse, and each granule cell makes only about 15 such contacts.

CA3 recurrent and Schaffer synapses are conventional glutamatergic spine synapses whose Hebbian NMDA-dependent plasticity within roughly 20 milliseconds of pre-post coincidence is the storage medium itself.

The temporoammonic synapses on CA1 distal tufts are weaker, strongly gated by inhibition and acetylcholine.

GABAergic synapses from basket and axo-axonic cells target CA1 and CA3 somata and initial segments; parvalbumin interneurons are coupled by connexin-36 gap junctions for rhythm; and dopamine, noradrenaline, and acetylcholine paracrine inputs set the write-versus-read balance.

SCALE OF ONE INSTANCE:

One hippocampal hemisphere is one instance: roughly 1.1 million entorhinal layer 2 cells fan out onto roughly 15 million dentate granule cells, which converge onto roughly 2.7 million CA3 pyramidal cells, which project to roughly 5.7 million CA1 pyramidal cells, figures from stereological counts with moderate confidence and honest variation between studies of about 30 percent.

A single traverse of the three synapses takes roughly 30 to 40 milliseconds, comfortably inside one theta cycle of 125 to 250 milliseconds.

NUMBER AND DISTRIBUTION OF INSTANCES:

Two instances, one per hemisphere, each repeating the same lamellar cross-section along the roughly 4 to 4.5 centimetre length of the human hippocampus, so the template is better counted as a few hundred partially independent lamellar slices per side than as one monolith.

The same three-station sequence runs at every septotemporal level, with the posterior levels biased toward space and the anterior toward emotion and gist.

WHERE IT IS INSTALLED (THE LAYER 9 MAP):

• The dentate gyrus, the separation station and the only site of adult human neurogenesis of any note.

• The cornu ammonis fields CA3 and CA2, the storage station, with CA2 as a specialised social-memory annex.

• The cornu ammonis field CA1, the comparison and export station.

• The subiculum, the output amplifier distributing the verdict to cortex and subcortex.

• The entorhinal cortex, the gateway whose grid and object codes are both the line's raw material and its customer.

HOW IT COLOURS ITS REGIONS:

Without this template the medial temporal lobe would still perceive but could not archive: patient H.M., whose bilateral resection removed it, kept his intellect, his language, and his childhood, and lost only the ability to add new episodes - the cleanest dissociation in clinical neuroscience.

The entorhinal cortex would become a gateway to nowhere, the subiculum an amplifier with no signal, and neocortical consolidation would lose the replay engine that trains it at night.

Downstream, prefrontal decision circuits would lose their supply of one-shot episodic evidence and be forced back onto slow statistical learning alone.

THE INPUT-OUTPUT TRANSFORMATION:

Station one is an expansion followed by thresholding: a dense entorhinal vector of about a million dimensions is projected into a 15-million-dimension space and clipped by inhibition to under 1 percent activity, a transformation that provably decorrelates overlapping inputs.

Station two is autoassociation: the sparse code is stored by Hebbian weight changes in a recurrent net whose attractor dynamics later complete a whole stored pattern from a roughly 30 percent fragment.

Station three is subtraction in the broad sense: CA1 output reports the match and the mismatch between the CA3 prediction and the entorhinal present, novelty emerging as a burst when the difference is large.

End to end: present state in, separated-stored-verified episode index out, once per theta cycle.

TEMPORAL SIGNATURE:

The whole line is clocked by theta at 4 to 8 cycles per second, with gamma at 30 to 90 cycles per second nested inside it (entry 24), encoding biased to one theta phase and retrieval to the opposite phase, so writing and reading alternate about six times per second and never collide.

During rest and slow-wave sleep the clock changes entirely: sharp-wave ripples at 80 to 150 cycles per second in humans sweep compressed replays of stored sequences out of CA3 through CA1 to cortex, ten to twenty times faster than the experience itself.

Single-traverse latency is 30 to 40 milliseconds; consolidation runs over weeks to years.

DYNAMIC REGIMES AND STATES:

The template has two great regimes, online theta operation for encoding and retrieval, and offline sharp-wave-ripple operation for replay and consolidation, switched largely by acetylcholine, which is high in the first regime and low in the second.

Within the online regime the oriens-lacunosum-moleculare gate tilts CA1 between reality-dominated and memory-dominated modes on alternate theta phases.

Its pathological regime is seizure: the dentate normally acts as the line's safety gate, and when hilar cell loss weakens that gate the CA3 attractor becomes an epileptic amplifier.

PLASTICITY AND LEARNING:

This is the most plastic composite in the brain: perforant-path and Schaffer synapses show NMDA-dependent long-term potentiation inducible in one theta burst, mossy fibre synapses show presynaptic potentiation, and CA1 dendrites add behavioural-timescale plasticity, in which a single plateau potential creates a place field from synapses active in the preceding one to two seconds.

Adult neurogenesis inserts new granule cells that pass through a hyperplastic adolescence, refreshing the separator's coding space.

Replay-driven consolidation gradually copies the line's indices into neocortical schemas, after which the hippocampus can let old episodes go.

VARIANTS AND SUBTYPES:

The dorsal-posterior variant runs the line on spatial grid input and manufactures place memory; the ventral-anterior variant runs it on amygdalar and hypothalamic input and manufactures emotional and gist memory.

CA2 is a variant station inserted between CA3 and CA1, resistant to conventional potentiation and specialised for social recognition memory.

The direct entorhinal-to-CA1 shortcut can run as a reduced two-station variant sufficient for familiarity without recollection.

DEVELOPMENT AND ASSEMBLY:

The ammonic fields are born from the medial pallium in mid-gestation, but the dentate is a late construction, its granule cells born mostly perinatally and into adult life from a displaced germinal hilus, which is why the separator matures last and why episodic memory before roughly age three is not retained, the infantile amnesia of every human autobiography.

The one-way ring is wired by reelin-guided lamination, and theta clocking begins in infancy as the septal pacemaker matures.

EVOLUTIONARY PROVENANCE:

The medial pallium of fish and amphibians already holds the germ of the loop, and birds run a functionally similar space-memory pallium, but the fully laminated three-station line with a detonator relay is a mammalian invention on the order of 200 million years old.

Its conservation across all mammals, from shrew to whale, at nearly constant architecture and merely scaled cell counts, argues that separate-store-compare is not one solution to episodic memory but the solution.

SUPPORT SYSTEM:

Hippocampal astrocytes regulate the glutamate economy of the most potentiation-prone synapses in the brain and gate NMDA receptors through D-serine, making them silent partners in every act of storage.

The dentate's neurogenic niche depends on its private vasculature, and CA1's notorious vulnerability to hypoxia, the reason cardiac arrest deletes memory first, follows from its high NMDA load and lean blood supply, the Sommer sector of the pathologists.

DISEASES AND DISORDERS:

Alzheimer's disease begins its cortical devastation in entorhinal layer 2 and CA1, the line's entry gate and export station, which is why the earliest symptom is a failure to form new episodes while old ones survive.

Temporal lobe epilepsy is the line's storage station turned amplifier, with hilar and CA3 cell loss, granule cell dispersion, and mossy fibre sprouting rewiring the separator into a recurrent exciter; hippocampal sclerosis is its scar.

Global amnesia after bilateral CA1 loss, transient global amnesia, and the memory deficits of schizophrenia and depression, with dentate hypofunction and stress-shrunken CA3 dendrites, complete the clinical roll.

SYSTEMS INTERFACE:

• SUBSCRIBES (INPUTS).

◦ Entorhinal layer 2 grid, object, and context codes by the perforant path, roughly 1.1 million source cells.

◦ Entorhinal layer 3 current-state copy by the temporoammonic path direct to CA1.

◦ Medial septal theta pacing, cholinergic and GABAergic, 4 to 8 cycles per second.

◦ Neuromodulatory write-enable signals: dopamine, noradrenaline, acetylcholine.

• PUBLISHES (OUTPUTS).

◦ Episode indices and novelty signals from CA1 and subiculum to entorhinal layer 5, prefrontal cortex, amygdala, and nucleus accumbens.

◦ Compressed sequence replays during sharp-wave ripples at 80 to 150 cycles per second.

• STATE.

◦ Stored weight matrices of CA3 recurrence and Schaffer input, current attractor occupancy, theta phase, cholinergic regime flag.

• PARAMETERS.

◦ Cell counts roughly 15 million granule, 2.7 million CA3, 5.7 million CA1 per hemisphere; dentate activity under 1 percent; CA3 recurrent connectivity roughly 2 percent; about 15 mossy contacts per granule cell.

• TIME CONSTANTS.

◦ Loop traverse 30 to 40 milliseconds; theta period 125 to 250 milliseconds; ripple event 50 to 100 milliseconds; behavioural-timescale plasticity window 1 to 2 seconds; systems consolidation weeks to years.

• FAILURE MODE.

◦ Alzheimer's disease beginning in entorhinal layer 2 and CA1: anterograde amnesia.

◦ Temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis: the store turned seizure focus.

◦ Anoxic CA1 loss: pure amnesic syndrome.

THE KONNECTOME NOTE:

Propose the module name episodic_memory_assembly_line, subscribing to current_context_vector, theta_phase, and write_enable_neuromodulation, and publishing episode_index, pattern_completion_output, and novelty_alarm.

The closest artificial intelligence analogues are, station by station, a random expansion with a k-winners-take-all sparsifier, a modern Hopfield or key-value associative memory, and a residual comparator, and the composite resembles complementary-learning-systems and retrieval-augmented architectures in which a fast episodic store supplements a slow parametric network.

The biological version differs in writing in one shot with a three-factor rule, in time-division multiplexing its read and write phases on a theta clock instead of separating them in software, and in running an offline replay service that trains the slow network while input is switched off - all three features worth copying literally.

ENGLISH READABLE CODE:

The purpose of this procedure is to pass one input pattern through separation, storage by association, and comparison, in series, as the hippocampal loop does.
Create a list variable called input pattern holding the current entorhinal values.
Create a large empty list variable called separated pattern.
Create a table variable called association weights with all values starting at 0.
Create a list variable called recalled pattern.
Create a number variable called novelty score with initial value 0.
Project the input pattern through fixed random expansion connections into a population ten times larger.
For each cell in the larger population, perform the following actions.
    If the cell's summed drive is within the top 1 percent of the population is true, then perform the following actions.
        Set that cell's value in separated pattern to 1.
    Otherwise, perform the following actions.
        Set that cell's value in separated pattern to 0.
    End the conditional block.
End the loop.
For each pair of active cells in separated pattern, increase their entry in association weights by 1.
Take a degraded copy of separated pattern with one third of its active cells removed, and call it the cue.
Repeat the following actions three times.
    For each cell, sum the association weights arriving from the cue's active cells.
    Set the cell active if the sum crosses the completion threshold.
    Set the cue to the resulting pattern.
End the loop.
Set recalled pattern to the cue.
For each cell, compare recalled pattern with separated pattern, and add 1 to novelty score for each disagreement.
Display recalled pattern and novelty score to the console.
The procedure is complete.

CODE SAMPLE:

Python is chosen because the claim - three motifs in series can separate, store, and verify a memory - is checkable in a few dozen lines of linear algebra, and Python with numpy states the algebra plainly.

# Hippocampal trisynaptic template: dentate separation -> CA3 completion
# -> CA1 comparison (Marr 1971; Treves & Rolls 1994; O'Reilly & McClelland 1994).
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
N_EC, N_DG, K = 100, 1000, 10          # expansion 10x, top-k sparsity 1%

W_sep = rng.random((N_DG, N_EC))       # fixed random perforant path

def dentate(x):                        # station 1: separate (entry 33)
    drive = W_sep @ x
    y = np.zeros(N_DG)
    y[np.argsort(drive)[-K:]] = 1.0    # winner-take-all sparse code
    return y

x = rng.random(N_EC)
x_similar = x + 0.1 * rng.random(N_EC) # a nearly identical experience
a, b = dentate(x), dentate(x_similar)
print("input overlap  ", round(float(x @ x_similar / (np.linalg.norm(x) * np.linalg.norm(x_similar))), 2))
print("dentate overlap", round(float(a @ b) / K, 2))   # separated apart

W_ca3 = np.outer(a, a)                 # station 2: one-shot Hebbian store (entry 29)
cue = a.copy()
cue[np.flatnonzero(a)[: K // 3]] = 0   # degrade the cue by one third
for _ in range(3):                     # attractor settles: pattern completion
    drive = W_ca3 @ cue
    cue = np.zeros(N_DG)
    cue[np.argsort(drive)[-K:]] = 1.0

novelty = int(np.sum(np.abs(cue - a))) # station 3: CA1 comparison (entry 34)
print("recalled fraction", float(cue @ a) / K, " novelty score", novelty)
# A one-third-degraded cue recalls the full episode; novelty 0 says
# memory and world agree, and any mismatch would ring the CA1 alarm.

WHAT MAKES IT UNMISTAKABLE:

Nowhere else do three distinct memory computations sit bolted in a fixed one-way series inside a single fold of cortex, clocked six times a second, with a detonator synapse in the middle and a reality-check shortcut across the top - and nowhere else does removing five centimetres of tissue remove the future while sparing the past.


CHAPTER 42. THE CEREBELLAR CORTICAL TEMPLATE (Uniform Adaptive-Filter Module) (The Calibration Crystal) (NON-COG)

The cerebellum holds four fifths of the brain's neurons in one tenth of its volume, and it spends them on a single circuit diagram repeated with a regularity found nowhere else in biology.

Mossy fibres in, an immense granule expansion up, parallel fibres out across the flat planes of Purkinje dendrites, one climbing fibre per Purkinje cell to say wrong, and inhibition from Golgi, basket, and stellate cells to keep the whole crystal sparse and sharp.

It does not decide anything; it takes whatever the rest of the nervous system decides and grinds the error out of it, movement by movement, millisecond by millisecond.

Calibration names the job: supervised correction of other circuits' output.

Crystal names the form: one unit cell, the microzone, tiled in near-perfect uniformity some thousands of times.

WHAT IT IS AND WHAT IT COMPUTES:

The cerebellar cortical template is the composite of the expansion recoder (entry 33) and the supervised error-correction module (entry 35) wrapped in a triple inhibitory scaffold, and it computes adaptive filtering: it learns to transform whatever contextual signals the mossy fibres carry into a corrective output that cancels the errors reported by the climbing fibres.

It is tagged (NON-COG) for its principal role, the calibration of movement, timing, and reflex gain, with the honest note that the identical module in the cerebrocerebellum is lent to prefrontal and language circuits, calibrating thought by the same algorithm.

THE WIRING DIAGRAM:

The node roles are the mossy fibre inputs, the granule cell expansion layer, the Golgi cell regulator, the parallel fibre bus, the Purkinje cell reader, the basket and stellate inhibitors, the climbing fibre teacher from the inferior olive, and the deep cerebellar nuclear output cell.

Mossy fibres form excitatory glutamatergic edges onto granule cell claws inside glomeruli, each granule cell receiving exactly about four mossy inputs, and also send excitatory collaterals to the deep nuclei.

Each granule cell axon ascends and splits into a parallel fibre running 4 to 6 millimetres transversely, forming weak excitatory edges en passant onto the flat, plane-confined dendritic trees of hundreds of Purkinje cells set perpendicular to it.

The Golgi cell receives excitatory edges from mossy and parallel fibres and returns an inhibitory GABAergic edge into the glomeruli, a feedforward and feedback loop that enforces sparseness on the expansion.
